title: Ofgem Fee Aims to Clear Grid Queue – Who Benefits?
content:
Ofgem has proposed a refundable Data Centre Commitment Fee and deliverability milestones for large data center grid connections in Great Britain, a move aimed at purging speculative projects from a congested queue while potentially favoring hyperscalers and established operators able to lock up capital for years.
The UK energy regulator is consulting on a refundable Data Centre Commitment Fee for large developments, paired with milestones that require evidence of financial capability, commercial maturity, and procurement activity. The fee would be refunded upon
energization
and forfeited if the project exits the queue early. The consultation remains open through September 16.
proposal
follows a surge in contracted demand offers, from 41 GW to 125 GW, between November 2024 and June 2025. Ofgem said data centers account for roughly 73 GW in the queue, raising concerns that nonviable applications are delaying credible projects and distorting future network planning.
Related:
What Britain’s Next Prime Minister Could Mean for UK Data Centers
Queue Shifts from First-Come to Prove It
Ofgem proposes setting the fee between £237,500 and £712,500 per megawatt (approximately $315,000 to $946,000 per MW), or about 2.5% to 7.5% of average project costs. For a 100 MW development, that equates to a security requirement of approximately £23.8 million to £71.3 million, according to an
analysis
Kristina Lesnjak, EMEA research manager at DCByte, told
Data Center Knowledge
that the proposal would shift the grid queue from being largely chronological to one that is more explicitly based on deliverability.
“These proposals aim to make the grid queue less about who applied first and more about who can demonstrate a credible path to delivery,” she said. “This will rule out many of the more speculative projects for prioritization straightaway, benefiting viable developments.”
The challenge will be distinguishing speculative proposals from projects that are credible but lack the balance sheet or established UK presence of a hyperscaler. Lesnjak said clear evidence requirements and firm deadlines will be essential to avoid arbitrary barriers.
“The process has to be transparent and set clear milestones for developers, for what evidence is required and when,” she said. “The goal should be to free up capacity from projects that are unlikely to proceed while giving serious schemes a fair opportunity to prove they can deliver.”
Capital Advantage Could Create a Two-Tier Market
The commitment fee is part of a broader shift in which grid operators expect large electricity users to prove both their demand and their ability to support it. In the US,
PJM has proposed requiring
many future large loads to secure sufficient generating capacity or accept curtailment during resource shortages, similarly aiming to prevent the cost of unverified or unsupported demand from falling on existing consumers.
Related:
The AI Demand Dilemma: Utilities Confront Speculative Growth
In Great Britain, the likely winners are operators with a record of
delivering large campuses
, access to capital, and projects deemed strategically valuable. Lesnjak cautioned that smaller developers and new entrants could face longer delays even when their projects are viable.
“This could lead to a two-tier market, with strategic, fast-tracked projects at the head of the queue and non-strategic schemes heavily delayed,” she said. “This could benefit those major operators and hyperscalers with an existing presence in the UK over smaller players and new entrants.”
Power Strategy Will Drive Site Selection
The policy could also reshape site selection, encouraging smaller developers to look beyond constrained clusters, band together to finance generation in lower-demand areas such as northern England and Scotland, or combine non-firm connections with owned energy assets. Strategies like these would turn
power procurement
into a central element of development rather than a utility step that follows site selection.
Related:
Power Bottlenecks Push Data Centers Beyond Traditional Hubs
“In essence, smaller developers are going to need to be more creative in how they secure power for projects,” Lesnjak said.

title: ContourGlobal announces 3 GWh of CATL BESS for global projects - Energy Storage
content: International power producer ContourGlobal has continued its busy 2026 expansion with an announcement that it has signed a 3 GWh order with Chinese battery giant CATL for battery energy storage systems (BESS) for its projects. The lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery order has been made to supply three of ContourGlobal’s projects, namely the 500MW/2,000 MWh Wallace BESS project in Scotland which it acquired in June and is in “advanced development”, the 100 MW/400 MWh Taxiarches project in Greece which it picked up as a ready-to-build in January, and the 90 MW/360 MWh battery for the Los Maitenes hybrid solar-plus-storage project in Chile, which hosts a 141 MW solar farm, which began just days ago. ContourGlobal said under the agreement with CATL, it will receive 526 battery containers, hosting LFP cells. Each container has a capacity of 5.64 MWh, configured for a four-hour discharge duration. While the peak power output wasn’t stated, each block would be expected to deliver 1.4 MW. CATL noted it will offer its liquid-cooled system integration technology. ContourGlobal has the backing of KKR, and the British firm has, according to its website, 5.7 GW of renewables projects in operation and 2 GW under construction. Just weeks ago, it also announced a PPA with Tesla on a 1 TWh solar-storage PPA in Arizona . In July 2025, it announced the acquisition of 9.5 GWh worth of BESS capacity in Italy. What they said: “We are very proud to announce this framework agreement with CATL, one of the world’s leaders in BESS,” said Antonio Cammisecra, CEO of ContourGlobal. “Beyond equipment supply, we are establishing a standardized utility-scale BESS platform across multiple countries, enabling consistent engineering, testing, commissioning and long-term asset management. By harmonizing technical requirements and project execution practices, we reduce delivery risk, accelerate project deployment and create a scalable model for continued growth of our storage business. This agreement reflects the shared commitment of both companies to accelerate the deployment of reliable utility-scale battery storage through long-term collaboration.” “This collaboration brings together our advanced battery technology and ContourGlobal’s deep expertise in developing energy infrastructure,” said LB Tan, CCO, Co-President of Sales and Marketing at CATL. “With a shared vision, we are delivering safe, reliable and long-term value for customers in the energy transition journey of Europe and the whole world.“ The post ContourGlobal announces 3 GWh of CATL BESS for global projects appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Energy Vault to supply 1.25 GW of off-grid BESS for US data center - Energy Storage
content: Energy Vault said it has signed its single largest commercial agreement, winning a deal to supply BESS and grid-forming power conversion systems, for a 1.25 GW integrated power infrastructure deployment serving a hyperscaler AI data center in Texas. In the rush to deploy data centers and with new restrictions and political pressure coming into play on the ERCOT grid for data centers, the structure is designed to bypass utility interconnection entirely. Even without new limitations, grid connection queues can be as long as five years or more in certain US markets. Texas Governor Greg Abbott said the state had 474 GW of requests to connect to the Texas grid, with 90% of those being data centers, though not all would be expected to be built and delivered. Energy Vault said its initial deployments are expected within four to 12 months, with revenue expectations provided given it is a public company, with the deal set to be in the range of $500–600 million across the second half of 2026 and 2027. The EPC partner on the power infrastructure and generation side has not been named, but the release suggested Caterpillar gensets will provide off-grid power. The system is designed to be FEOC-compliant as it becomes a standard requirement for US projects seeking federal incentives. Energy Vault said the two companies intend to pursue additional hyperscaler and neocloud opportunities beyond the initial Texas deployment without revealing further targets, but Energy Vault’s Chairman and CEO Robert Piconi noted that artificial intelligence is “fundamentally changing how critical power infrastructure is designed, deployed and operated.” What else they said: Energy Vault’s Robert Piconi: “As our largest single contract executed to date, this milestone agreement represents another important step in Energy Vault’s strategic evolution from an energy storage technology pioneer into an integrated energy infrastructure provider. More importantly, it establishes a repeatable commercial platform that we believe can support substantial future expansion as hyperscaler AI infrastructure investments continue to accelerate globally.” An unnamed senior executive at Energy Vault’s strategic power infrastructure partner commented, “Energy Vault’s BESS, grid-forming technology and software platform are central to this solution. By integrating those systems into our modular plant design, we can bring large blocks of dependable power online quickly while maintaining the performance, scalability and flexibility that hyperscale campuses require.” The post Energy Vault to supply 1.25 GW of off-grid BESS for US data center appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Malawi inaugurates first battery storage system - Energy Storage
content: The government of Malawi has switched on the country’s first battery energy storage system (BESS). The 20 MW/40 MWh project is located in the township of Kanengo, within the northern region of Lilongwe, Malawi’s capital. The Kanengo BESS project was implemented with support from international non-profit initiative Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP) alongside the Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi (ESCOM), Malawi’s state-owned power transmission and distribution company. The project, supported by $20 million in catalytic grant financing, is designed to stabilize Malawi’s national grid and reduce reliance on diesel. “Malawi’s electricity grid has long faced systemic challenges, including instability, high levels of renewable energy curtailment, dependence on hydropower and a costly reliance on diesel back-up generation,” a statement posted by GEAPP explains. “The Kanengo BESS directly addresses these structural constraints by storing energy and managing fluctuations.” ESCOM CEO William Kayipa added that the project unlocks around 100 MW of renewables that were previously constrained. “This is not just an engineering achievement – it is the foundation for ESCOM’s transformation into a financially viable, high-performing utility capable of supporting Malawi’s target of 70% electricity access by 2030,” Kayipa said. Speaking during an inauguration ceremony held last month, Malawi’s Minister of Energy, Jean Mathanga, said the BESS marks the beginning of a new era in promoting the country’s energy independence. She added that battery storage will help reduce power outages in the country while helping hospitals, schools and businesses access reliable electricity. “Solar power has revolutionized Malawi’s energy sector, but the battery energy storage system will make the transition sustainable,” the minister said. A memorandum of understanding is in place between the government of Malawi and GEAPP to help assist ESCOM to transform and strengthen the country’s electricity system. The partnership also includes plans to establish the Southern Africa BESS Centre of Excellence at Mzuzu University in northern Malawi, which the Ministry of Energy says will “position Malawi as a technology leader in BESS in the southern African region.” According to data compiled by the Africa Solar Industry Association (AFSIA), available in its online project database, Malawi has a combined 92.5 MWh of battery projects under development. title: Romania exceeds 1 GW of utility-scale BESS capacity - Energy Storage
content: Romania has surpassed 1 GW/2 GWh of installed utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS), according to figures provided by the Romanian Photovoltaic Industry Association (RPIA). Irene Mihai, RPIA policy director, told ESS News that Romania currently has around 1.1 GW/2 GWh of installed utility-scale BESS, compared to 494 MW/914 MWh at the start of the year. Recent developments in Romania’s storage market indicate that this growth trajectory is set to accelerate in the coming years. In March, Vienna-based independent power producer Enery said it secured financing for a 1 GWh BESS to be co-located with a 761 MW solar project in Romania. A month later, Austria’s Renalfa revealed it is planning 3.6 GWh of BESS , through a combination of both lithium-ion and sodium-ion solutions, across two renewable energy projects in Romania. Mihai also revealed that Romania is set to launch a call for projects for standalone batteries, expected to support the deployment of around 3 GWh of BESS, in the near future. The European Commission gave the subsidy scheme the green light in March. As of May this year, Romania’s energy regulator ANRE estimated storage capacity in the prosumer market at around 850 MW. Mihai also shared that the percentage of residential solar prosumers with batteries has increased from 23% at the start of the year to 33% now, while the percentage of C&I solar prosumers with batteries has increased from 7.5% to 10%. Romania is planning to replace its rebate scheme for solar with support for prosumers looking to install batteries. At the time of the initial announcement, Mihai said that the focus of public support in Romania is gradually shifting from expanding solar capacity toward improving system flexibility and self-consumption through battery storage. Mihai also said that storage is increasingly being perceived not only as an add-on technology, but as a key component of a more efficient and resilient rooftop PV system. “While the BESS programme may not fully replace the deployment levels created by [the solar subsidy scheme], it should help sustain investment activity among existing prosumers and support the maturation of the Romanian rooftop PV market,” she said. title: U.S. energy provider deploys plug-in batteries across 21 commercial kitchens to slash power costs - Energy Storage
content: Software-enabled energy supplier David Energy has partnered with food technology platform Wonder to deploy consumer-grade, 120-volt plug-in battery storage across 21 New York City locations, utilizing custom software integration to cut commercial kitchen electricity bills by 3% to 5% while bypassing traditional utility interconnection queues entirely. David Energy has expanded its commercial distributed energy resource footprint across New York City, partnering with food technology platform Wonder to deploy consumer-grade, 120-volt plug-in battery systems across 21 eligible locations. The turnkey project leverages custom software integration to automate commercial load-shifting, reducing store electricity costs without requiring upfront capital expenditure or traditional utility interconnection queues. The deployment utilizes EcoFlow STREAM Ultra modular hardware units, featuring lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry rated for 800 W output and 1.92 kWh of storage capacity per base unit. Connecting directly to standard 120-volt AC circuits inside store breaker rooms, the hardware relies on custom software integration developed by David Energy rather than standard commercial-grade battery management architectures. By controlling charging and discharging schedules through its proprietary platform, David Energy executes automated time-of-use arbitrage for Wonder’s all-electric kitchen loads. The batteries draw power during off-peak overnight hours when wholesale market prices and grid congestion are lowest, then discharge stored energy to power kitchen refrigeration and food preparation equipment during high-cost utility demand windows. Because these 120-volt consumer-grade units operate strictly behind the meter with zero backfeeding onto the distribution network, the installations completely bypass standard utility interconnection queuing in Con Edison territory. This non-interconnected operational profile enables rapid multi-site deployment without waiting through traditional utility study and approval timelines. Under a standard 36-month zero-capex contract structure, David Energy retains ownership of the battery hardware while providing the turn-key system to commercial end users. The financial model combines direct time-of-use bill management, demand charge reduction, demand response earnings, and capacity tag (ICAP) mitigation, lowering total customer electricity bills by an average of 3% to 5%. By controlling the hardware to reduce its own wholesale cost to serve, David Energy achieves a simple payback period of approximately three years per deployment. The company expects payback timelines to compress further as hardware costs decline and software control algorithms continue to improve. To supply virtual power plant capacity to the regional grid, eligible locations deployed prior to program deadlines are enrolled in Con Edison’s Commercial System Relief Program (CSRP) and Distribution Load Relief Program (DLRP). Dispatched during peak thermal stress, the aggregated plug-in batteries alleviate local feeder congestion during summer heatwaves and mitigate reliance on fossil-fired peaker plants across the metropolitan area. Building on the initial 21-site rollout in New York City, engineering teams from David Energy and Wonder are developing back-of-house architectural templates for Wonder’s 2027 location builds. These schematics will integrate standardized battery placements directly into future store construction plans. Beyond Wonder’s restaurant network, David Energy is rolling out the zero-capex plug-in storage offering to other power-dense small-business verticals across New York City’s five boroughs, targeting laundromats, independent grocers, convenience stores, and commercial retail chains. title: Archer makes wild deal with Boeing swapping eVTOL startups for equity
content:
Archer Aviation
Fred Lambert
| Aug 10 2026 - 7:35 am PT
Archer Aviation is buying three of Boeing’s aerospace subsidiaries: autonomous air-taxi developer Wisk Aero, military drone maker Insitu, and airspace-software firm SkyGrid. The deal also hands Boeing a stake in Archer.
Investors loved it. Archer (ACHR) stock jumped more than 20% on Monday, and the acquisition instantly turns a pre-revenue eVTOL startup into a company with a profitable defense business behind it.
It could accelerate Archer’s eVTOL plans.
What Archer is buying
Insitu is the prize. It’s a defense drone maker generating over $200 million in annual revenue, it’s profitable, and it has built more than 3,500 uncrewed aircraft systems fielded by the armed forces of 35 nations.
Wisk Aero is the autonomous eVTOL developer Boeing has bankrolled for years. Archer says it’s the only company to design, build, and fly six generations of eVTOL aircraft, with more than 1,700 flight tests. SkyGrid rounds out the deal with aircraft-agnostic air traffic management software.
Financial terms weren’t disclosed. Boeing isn’t only selling here. It’s taking a stake in Archer and entering a technology-sharing collaboration, though no purchase price, investment amount, or equity percentage was announced. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026, pending antitrust review.
The “physical AI” pitch
Archer is selling this as a bet on “physical AI.” The company says combining autonomy, eVTOL aircraft, and drones creates “an end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense,” all feeding into Archer’s own AI foundation model, ZEE.
“This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense,” said founder and CEO Adam Goldstein. “This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform.”
Boeing kept its framing simpler. “This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing’s VP of Commercial Airplanes Product Development. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market.”
The move accelerates a defense pivot Archer started in late 2024, when it partnered with Anduril to build a hybrid VTOL military aircraft and raised $430 million. Last month, the two unveiled Thunder, a jointly developed autonomous VTOL aircraft for defense and commercial missions. Insitu gives that ambition real revenue and real contracts instead of renderings.
Archer’s core business keeps moving in the meantime. It
began piloted operations of its flagship Midnight aircraft
last year, and it’s the
exclusive air taxi provider for the 2028 LA Olympics
The rivals who used to sue each other
There’s history here. Wisk sued Archer in 2021, accusing it of stealing trade secrets, in a bitter multi-year court fight. The two settled on August 10, 2023, with Boeing investing in
Archer’s funding round
and the companies agreeing to collaborate on autonomy.
That settlement was exactly three years ago today. Now Archer owns Wisk outright.
Electrek’s Take
The “physical AI” branding is doing a lot of work. Every startup slaps AI on a press release now, and Archer is no exception. But strip the buzzword and the logic holds up. Archer just bought its way from pre-revenue promise to a real defense business with $200 million in revenue and drones flying in 35 countries.
For a company that has burned cash for years chasing FAA certification, buying Insitu’s profitable, cash-generating business changes the entire company overnight. It steadies the balance sheet with real manufacturing and contracts, which until now were mostly a splashy unveiling and a stock pop.
I think there’s a real chance that it will accelerate the advent of eVTOLs, but I remain skeptical. I would keep a close eye on Archer becoming more focused on its new defense business, which I don’t really care for, at the detriment of its promise of commercial electric flight.

title: BYD's kei EV already looks like a hit with over 1,000 orders in its first 2 weeks
content:
BYD’s first electric kei car received over 1,000 orders in just two weeks after it went on sale.
BYD Racco EV orders reach over 1,000 in two weeks
BYD is going where no foreign brand has gone before. The Chinese EV giant officially launched Racco on July 28, its first electric kei vehicle, specifically designed to crack open Japan’s tiny-car market, long dominated by domestic brands like Nissan, Honda, Toyota, and Suzuki.
The Racco is already off to a promising start. BYD announced on Monday that its new mini EV received over 1,000 cumulative orders in its first two weeks on the market.
BYD said it was “the fastest pace for any model introduced to date,” and the vehicle was “attracting significant attention throughout Japan.”
According to a survey from early buyers, the Racco is exceeding expectations for its “excellent cost-performance ratio,” features, and craftsmanship.
About 80% of buyers chose the more expensive Racco 300 Premium trim, 14% chose the Plus, and the remaining 6% chose the base 200 model.
Interestingly, 37.5% of buyers added the Racco as an additional vehicle, 35.7% replaced their old vehicle, and 26.8% purchased it as a new vehicle.
BYD said 55.4% of early buyers already had EV charging equipment at home, 43% did not, and 1.6% did not answer.
Why are buyers interested? For one, BYD’s electric kei car is more efficient and, thanks to its electric powertrain, it also has lower maintenance costs. The Racco offers more advanced features as a software-defined vehicle (SDV), and with software updates it will continue to introduce new features, much like a smartphone.
BYD’s electric kei car starts at just ¥2,145,000, or about $13,000 in Japan. The base Racco 200 uses a 22.4 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with a WLTC driving range of 210 km (130 miles).
The higher-priced 300 Plus and Premium trims use a larger 35.84 kWh battery with a range up to 320 km (199 miles), which BYD said makes it the first kei EV in Japan to offer over 300 km.

Top comment by jrharbort
BYD will do well in Japan where others have failed due to two big reasons. 1) They understand the market and its needs. Inflation has spiraled out of control even in Japan while wages have hardly gone up. An extremely affordable and highly capable electric KEI car for those that need a car will be very attractive because 2) Japan imports all of their oil and are extremely sensitive to price fluctuations caused by conflicts. These cars will help to weaken that reliance on energy imports.
While Honda’s N-Box, Japan’s best-selling vehicle, is slightly cheaper, starting at ¥1,739,100 ($10,500), BYD’s kei EV is eligible for a ¥150,000 ($900) government subsidy, bringing the Racco’s starting price to ¥1,995,000 ($12,200).
The Racco is cheaper than the Nissan Sakura, Japan’s current best-selling EV, which starts at ¥2,448,600 ($15,000) and offers a longer driving range. It’s no wonder buyers are lining up for it.

title: Getting your teen a back-to-school e-bike? Don’t forget this cool-looking protective gear
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 10 2026 - 8:46 am PT
Back-to-school season often means shopping for backpacks, notebooks, and maybe even a new ride. For a growing number of families, that ride is an electric bike.
And I’m all for it. Giving teenagers the freedom to get themselves to school, sports practice, or a friend’s house without needing a car is one of the best things e-bikes can offer. But just like we’d encourage a new driver to wear a seatbelt, young e-bike riders should be equipped with the right protective gear too.
A good helmet is the obvious starting point. And I’m glad to see that many parents get that part right. But after that, there’s another layer of gear that I think more families should consider for their e-bike riding teens: protective clothing.
And there’s a company in this space whose gear I’ve become a big fan of:
Beyond Riders
I’ve tested a number of their products
over the last couple of years
, and what I like most is that they don’t look like motorcycle gear, even though they offer much of the same protection.
Their hoodies, riding shirts, jeans, and jackets can be fitted with CE-rated Level 1 or even Level 2 armor at the shoulders, elbows, and back, giving riders meaningful impact protection without making them look like they’re headed to a racetrack.
And let me be clear from the start: I don’t get any kickbacks for this, no affiliate links, nothing. I just really like their gear, and I support what they’re doing: making safe riding clothes that look good and don’t give the impression that I’m heading off to the closest biker bar.
Believe it or not, this hoodie has motorcycle armor in the chest, back, elbows, and shoulders, plus is built for the slide!
My personal favorite is the armored hoodie, above. It looks just like the kind of hoodie most teenagers already wear every day, which means they’re actually more likely to keep it on instead of leaving it at home.
The fit is comfortable, the styling is casual, and the built-in armor disappears into the garment. You wouldn’t know it, but behind the abrasion-resistant textiles are CE Level 2 armor in the shoulders, elbows, back, and chest.
There are even hidden features, like secret pockets and a hidden microfiber cloth in the corner for quickly cleaning your sunglasses.
The riding shirt feels like a light canvas jacket but packs in motorcycle-level protection
I’m also a big fan of Beyond Riders’ canvas riding jacket. It looks like a canvas overshirt or lightweight jacket, but underneath that casual appearance is full armor in the shoulders, back, and elbows, along with abrasion-resistant materials designed to help prevent painful road rash if you end up sliding across pavement.
In fact, Beyond Riders has become popular not just with e-bike riders, but also with electric skateboard riders and even motorcyclists who want protective gear that doesn’t scream “motorcycle.”
No piece of gear can eliminate the risk of a crash, but quality protective clothing can absolutely reduce the consequences. As more teenagers discover the freedom and independence that e-bikes provide, it’s worth thinking beyond just the bike itself. Pair that new e-bike with a quality helmet and some protective riding apparel, and you’ll be giving your young rider a much better chance of walking away from the unexpected.

title: Musk's Terafab chip plant will run on gas, not Tesla solar
content:
Fred Lambert
| Aug 10 2026 - 6:55 am PT
SpaceX confirmed it will power Terafab, its $16.8 billion chip megafactory in Texas, with its own natural gas power plants and “very large battery arrays.” Tesla solar isn’t in the plan.
That’s despite Tesla being a partner on the project, and despite Tesla selling solar panels, Powerwalls, and grid-scale batteries built for exactly this kind of load.
A chip fab on the bones of a coal plant
Tesla and SpaceX
confirmed Terafab last week
: a semiconductor plant in Grimes County, Texas, about an hour northwest of Houston, that the companies call the largest chip manufacturing facility on the planet. The first phase runs $16.8 billion, down from a $25 billion figure floated in March. It’s meant to churn out over a terawatt of compute per year for SpaceX and xAI data centers, plus future chips for Tesla’s Optimus and Cybercab.
Here’s the detail that got buried. The plant sits on the site of a former coal-fired power plant, and SpaceX plans to power it with newly built natural gas plants and batteries. So the compute future gets built on the same fossil ground as the past. Just swap coal for gas.
There’s no mention of Tesla solar anywhere in the power plan, even though Tesla co-owns the project.
The same gas playbook, only bigger
None of this is a one-off. It’s the pattern.
xAI’s Colossus data center around Memphis has been running on gas turbines since 2024, many of them unpermitted. The NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center, and Earthjustice are suing over 27 unpermitted turbines in Southaven, Mississippi, that they say pump out more than 1,700 tons of nitrogen oxides and 19 tons of formaldehyde a year next to homes, schools, and churches. “A data center should not be a potential death sentence for a community’s health,” said the NAACP’s Abre’ Conner. When regulators moved in,
Trump’s DOJ intervened to keep the turbines running
on national-security grounds.
Then Musk
personally bought gas turbine company APR Energy for about $1 billion
in July, picking up more than a gigawatt of turbine capacity. SpaceX has separately committed more than $2.8 billion to gas turbines to power its data centers. Terafab’s on-site gas plants are the next brick in that wall.
Tesla sells the alternative — Musk just won’t buy it
The strange part is that the cleaner option lives inside Musk’s own companies.
Tesla sells solar, Powerwall, and Megapack. xAI itself bought $269 million of Tesla Megapacks earlier this year. In June, Tesla and Sunrun
launched a 16 GW virtual power plant pitched directly at data centers
. Tesla is literally marketing solar-plus-storage as an answer to AI power demand.
And this is the same Musk who spent years selling a “solar electric economy,” who once
pitched space-based solar as the long-term fix
while burning gas on the ground. The vision is solar. The buildout is gas.
Electrek’s Take
Running gigawatt-scale, 24/7 chip fabs and AI training clusters on solar alone is genuinely difficult today. You need firm power, but Tesla’s and solar plus battery expertise is the solution.
But that’s not the choice Musk is making. He’s not building a solar-and-gas hybrid and squeezing the gas down over time. He’s going gas-first with zero Tesla solar. The driver here isn’t physics, it’s speed and cost.
It’s also incentives. Yes, this would be a great project for Tesla, which Musk owns about 20% of, but it is an even better project for Musk’s newly acquired APR Energy, which he owns 100% of.
Tesla used to exist to accelerate the transition to sustainable energy. Its founder is now behind one of the biggest new gas buildouts in the country.

Is Volvo launching an electric sedan?
After pulling the S90 and V60 Cross Country, Volvo will no longer offer sedans or wagons in the US, leaving its lineup consisting of just SUVs and crossovers.
The Swedish automaker is revamping its lineup as it navigates the Trump Administration’s policy changes.
Importing vehicles from Europe has become too costly, and Volvo has struggled to sell electric vehicles following the elimination of the federal EV tax credit last September.
For that reason, Volvo is
discontinuing the EX30
in the US after the 2026 model year, its smallest electric SUV.
The Single Motor EX30 variant was expected to go on sale as one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at around $ 35,000, but Volvo dropped the electric SUV from its lineup altogether, citing “market conditions and financial factors.”
According to
Automotive News
, Volvo is eyeing a return to the small-car market with a midsize electric sedan and wagon.
Volvo would build the two new vehicles in Europe, while both would be underpinned by its new SPA3 platform.
While the new EVs are expected to arrive in the second half of 2028, another new Volvo sedan was captured for the first time.
The images posted on
NewCarScoops
show the vehicle heavily camouflaged. Despite the disguise, you can see it’s equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR, but it still has exhaust pipes underneath, suggesting it will use a gas engine.
Keep in mind this is still an early-stage test vehicle, and the actual production model could change.
Volvo is also expected to launch a new plug-in hybrid (PHEV) and traditional hybrid options, including updated versions of the XC40, XC60, and XC90, so a refreshed S70 hybrid could be in the works.
While Volvo is introducing new hybrid and plug-in hybrid models, it isn’t abandoning pure electric vehicles altogether.
The 2027 EX60 is
now on sale
, starting at $58,400. As the first vehicle based on its SPA3 platform, the electric SUV is Volvo’s longest-range, fast-charging, and most technologically advanced EV to date.
Volvo said the range-topping EX60 P12 AWD will go on sale later this year, offering an estimated range of up to 400 miles. The P10 grade, currently on sale, offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 330 miles. It can also add up to 165 miles in 10 minutes of charging.

The aging EX40 is expected to be replaced by
the EX50
, a bigger and more affordable electric SUV as Volvo’s new entry-level EV.

title: Why does Monarc build its e-bikes with their forks on backward?
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 10 2026 - 5:37 am PT
If you’ve spotted one of Monarc’s new e-bikes, there’s a good chance one of your first thoughts was,
“Wait… did they install the fork backwards?”
The answer is no, it’s not really on backward – despite how it may look. Monarc just uses what’s known as a reverse-arch suspension fork, a design that’s uncommon in the cycling world but one that offers several engineering advantages.
Instead of placing the fork brace in front of the fork wheel like most suspension forks, Monarc’s in-house designed Gneiss fork moves that arch to the rear, allowing it to be shorter and stiffer.
It’s an eye-catcher on the company’s flagship
Monarc Marker off-road e-bike
, but it has a very specific purpose.
While it might look unusual, the concept isn’t new. Reverse-arch forks have appeared before in mountain biking and motorcycle suspension, where engineers have long appreciated the potential benefits.
They were originally patented by Manitou, appearing for years on those high-end mountain bikes.
But when the patent expired a few years ago, others were able to incorporate the design. Monarc is the latest yet,
bringing a more refined and better-performing fork design to e-bikes
in a way that has never been this accessible.
According to Monarc, relocating the arch allows the fork to be lighter while also increasing stiffness and strength.
Greater fore-aft rigidity can help the front wheel track more precisely through rough terrain, improving steering accuracy and reducing unwanted flex under braking or hard impacts. The company says it achieved those gains while still providing 80 mm of suspension travel for trail riding.
There’s also a practical advantage. By moving the arch rearward, mud, sticks, and trail debris have less opportunity to become trapped between the tire and fork brace. It’s a small detail, but one off-road riders will appreciate.
It’s a rarity in the e-bike industry, but refreshing to see companies experimenting with genuine engineering rather than simply changing colors or frame shapes. Monarc says it developed the Gneiss fork entirely in-house, giving its engineers the freedom to rethink one of the most recognizable components on an e-bike.
So no, Monarc didn’t accidentally install the forks backward. They just chose a different solution to the same engineering challenge – and one that happens to turn a few heads along the way.

title: 楚能80GWh锂电池项目投产，启钠/汉驰推进电池产业布局
content:
近期，电池产业链项目建设持续推进。其中，楚能新能源宜昌二期80GWh锂电池产业园正式投产，武汉启钠5万吨高性能钠电正极材料项目落地江西抚州，河北汉驰1GWh锂离子固态电池中试生产线项目获环评审批，新能源电池产业链上下游布局进一步加快。
楚能新能源宜昌二期80GWh锂电池项目投产
8月9日，楚能新能源（宜昌）二期80GWh锂电池产业园项目正式投产。该项目位于湖北省宜昌市夷陵区龙泉镇，总投资220亿元，规划产能80GWh。
据介绍，项目二期采用智能化生产线，将聚焦新一代快充动力电池及大容量储能电池等贺新年产品，相较一期单线生产效率提升超60%，满产后日均可生产电芯超80万颗。
楚能新能源宜昌基地项目于2022年启动建设，一期已实现投产运营，随着二期项目投产，宜昌基地整体产能进一步提升。
武汉启钠钠电正极材料项目落地江西抚州
据抚州新闻网消息，2026年8月，武汉启钠新能源科技有限公司年产5万吨高性能钠电正极材料项目正式落地江西省抚州市黎川县。该项目总投资约8亿元，预计将于2026年8月开工建设，建设周期为10个月。
根据规划，该项目将建设高性能钠电正极材料产线，并推动钠电产业技术研究院及中试平台建设，覆盖材料、电芯及电池系统等环节。
据了解，武汉启钠新能源成立于2022年，主要从事储能及动力电池正极材料的研发、生产与销售，布局聚阴离子型钠电正极材料（NFPP）技术路线。目前，公司已建成千吨级纳米复合聚阴离子型钠电正极材料产线，产品已向宁德时代、双登集团等企业送样及供货。
河北汉驰1GWh固态电池中试生产线项目环评批复
8月7日，河北汉驰新能源有限公司保定市阜平县1期1GWh锂离子固态电池中试生产线项目环评审批结果公示。
该项目位于河北省保定市阜平县，项目总投资3亿元，主要建设1栋研发中心（第6代锂离子新型储能电池研发，固态电池、锂离子电池小试生产研发）1栋生产车间、1栋仓库，购置两条PACK生产装配线及相关配套设施，年生产1GWh锂离子电池。
据悉，河北汉驰新能源有限公司成立于2024年4月，是一家专注于新能源领域的企业，核心业务涵盖电池制造与销售、风力发电技术服务及电力供应，由北京百斯德新能源科技有限公司全资持股。

content:
集邦光储观察获悉，8月7日，山东海辰储能全球首个长时储能一体化产业园（山东菏泽基地）量产推进会在菏泽鲁西新区举行，标志着该基地正式进入规模化生产阶段。
据了解，山东菏泽基地规划总占地约1200亩，全产业链计划总投资超过130亿元，是全球首个专注长时储能的一体化产业园。项目以产业链整体落地形式建设，涵盖磷酸铁锂储能电池智能制造、模组系统集成、新材料生产及上游原材料生产，实现从材料、电芯到系统的全链条贯通。
海辰储能联合创始人、总裁、山东海辰储能董事长王鹏程表示，菏泽基地于2024年10月底开工建设，此次量产下线较原规划提前两年完成，一、二期项目实现整体运营。基地投产后，将进一步提升海辰储能长时储能电池规模化制造和市场交付能力。
据介绍，菏泽基地搭载海辰储能第五代智能制造产线，贯通原材料、电芯制造、系统集成及交付流程。其中，单线产能达到15GWh，自动化率超过95%，并通过AI视觉检测等技术实现生产过程质量管控。
在推进会现场，海辰储能携手多方合作伙伴，围绕金融支撑、产业链协同、项目应用等关键维度，密集达成多项战略合作。
其中，海辰绿能与菏泽交投将围绕新能源项目开发开展合作，依托双方在区域资源、项目渠道及产业能力等方面的优势，共同推进新能源项目落地。
在投资领域，海辰绿能与珠海市汇垠德擎股权投资基金管理有限公司达成合作，双方将围绕新能源产业链相关项目开展投资合作，通过产业基金、股权投资等方式，引入资本及产业资源，共同推动优质新能源项目开发建设。
此外，海辰绿能与江西电建签署合作协议，双方将在新能源项目工程建设领域展开协同。依托江西电建在电力工程建设、技术服务及项目实施方面的能力，双方将共同提升新能源项目建设效率，推动相关项目落地。
随着菏泽基地进入量产阶段，海辰储能在长时储能领域的产业化布局进一步提速。通过产能建设与产业生态协同推进，公司将持续完善从储能电池制造到项目开发、建设及应用的全链条布局，加快推动长时储能规模化应用落地。

title: 隆基等4企新签3.5GW光伏组件订单
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，光伏组件市场订单持续推进，国内外项目采购及供应合作不断落地。隆基绿能、恒羲光伏分别获意大利71MW及迪拜3GW光伏组件订单，润马光能、天富天耀中标1GW光伏组件集采。
隆基获意大利71MW组件订单
近日，隆基绿能宣布与欧洲独立发电商Innovo Renewables达成战略合作，将为其在意大利开发建设的71MWp集中式光伏项目供应光伏组件。
这是双方在欧洲集中式光伏领域的首个大型合作项目，将采用隆基Hi-MO 9高效BC组件，该款组件基于第二代HPBC 2.0背接触电池技术，通过将电极触点移至电池背面，有效减少正面栅线遮挡，扩大受光面积并提升能量转换效率，其组件效率最高可达24.8%，功率最高可达670W。
目前，双方正在就后续清洁能源项目展开进一步探讨，未来将充分借鉴本项目在技术选型、系统设计和交付协同等方面的实践经验，持续扩大清洁能源项目规模。
此外，8月7日，隆基宣布其搭载ACM技术的组件出货已突破500MW，该技术于7月14日在隆基2026光储创新技术发布会上首次亮相，通过新型栅线材料与工艺优化提升电池及组件性能。目前，ACM技术已完成从量试线到规模化量产的推进，进一步加快高效组件技术的市场应用。
恒羲光伏获3GW迪拜光伏组件订单
8月7日，恒羲光伏与迪拜房地产开发商阿齐兹开发（AZIZI DEVELOPMENTS L.L.C.）签署3GW能源项目战略合作备忘录，双方首期合作聚焦2GW光伏组件供货。
根据协议，恒羲光伏将为阿齐兹开发旗下能源项目提供光伏组件产品。阿齐兹开发于2025年正式布局能源业务，计划建设总装机容量约10GW的多元化发电设施，此次合作将助力其新能源领域发展。
阿齐兹开发创始人、董事会主席Mirwais Azizi表示，未来双方将进一步扩大合作规模。阿齐兹开发计划在上海设立采购办公室，并推动与上海电气在新能源及相关领域开展更深入的战略合作。
润马光能、天富天耀中标432MW光伏组件集采
8月4日，第八师石玛兵地融合陕建100万千瓦“草光互补”光伏项目组件采购（一期）中标结果公示，润马光能与天富天耀分别中标该项目的标段1、标段2，中标单价分别为0.706元/W、0.726元/W。
招标公告显示，本项目建设地点位于新疆维吾尔自治区玛纳斯境内，建设规模为1GW光伏发电项目，直流侧规划装机容量为1069.36128MWp，组件主要技术参数为单晶硅双面双玻N型组件（功率720Wp及以上）。其中，此次招标标段1计划采购组件30万块，标段2计划采购组件30万块，每个标段规模约为216MW。

Heavy equipment manufacturer JCB has broken a 2010-set hydrogen-fuelled land speed record as it strives to break the official Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) title late this week.
The company’s 32-foot JCB Hydromax achieved an average speed of 368.3mph driven by two JCB hydrogen internal combustion engines (ICE), exceeding previous hydrogen ICE (185.5mph), diesel (350mph), electric (342mph), and fuel cell (303mph) records.
The run on the Bonneville Salt Flats, Utah, won the British firm the Southern California Timing Association’s (SCTA) record ahead of the prestigious FIA record attempt tabled for this week. If achieved, it would beat a record set by JCB’s Dieselmax vehicle in 2026.
JCB CEO, Anthony Bamford has previously billed the record attempts as a bid to prove the company’s seriousness about hydrogen.
JCB has been developing its own hydrogen technologies,
unveiling an ICE
as a zero-emission solution for construction and agriculture equipment in January 2023, and
trialling it on-site
, fitted in a JCB loadall, last year.
The record attempts come as hydrogen’s role in mobility is questioned, with battery-electric vehicles taking the lead in the passenger sector thanks to improvements in range and recharge times.
While it is still criticised for its low energy efficiency and high costs, many players increasingly see the molecule playing a leading role in decarbonising heavier applications like long-haul and heavy-duty transport, as well as construction.
In 2021, JCB pledged to invest £100m ($135m) to develop hydrogen engine technology. It has since deployed machines with the technology in the UK and secured approval for their commercial use across Europe.

title: CB&I advances large-scale liquid hydrogen storage
content:
The 20 m³ demonstration tank is integrated into NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) Hydrogen Test Facility (HTF) and triples the facility’s total liquid hydrogen (LH₂) storage capacity. The tank can be refilled as frequently as once per day, enabling accelerated testing of insulation systems through repeated thermal cycles while expanding the HTF’s capacity for long-duration LH₂ tests.
The program, announced in 2025, brings together CB&I, Shell, NASA, GenH2, and the University of Houston to develop and validate affordable, scalable LH₂ storage solutions in a real-world operating environment. Non-vacuum insulation technology is being explored as a pathway to reduce capital costs for high-throughput LH₂ storage applications.
Yogesh Meher, Vice President of Engineering at CB&I, said: “The successful first fill of our demonstration tank marks an important step toward validating a more cost-effective approach to large-scale liquid hydrogen storage. By demonstrating this technology under real operating conditions at NASA’s Hydrogen Test Facility, we are accelerating the path to commercial deployment and helping enable the hydrogen economy at scale.”
Over the coming months, NASA, CB&I, and Shell will evaluate the performance of the non-vacuum insulation system, generating data to support the commercialization and deployment of large-scale LH₂ storage technologies.
CB&I has stated it has constructed more than 130 LH₂ storage spheres worldwide, including the world’s largest LH₂ storage sphere, completed in 2022 to support NASA’s Artemis program.

title: Ultra-low iridium PTE collaboration targets PEM scale-up
content:
As a major milestone in the partnership, the companies will initiate a 3,000-hour long-term durability test this autumn. The testing campaign will evaluate the operational stability of Smoltek Hydrogen’s proprietary nanostructured iridium catalyst layer, which the company describes as a critical step toward the commercialization and large-scale industrialization of cost-effective green hydrogen production.
The collaboration combines Smoltek Hydrogen’s nanotechnology with Heraeus Precious Metals’ expertise in precious metal electrocatalysts and material analysis. The catalyst architecture is designed to reduce iridium loading to below 0.1 mg/cm² while maintaining high electrolyzer efficiency.
Fabian Wenger, Head of R&D at Smoltek Hydrogen, said: “Our nanostructured layer offers a unique capability to maximize charge and mass transport properties within a thickness of just a few microns. By optimizing this specific catalyst architecture, we can simultaneously maintain high electrolyzer efficiency while successfully reducing the amount of iridium needed to below 0.1 mg/cm² loading.”
Heraeus Precious Metals will lead the upcoming testing phase, providing material analysis under realistic operational conditions.
Christian Gebauer, Head of Innovation at the Hydrogen Systems Division of Heraeus Precious Metals, said: “We are looking forward to commencing this extensive testing campaign and to provide the critical material analysis required to validate this technology. With our capabilities we will continue to support all steps towards an industrialization of these highly promising ultra-low iridium PTEs with our comprehensive analytical and testing capabilities.”
The joint effort directly addresses the high cost of iridium as a key bottleneck in scaling proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis for green hydrogen production.

title: Meta 扎克伯格：美国若想取得开源 AI 领先，就得减少政策障碍
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据路透社报道，Meta CEO 马克 · 扎克伯格呼吁美国减少开源 AI 面临的政策障碍，以便更好地与中国竞争对手抗衡。
今天早些时候，Meta 发布了新的开放权重模型 Muse Glimmer，更多模型很快也将推出。与竞争对手的顶尖 AI 模型相比，Muse Glimmer 规模更小，定位也有所不同。模型可以在只有一张显卡的 Mac 或 PC 上运行智能体任务，瞄准直接在个人设备运行 AI 的需求。
扎克伯格在 14 页的长文《未来属于所有人》中呼吁：让 AI 得到广泛普及，而不是掌握在少数人手中。“认为 AI 危险到只有把权力高度集中起来才安全，这种想法本身就有问题。”
Meta 还准备公开当前旗下最先进模型 Muse Spark 1.2 的权重。该模型由去年重金组建的超级智能团队开发，被寄予重新追赶 AI 竞赛的厚望。
Meta 长期支持开放模型，也是少数将这一理念付诸行动的美国科技企业之一。不过，去年 Llama 4 反响不佳后，Meta 被迫调整战略。
扎克伯格还宣布设立 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 67.52 亿元人民币）基金，向社区提供支持，希望缓解外界对 Meta 大规模建设数据中心影响当地社区的担忧。他还坦言，与中国等国家相比，美国的一大劣势就是基础设施更难建设。
扎克伯格还表示，如果美国企业希望在开放权重模型领域领先，就必须重新审视数据使用和蒸馏等一系列政策。
谈到开源模型时，扎克伯格称：“外国实验室目前在多个方面占有优势，因为美国实验室在训练数据方面要遵守更多限制。如果希望美国的开源模型长期保持领先，美国政策就必须减少这些额外阻力。”
他还指出，限制获取外国开源模型并不能解决问题。

驰为曾宣传其平价笔记本 UniBook 配备 100% sRGB 色域覆盖的 IPS 面板
。但在实际测试中，这款笔记本的色域规格明显对不上厂家宣传口径。
据报道，驰为在这款 UniBook 的商品页宣称，这款笔记本配备雾面 IPS 面板，分辨率为 1920*1200，覆盖 100% sRGB 色域。
IT之家在此援引 Notebookcheck，该媒体在实机测试中发现，厂商宣传的“完整覆盖 sRGB 色域”说法不符合实际情况。评测人员打开该笔记本就发现了异常，屏幕显示效果明显不如那些 100% sRGB 色域的产品。
随后 Notebookcheck 使用专业色彩测试软件 CalMAN 进行分析，
结果显示该笔记本的屏幕仅覆盖不到 60% sRGB 色域
更严重的问题在于，
驰为在这款笔记本上市后仍然宣传
该机配备 100% sRGB 色域覆盖的面板
该媒体后续联系了驰为进行确认。驰为确认了他们的测试结果，并将官网的“100% sRGB 色域覆盖”宣传语删除。如果消费者在规格修改前购买该笔记本，然后发现产品的实际规格与宣传存在出入，那寻求退货退款应该不会有太大问题。
考虑到驰为今年初的“虚假 CPU”事件，这次的显示屏规格问题进一步引发外界担忧。

title: 宝马最新研究：先进技术可回收报废车辆 51% 材料，并用于新车
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据外媒 BMW Blog 今天（10 日）晚间报道，宝马集团及合作伙伴开展的 Car2Car 研究项目显示，报废汽车中真正能够重新用于新车制造的材料比例，还有提升空间。
Car2Car 项目研究如何让报废车辆中的钢、铝、铜、塑料和玻璃重新进入汽车生产体系。采用更先进的处理和分选技术后，宝马定义的“Car2Car 回收率”从 6% 提高到了 51%。
IT之家注：这里的 51% 并不是整车可回收比例，而是指从报废汽车中回收后，质量仍足以重新用于新车制造的材料占比。
不同材料的改善程度相差很大。采用先进回收工艺后，钢材的 Car2Car 回收率从 1% 大幅提高到 81%，铝从 23% 升至 52%，铜也从 48% 提高到 68%。
相比之下，塑料和玻璃若以新车所需的质量重新进入汽车供应链，仍有难度。要实现上述提升，也不能只是把报废汽车送进传统粉碎机。
项目还探索了更细致的预分选、改进后的粉碎工艺、传感器材料分选和分类，并进一步区分不同种类的铝合金。按照当前更常见的处理方式，整体 Car2Car 回收率只有 6%。
钢材最能体现精细分选的作用。报废汽车中的线束、连接器等部件会让废钢混入铜杂质，导致回收钢材无法满足高品质汽车薄板钢的要求。Car2Car 项目增加了一道分选工序，降低废钢中的铜含量，使其能够重新用于生产汽车所需的扁钢。
完成再生钢测试后，宝马在莱比锡工厂进行了生产试验，使用项目回收的材料制造了超过 10 万个量产零部件并装配到车辆上，其中部分预计用于全新 i3 轿车，该车型的再生材料占比达到 30%。
项目使用的回收材料来自 433 辆报废汽车，覆盖宝马集团 60 款车型。宝马表示，实现上述回收率并不需要在现行强制拆解流程之外大幅增加拆车工作。
不过，51% 的成绩是在经过优化的研究和示范环境中实现的，现有回收设施并不能普遍达到同样水平。若要大规模推广，还需要继续投资拆解、分选、处理设备和基础设施。塑料和玻璃尤其难处理，当前的汽车使用多种不同配方的塑料和复合材料，分离和再利用远比金属复杂。
宝马表示，还需要进一步改进分选和处理技术，才能稳定达到新车制造的质量标准。宝马在电动汽车电池等难度较高的回收领域也取得了进展，不过相关工作主要由回收与拆解中心负责。
Car2Car 项目也为宝马未来从设计阶段提高汽车可回收性提供了数据支持。研究成果将纳入现有的“Design for Circularity”工作，让车辆在投产前便考虑材料最终如何回收并重新用于生产。

title: 扎克伯格呼吁美国放宽开源 AI 限制，以应对中国竞争
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据路透社报道，Meta 首席执行官马克 · 扎克伯格近日呼吁美国政府减少限制开源 AI 模型，以便与中国竞争对手抗衡。
据IT之家此前报道，Meta 今天推出 AI 模型 Muse Glimmer，采用 4bit 量化技术，使其可在 24GB/32GB 显存的 Mac 或 PC 上本地运行。
扎克伯格认为 AI 技术应该普及，而不是握在少数机构手中。他对此解释称：“认为 AI 只有极端集权才是安全这种观点，本来就存在问题。”
扎克伯格此番表态引起开源 AI 模型圈子热议。随着各大企业不断担忧 AI 成本上涨，以及 Anthropic、OpenAI 近期发生的网络安全事件，越来越多人开始关注开放权重 AI 模型。
开放权重模型的训练成本，通常比 OpenAI、Anthropic 等公司的闭源模型成本更低。同时这些模型的核心组件是公开的，用户完全可以自定义。
中国各大企业正在开放权重模型竞争中领先。月之暗面的 Kimi K3、阿里巴巴的 Qwen3.8-Max 以及 DeepSeek 的 V4-Flash，都已经能够与美国顶尖 AI 模型正面竞争。

title: 新调查显示：AI 时代下，超八成家长和老师认为学生应具备更强的数据素养
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据外媒 Phys.org 今天报道，DS4E 和 Mathematica 近日发起的调查显示，随着人工智能重塑教育和就业，越来越多家长认为，青少年应在教育阶段就拥有更强的数据素养。
据报道，本次调查收集 1333 名家长、教师和教育局官员的问卷。各方普遍认为，数据素养应成为 K-12（IT之家注：幼儿园到高中）教育的核心学习内容，IT之家附具体结果如下：
- 88% 受访者认为，所有学生应在高中毕业前具备数据素养能力；
- 84% 受访者认为，数据素养和数据科学应融入更多学科，而不是局限于数学和计算机科学；
- 76% 受访者认为，AI 发展让数据教育的重要性达到前所未有的高度。
大多数受访人士认为，比起掌握技术，学生更应该在 AI 时代学习解决问题的能力和批判性思维，并扎实学习数学、科学和英语等基础学科。相比之下，他们认为编程、编写提示词（Prompt）并不是 AI 时代优先学习的东西。

title: 日产在美国工厂部署 AI 摄像头，能帮装配工人“纠正”操作姿势
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据外媒 Carscoops 今天（10 日）报道，日产已开始在美国密西西比州坎顿工厂用 AI 分析装配工人的动作。
厂内安装的摄像头能够识别关节位置和身体角度，判断员工是否弯腰过度、长时间保持别扭姿势，或没有按照标准顺序完成操作。
日产为每项装配工作设定了一套名为“golden cycle”的标准动作，不仅规定零部件安装顺序和完成时间，也包括员工操作时应该采用的动作方式。
AI 发现异常动作后，管理人员和工程师会进一步检查原因，可以据此指导员工改用更安全的动作、调整工作岗位，也可能直接修改工位设计。系统不仅能发现员工是否偏离标准操作，也能帮助日产判断工作流程本身是否需要改进。
日产强调这套系统并非用于取代员工。日产制造业务高管维克托 · 泰勒回应称：“我们讨论的不是取消岗位。相反，AI 主要用于改善培训、淘汰低效操作，并进一步减少员工受伤。”
起初，人体工学甚至并非开发重点。日产流程工程师奇 · 阿梅奇表示，公司最初研究这套系统，是为了提升培训和生产效率，后来才发现 AI 也能识别可能伤害员工身体的动作。
日产表示，这项技术已经为坎顿工厂节省约 3,400 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2.3 亿元人民币）的安全和健康成本。
日产取消纯电动汽车计划后，坎顿工厂未来将重点生产卡车和电动化 SUV。随着资深员工退休，这套系统也更有价值，因为几十年积累的制造经验无法一夜之间补上。

title: 杰富瑞分析师：因良率不佳，苹果已砍掉 20 周年全玻璃 iPhone 机型
content:
IT之家 8 月 10 日消息，据彭博社今天（10 日）报道，杰富瑞分析师李裕生（Edison Lee）将苹果股票评级下调至“跑输大盘”，市场对苹果的看空情绪进一步升温。
李裕生对 iPhone 前景表示担忧，尤其是苹果未来能否继续提高产品平均售价。“供应链调查显示，由于生产良率不佳，苹果已经取消 20 周年全玻璃 iPhone。这表明，苹果想通过改变 iPhone 产品形态来提高平均售价，比预想中更加困难。”
李裕生预计，下个月亮相的可折叠 iPhone 将成为未来几年提高平均售价和利润率的唯一关键动力。但内存芯片等关键零部件价格大涨，势必推高新机售价。“我们仍然认为，如此昂贵的手机只会是一款小众产品”。
杰富瑞此前给予苹果“持有”评级，此次不仅下调至“跑输大盘”，还将目标价从 285.56 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,928 元人民币）降至 263.66 美元（现汇率约合 1,780 元人民币）。苹果股价上周五收于 313.33 美元（现汇率约合 2,116 元人民币）。
数据显示，目前已有 6 家机构给予苹果相当于“卖出”的评级，追平 2012 年以来最高纪录。KeyBanc Capital Markets 上个月也因担忧需求和估值，将苹果评级下调至“减持”。
苹果目前的市场综合评级为 5 分制 3.88 分，创 2019 年以来最低水平。该指标反映买入、持有和卖出评级的比例。目前不到 60% 的分析师建议买入苹果股票，远低于微软、亚马逊和英伟达 —— 三家公司获得的买入推荐比例均超过 90%。
苹果股价周一盘前下跌 1.3%。按上周五收盘价计算，股价已较近期高点回落约 8%。
苹果公布季度业绩后股价再度走弱。受零部件短缺影响，苹果给出的销售预期未能达到市场期待。

Fraunhofer SCAI hat seine Verpackungssoftware PackAssistant um die Planung von Paletten- und Lkw-Beladungen sowie eine Kostenberechnung erweitert. Damit bezieht die neue Version zusätzliche Stufen der Transportkette in die Verpackungsplanung ein. Unternehmen können nun mehrere Lösungen hinsichtlich ihrer Verpackungs- und Logistikkosten vergleichen.
Kern der Software bleibt die platzsparende Anordnung baugleicher Teile in Behältern. Die dreidimensionale Verpackungsplanung basiert auf CAD-Daten und berücksichtigt neben Länge, Breite und Höhe auch die tatsächliche Geometrie der Bauteile. PackAssistant berechnet daraus Anordnungen, die den verfügbaren Raum bestmöglich nutzen und die Teile zugleich vor Beschädigungen schützen. Vor allem bei komplex geformten Komponenten kann die Berechnung aufwendige manuelle Packversuche verkürzen oder ersetzen. Verpackungslösungen lassen sich dadurch bereits während der Produktentwicklung untersuchen.
Auf dieser Behälteroptimierung bauen die neuen Funktionen auf. Steht die Anordnung der Bauteile fest, platziert PackAssistant die beladenen Behälter auf Paletten und ordnet sie anschließend im Laderaum eines Lkws an. Auch eine Beladung ohne Paletten ist möglich. Die benötigten Behälter-, Paletten- und Lkw-Typen kann man über die Benutzeroberfläche auswählen.
Das Ergebnis der Berechnung stellt die Software grafisch dar. Auf diese Weise ist nachvollziehbar, wie der vorhandene Raum im Behälter, auf der Palette und im Fahrzeug genutzt wird. Für eine realistischere Darstellung werden nun auch Packmaterialien wie Trays, Inserts und Gefache direkt angezeigt.
Zusätzlich weist PackAssistant die Kosten der berechneten Varianten aus. In die Kalkulation fließen unter anderem Aufwendungen für unterschiedliche Packmaterialien, Behälter sowie für die Logistik ein. Angezeigt werden die Kosten pro Bauteil sowie die daraus abgeleiteten Kosten für einen Behälter, eine Palette und einen kompletten Lkw. Für den Straßentransport nennt das Programm außerdem die Kosten je Fahrt.
Die Ergebnisse zeigen, welche Lösung den Raum am kostengünstigsten nutzt und wie viele Behälter, Paletten oder Transporte dafür benötigt werden. Sie können außerdem in die Angebotserstellung und in die logistische Kalkulation einfließen.
PackAssistant richtet sich vor allem an Industrieunternehmen, die häufig große Stückzahlen baugleicher, auch komplex geformter Teile verpacken. Mehr als 400 Kunden nutzen die weltweit über 2.000-mal installierte Software. Fraunhofer SCAI entwickelt das Programm. Die scapos AG, ein Spin-off-Unternehmen von SCAI, übernimmt den Vertrieb über ein internationales Netz von Distributionspartnern.

title: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
content:
AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
AI agents that can model the human process of research will accelerate discoveries in science.
Every few decades, someone announces that science has reached its end. In 1903, the revered physicist Albert Michelson wrote that the “facts of physical science have all been discovered.” In the 1980s, Stephen Hawking predicted that theoretical physics might be finished by the end of the century. With the explosive arrival of artificial intelligence, the feeling is in the air again—this time accompanied by a Nobel Prize.
In 2024, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of Google DeepMind were awarded part of the Nobel in chemistry for their neural network AlphaFold, which predicts the three-dimensional structures of proteins by learning from thousands of experimentally measured shapes. This devilish problem had resisted systematic attacks for half a century; AlphaFold seemed to have solved it once and for all, and the world became fixated on the promise of its approach. Hassabis and his team called AlphaFold “the template for how AI can accelerate all of science to digital speed.” A wave of startups building foundation models for biology, chemistry, and materials discovery raised billions of dollars, buoyed by DeepMind’s success. AlphaFold had shown that the combination of AI and sufficient data could make groundbreaking discoveries (even if we did not understand the underlying mechanisms involved), and it seemed, once again, that a path through the rest of science was laid out before us.
To be sure, AI will bring extraordinary changes to science, but it has become increasingly clear that AlphaFold, and things like it, may not be the best template for that metamorphosis. Though it is a profound achievement, the conditions that produced the likes of AlphaFold are rare, and the time it will take to meet those conditions in other fields will be measured in decades, not years. Instead, the acceleration of science will come about thanks to another approach: AI agents.
The primary condition for AlphaFold’s success was the existence of the Protein Data Bank, a data set of roughly 170,000 experimentally validated protein structures on which DeepMind’s team could train its model. The creation of the Protein Data Bank was not simple: It took 53 years of international scientific cooperation and, by a recent estimate, roughly $21 billion worth of experimental work to assemble. Efforts of that scale are infamously difficult to fund, next to impossible to coordinate, and hugely time-consuming to execute; they have often been unsuccessful as a result.
But even in fields with the requisite cohesion and resources, and where the relevant data are not rendered inaccessible by commercial ownership, another barrier is too little discussed: the scientific impossibility of generating comparable data. In the case of protein structures, the key experimental technique—protein crystallography—is an unusually replicable and dependable tool, so much so that over 25 Nobel Prizes have relied on it. But in most of experimental science, results vary more often than not. Cell lines drift. Chemicals have trace contaminants. Lab humidity changes. The creation of measured datasets that will be consistent enough, accurate enough, precise enough, and scalable enough to train a modern neural network in biology or most of chemistry would require new kinds of measurement and new standardized approaches—none of which will be ready anytime soon.
Of course, there are a handful of fields where these requirements are met: weather forecasting, much of genomics, very limited areas of chemistry. These may see AlphaFold-style breakthroughs soon, if they haven’t already. Government support for the production and coordination of those datasets will be critical, as the US National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology has argued. But for most open questions in science, we will need a different plan, at least in the short term. Luckily, something quieter and more modest has begun to show promise.
Scientists have always reasoned under uncertainty. Biologists working to identify new drug targets have never had perfect datasets. Instead, they combine docking calculations and known structures, factor in molecular dynamics, run a handful of binding assays, and use their judgment to weigh each method according to its particular strengths and points of failure. The skill of science is not in any single tool; it is synthesizing what many tools produce, and revising the results as the evidence comes in. This is how most working research actually proceeds. But until very recently, no software could do it.
Agents now can. Simply put, an agent is an AI reasoning engine that has been given access to tools—digital or physical—and the capabilities to use them. Over the last few years, a fundamental architectural shift in AI has enabled the rapid proliferation of these programs, which are powered by large language models, dramatically reducing the need for scientifically specialized datasets. For science, this technological advancement represents a foundational change: it has allowed us to create digital tools that can mimic the iterative, highly contingent process of actual research. While tools like AlphaFold apply a powerful approach to a limited question, agents are inherently generalists. They do not represent a new way to do science—instead, they digitally model the human process of discovery.
Consider Google’s AI Co-Scientist, announced in May. Researchers gave it a one-page brief and a goal: Figure out how antibiotic resistance spreads between bacterial species, a key driver of drug-resistant infections. The system spun up sub-agents. One drafted hypotheses from the literature. Another picked them apart like a peer reviewer. A third ran tournaments to rank the strongest candidates. A fourth refined the winning hypothesis. The agent concluded that resistance genes were hitching rides on bacterial viruses, borrowing whichever virus could ferry them into a new host. The hypothesis was correct. Researchers at Imperial College London had spent a decade reaching the same conclusion through painstaking wet-lab work; their paper, previously unseen by Co-Scientist, was still in peer review.
Agents like Co-Scientist are still novel tools, and there are real challenges to overcome before they become a ubiquitous part of the scientific process: They are still liable to hallucinate, their judgment is not consistent, and they have memory and input constraints that limit the time they can run autonomously. But these technical barriers will fall away, and as they do we will begin to notice the compounding effects of scientific agents on the reliability, consistency, and velocity with which science is done.
Perhaps most notably, agents offer a structural fix for science’s “reproducibility crisis,” the widespread problem of researchers’ inability to replicate each other’s results. For decades, the scientific community has begged researchers to share their raw data and exact code in an effort to standardize experimental processes. But researchers have long resisted this tedious administrative work, which happens after the interesting science is already done. Agents, in contrast, automatically log every move they make, creating an exact record of the method that led to their results and allowing for precise replication.
A second consequence will be an amplification of scientific memory. The transfer of knowledge between researchers is a famously murky process; if it isn’t done over years of training and observation, graduate students are left to pore through the messy lab notebooks kept by decades of predecessors, looking for the details that will make or break their protocol. As agents become an increasingly large part of the scientific process, though, a lab’s entire scientific history will be recorded in a central, standardized repository of institutional knowledge.
But the most important impact of agents will be speed. In any field, when testing an idea takes less time than arguing about it in a meeting, people stop debating and just run the test. An agent that can read a thousand papers in an hour, design 500 molecules, and learn from its failed tests by morning will bring down the cost of experimentation and fundamentally change the pace at which science gets done. It will also give researchers the freedom to chase bold, strange questions they never would have risked their time on before, opening scientific doors we have yet to imagine.
While the AlphaFold template will certainly be key to incredible discoveries, it alone will not bring us to the end of science. Instead, the shift toward agentic AI represents a much rarer tier of breakthrough: a tool that envelops every field of science at once. Historically, tools of such scope have arrived just a handful of times: calculus, statistical inference, spectroscopy, the computer. Each revealed a world of problems no one had thought to formulate, and those problems, in turn, defined their fields anew. With agents, another such transformation is upon us.
Eric Schmidt was the CEO of Google from 2001 to 2011. In 2024, with his wife Wendy, he co-founded Schmidt Sciences, a philanthropic venture to fund unconventional areas of exploration in science & tech.
Suhas Mahesh leads AI for Science work at the AI Center of Schmidt Sciences. He is a specialist in AI for materials discovery.

title: These startups are chasing the next big thing in LLMs
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
MIT Technology Review
’s What’s Next series looks across industries, trends, and technologies to give you a first look at the future. You can read the rest of them
Way back in the summer of 2017, AI researchers at Google put out a paper called
“Attention Is All You Need,”
in which they described a new type of neural network called a transformer. It proved to be very good at processing long sequences of data, especially text.
Nine years on, transformers are the engines inside every major large language model on the market. “The entire AI industry is built on transformers,” says Justin Dangel, cofounder and CEO of the AI startup Subquadratic. “They are one of the most important innovations in the history of computer science, and they’ve changed the world.”
But transformers are starting to show their age. Many of the recent advances in LLMs, such as the development of so-called reasoning models and their ability to handle large amounts of input at once, are not neat extensions of that core technology but workarounds that patch over some of its fundamental flaws.
A growing number of scientists and engineers are now asking what’s coming next. LLMs are not going anywhere, but the way they get built is up for grabs. (
MIT Technology Review
dubbed this future generation of models
in this year’s list of the
10 things that matter in AI
Enter a wave of startups hoping to push the boundaries of this boomtown technology. Some will no doubt fail—but they have everything to play for and far less to lose than the companies at the front of the pack today.
Strength in numbers
But first, the problem. The key strength of transformers lies in a mechanism called dense attention, which
encodes the meaning of a block of text in a series of numbers
. The process involves comparing every word (or part of a word, known as a token) in that text with every other word via a form of multiplication.
Dense attention can capture the meaning of text with remarkable accuracy. But as the length of that text grows, the number of computations needed to process it adds up fast. A document 10,000 words long might require a transformer to perform 50 million multiplications. That’s the main reason
LLMs suck up so much power
The costs are huge. OpenAI is set to
spend $50 billion on computing this year
, according to the company’s president, Greg Brockman. And the International Energy Agency predicts that the total
amount of electricity consumed by data centers will double by 2030
What’s more, transformers struggle with what many of the latest models are designed to do. Because of the way they process text word by word, transformers are not great at keeping track of a lot of information at once (in other words, what's known as their context window cannot get too large). And yet if LLMs are to carry out harder tasks, they will need to take in larger amounts of data: a whole library of documents, an entire code base, or in the case of agents, output from other LLMs.
As for reasoning models, they work by writing notes to themselves (in a kind of
scratch pad known as a chain of thought
) and then reading them back, which again adds to the amount of data to stay on top of.
As LLMs get bigger and better, transformers have become a bottleneck. The technology’s key strength is now a limitation.
Here are four new ideas for how to solve the transformer problem—innovations that could change LLMs for good, making them faster, far more efficient, and (maybe) even smarter.
01: Rethinking attention
An obvious way to make LLMs faster and cheaper is to tackle the problem head on and change the way attention works. Swapping out dense attention for a mechanism called sparse attention, which runs calculations on only some pairings of words in a block of text instead of all of them, can radically reduce the amount of computation LLMs need to do.
Researchers have come up with plenty of sparse attention mechanisms over the years. The problem is that none of them were as good as dense attention at capturing meaning.
That might have changed. Subquadratic, a startup based in Miami, claims it has invented the first sparse attention mechanism that rivals top mainstream LLMs on a handful of tasks, including search and coding. It’s a huge claim (and
some people in the industry remain skeptical
Subquadratic says its model, SubQ, works by figuring out on the fly—for each piece of text it is given—which words matter and which don’t. The company also claims that thousands have signed up to its waitlist and plans to make the model widely available soon.
Meanwhile, Manifest AI, a startup based in San Francisco, is coming at the problem from a different angle. Instead of changing how attention works, it is replacing it with something else.
It has developed a mechanism it calls power retention, which stores only the most relevant information for a given task and ensures that the amount of data an LLM has to keep track of doesn’t blow up.
Attention mechanisms force LLMs to keep track of everything in their context window. A sparse attention model (such as SubQ) throws out a lot of the individual words, but it still retains a rough picture of everything it has seen. In contrast, power retention works by providing the model with a rolling summary of its context window. As new information is added, less relevant information is dropped.
The basic principle of retention has been around for a decade. Manifest AI claims it has updated those techniques to build models that can stand up to transformer-based LLMs for the first time.
The company says it is possible to adapt a transformer model into a power retention model with minimal retraining. To demonstrate this, it has turned an existing open-source coding LLM called StarCoder into a version that uses power retention, called PowerCoder. It has also released a model called Brumby, which it claims rivals some versions of Alibaba’s popular open-source model Qwen.
Manifest AI wants its power retention tech to become the go-to solution when LLMs need to carry out tasks that involve processing huge amounts of data. There are many useful applications, Manifest AI’s cofounder and CTO, Carles Gelada, claimed in a video announcing his company’s technology last year—from analyzing videos that are hours long to building agents that can stay on task for weeks at a time.
02: Making models smaller and more flexible
Liquid AI, an MIT spinout based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, hasn’t changed or ditched transformers fully but pairs them with its own tech, liquid neural networks, to build what cofounder and CEO Ramin Hasani calls LFMs (liquid foundation models).
Liquid AI’s models are far smaller and use less energy than most LLMs. The firm builds models for car makers, including Mercedes, which run on the small chips inside vehicles. Its latest models can run on a Raspberry Pi, a low-powered hobbyist computer that costs $50.
Its models are available for free to any organization with an annual revenue less than $10 million. And they have proved popular: The company has racked up almost 34 million downloads, says Hasani.
Liquid neural networks were inspired by worm brains. They are an extension of another type of neural network that predates transformers, called convolutional networks. The key innovation is a mechanism that lets a model adapt its behavior to new information, so it can learn as it goes. That’s not possible with transformers: Once a model is trained, its behavior is fixed.
Liquid AI’s first models were pretty basic but could fly drones or drive vehicles. With LFMs, the company is trying to scale up its technology to compete with mainstream LLMs. Its new models match the performance of rivals four times bigger, including versions of Alibaba’s Qwen and Google’s open-source LLM Gemma.
A typical LLM is built from a stack of transformers wired together. Liquid AI’s recent LFMs are hybrid models made up of 20% transformers and 80% liquid neural networks.
That ratio was hit upon by another AI system that Liquid AI has built, which it uses to help design all its models. “It’s the core technology of our company right now,” says Hasani. This designer AI sifts through many different combinations of neural networks—liquid, convolutional, and more, as well as transformers—and comes up with designs that bolt different ones together to hit a sweet spot of performance and efficiency.
Hasani thinks transformers were just the beginning: “Your brain is an AGI system, you know, and it operates with 20 watts of power. How is it possible? We can get a lot more innovative.”
03: Generating text all at once
Almost all LLMs produce their output one word at a time. It makes sense, because that is how people speak and write. But for computers, it’s very inefficient.
It is faster and cheaper for LLMs to generate text all at once—spitting out whole sentences or paragraphs in one shot. That’s the approach taken by Inception, a startup based in Palo Alto, California, which is building LLMs using a technique called diffusion.
Diffusion is better known as the technology that drives most
image and video generation models
. Diffusion models are trained to take a random grid of pixels—like the static on an old TV set—and
turn it into an image
. They do this by working on all the pixels at the same time, figuring out which need changing to make the static look more like a high-definition photo.
It turns out this process works on text too. Inception has trained its LLMs to take a random string of words and turn it into sentences that make sense. Diffusion LLMs still use transformers to encode meaning, but by producing whole blocks of text at once, they make transformers do more for less. “You’re still using a big transformer model, but you can predict many tokens at the same time,” says Inception’s cofounder and CEO, Stefano Ermon. “That’s why these models are so much faster and cost-efficient compared to what most other people are building today.”
The challenge was to take a technology designed for image generation and apply it to text. With images, if you need to change a blue pixel to a red one you can step through intermediate colors, says Ermon. That doesn’t work with text: “When you have ‘cat’ and ‘dog,’ there is not really something in between.”
Ermon is also a researcher at Stanford University. In 2024, he and a pair of his Stanford colleagues figured out the math to make diffusion models work with text. They trained a diffusion model that matched the performance of GPT-2—an LLM that OpenAI built in 2019—but was 10 times faster. It was enough for Ermon to spin out a company.
Today he has his sights on the big league. Inception claims its latest model, Mercury 2, performs as well as some of OpenAI’s GPT-4 models, released in 2023, but again 10 times faster. “We’re bullish about this approach because it’s the one that is going to scale up,” says Ermon.
The only things that matter are speed and cost, he adds: “Ultimately, the currency is going to be intelligence per dollar.”
Inception is not the only company betting on diffusion. Google is also experimenting with this approach and has built a prototype LLM called
Diffusion Gemma
. But Ermon is not worried about the competition. “I think it's validating,” he says. “This is the future.”
04: Moving beyond words
Pathway, another startup based in Palo Alto, is perhaps the most extreme of this new bunch. It wants to free LLMs from the constraints of language.
The firm has built a type of LLM called Dragon Hatchling (named after the dragons in Terry Pratchett’s novel
Color of Magic
, which materialize if you think about them hard enough). Its standout result so far is a high score on a benchmark that pits LLMs against more than 250,000 very hard sudoku puzzles. Dragon Hatchling beat more than 97% of the puzzles; several leading LLMs from the top labs failed to solve any.
The point Pathway wants to make is that despite their remarkable success at many different tasks, there are still crucial classes of problems where LLMs fail. Sudoku is just one example. If we want LLMs to come up with genuine, novel solutions to real problems, we need to move beyond transformers, says Pathway’s cofounder and CEO, Zuzanna Stamirowska.
That’s because transformers force LLMs to do everything with text. But language is not the best tool for certain kinds of reasoning. “It’s very difficult to represent a sudoku board word by word,” says Stamirowska.
Pathway’s solution is to change the math behind the transformer, replacing the attention mechanism with a mathematical structure called a state space. Instead of encoding information word by word, state spaces compress it into a more abstract representation. Using this technique, Dragon Hatchling can still process and produce text, but it can also mimic forms of reasoning that do not involve sequences of words. This not only makes Pathway’s model more efficient, but (in theory) it lets it take on tasks that other LLMs cannot do.
Think of chess or mathematics—those kinds of puzzles are not held in your head as a long sentence, says Stamirowska: “The eureka moment that pops up in your brain isn’t necessarily in language. We would argue that if you have to reason in language, you’re somehow constrained.”
Stamirowska admits that a mainstream LLM could read a book about how to solve sudoku and then write code to do it. But we want to build models with more than book smarts, she says: “The hope for AI is not to solve sudoku; it’s to cure cancer. There’s not a book for that.”
“Transformers are an engineering convenience that we fell on,” she adds. “It started a religion, but it’s silly to think that a breakthrough won’t happen again.”

关于宁德时代塑料冷板接头组件的一些专利探讨
2026年4月21日，宁德时代在北京举办超级科技日新品发布会，正式发布第三代麒麟电池。第三代麒麟电池的电芯能量密度达280Wh/kg，在实现1000公里续航的同时，标配10C超充，电池包重量控制在625kg，与市售同级别千公里续航磷酸铁锂车型相比，减重255kg，空间节省112L。
优秀的轻量化指标为整车带来的收益非常显著。第一、能耗方面，百公里能耗降低6%以上，每百公里节省约0.78度电，以每车年行驶2万公里、100万辆规模计算，年节电量达1.56亿度，可减少二氧化碳排放7.85万吨，相当于种植255万棵乔木、覆盖1250公顷绿地。
第二、操控与安全方面，零百加速时间缩短约0.6秒，超车并行危险窗口期降低12%；麋鹿测试通过车速提升8%，车身侧倾角减少6.5%，极限避险能力提升15%至25%；百公里制动距离缩短约1.44米。据中汽研等机构数据，百公里制动距离每缩短1米，高速事故概率可降低8%。
第三耐久性方面，底盘关键部件寿命提升40%，轮胎寿命延长30%，以前3至4万公里需更换，现在至少多跑1万公里。节省的112L空间可为座舱增加至少18mm头部空间，或用于优化整车风阻设计。
电池包的轻量化可以从电芯、单体电池和pack整包结构去设计。
本文拟从专利的角度来看看宁德在散热组件的减重上做的一些尝试，侧重于从冷板两端的接头组件专利去挖掘一些宁德的减重设计思路。
为了解决电池的热管理问题，一般会在电池模组的内部设置冷板，冷板位于多个电池单体的一侧，冷却板的内部有供冷却介质流动的通道。这种结构的冷板由于本身具有较大的重量，且在注入冷却液后会导致冷板的重量进一步增加，使得具有这种冷板的电池的重量较大，从而导致电池整体的能量密度下降。基于此，宁德一直在探索冷板减重的尝试。
整体散热结构概览
先来看下整体的散热结构。如下图所示，宁德在模组的单体电池间采用的还是传统的侧面冷板（下图换热机构），但在冷板的两端，采用了注塑一体的接头设计。宁德在专利里给这个接头结构统称为“集流体”。这个“集流体”有别于我们传统认知的电池正负极上采用的铜铝箔集流体。这里的“集流体”是指冷却介质流通到两边接头时的流体收集结构。下文所称的“集流体”均指冷板两端的接头组件。
（该专利电池包结构图与麒麟电池产品图相似）
冷板的内部结构类似于口琴管的结构，是多通道设计。冷板是金属结构，两端的集流体结构是注塑一体结构。注塑集流体可以有效降低集流体的生产成本。然而不同的材质连接，密封性和可靠性是设计的重点。所以宁德在2024年申请的专利里有大量的连接结构设计专利。2024年的相关专利申请量也是最多的一年。可见宁德在这个结构设计上做了深度研究。
核心专利技术分类解析
宁德时代围绕塑料冷板接头组件的技术攻关，从连接强度、密封防漏、智能监控、装配效率、碰撞缓冲到整包级流体管理，形成了多层次的技术覆盖。
（一）连接强度与可靠性
异种材料（金属冷板与塑料集流体）的连接是技术核心难点。宁德时代在多个专利中提出了不同的解决方案：
1)专利CN120261797A在冷板和集流件之间增加套筒和封堵结构，以提高集流件和冷板的连接强度。
CN120261797A
2)专利CN223285180U设计连接件注塑包覆连接冷板与集流体，提升连接稳定性。
CN223285180U
3)专利CN223993290U中，集流件通过转接件与换热板密封配合且连接，可降低换热板、集流件和转接件之间的安装难度，提高连接可靠性，并能减小封堵件的尺寸，降低电池单体膨胀时局部面压较大的风险。
CN223993290U
4）专利CN223842953U设计转接部外套于换热管的一端并设有多个转接通道，集流体固定至转接部并设有集流口和至少一个导流通道，以降低集流体与换热管的装配难度，提升装配质量，并提高换热管的换热效果。
CN223842953U
5）专利CN223828490U针对现有电池装置中换热器集流体与转接环通过端面钎焊成型导致焊接端面宽、集流体高度高、易与其他结构干涉、影响电芯安装和电池装置布局的问题，提出转接部与集流体插接配合，并通过插接部焊接连接，减小整体尺寸，增强连接强度和密封性；采用插接凸起和槽结构增大摩擦力，稳定焊接过程。该方案减少了换热器整体尺寸，避免结构干涉，提高了焊接效率和密封性，方便电池装置的结构布局与安装。
CN223828490U
（二）密封防泄漏
密封失效是异种材料连接的致命缺陷。宁德时代在密封方面同样布局了多项专利：
1）专利CN221928280U在集流体上设置卡接件和密封件，提高可靠性，防止密封失效。
CN221928280U
2）专利CN120834320A通过连接部和封堵部的组合，降低安装难度，提高连接可靠性和密封效果，增强封堵部对换热流道的封堵效果，减少泄漏风险。
CN120834320A
专利CN221126065U在集流体上设置感应装置，用于监控换热介质的压力、流速、温度中的一种或多种。该设计将传感器集成于接头组件，实现了对冷却系统运行状态的实时感知，为热管理系统的智能化控制提供了硬件基础。
CN221126065U
（四）装配效率与浮动容差
大规模制造对装配效率提出了高要求。专利CN121097277B中，集流部件与换热端部通过柔性连接结构连接以形成浮动间隙。柔性连接件可为一体注塑件，也可为塑胶件、橡胶件或硅胶件，该结构可有效提高装配效率。
CN121097277B
（五）碰撞缓冲保护
电池包的安全性不仅体现在热管理，还涉及碰撞工况下的结构防护。专利CN224036547U中，集流体包含形变区域，能够在受力时产生形变，吸收碰撞冲击力，从而保护换热板。该形变区域可由弹性材料制成，例如橡胶、塑料等注塑成型，也可为金属、合金等形成的弹片、弹簧等。
CN224036547U
（六）整包级流体管理
除单块冷板接头结构的设计外，宁德时代还考虑了整包层面的接头设计，以实现流体的分流和汇流。专利CN223757565U设置了进出口接口件，实现流体的分流和汇流，进行电池单体与流体的换热。该设计将接头组件的功能从单板连接拓展至整包流体网络，体现了从零件级到系统级的完整技术闭环。
CN223757565U
专利布局策略与时间特点
从专利申请的时间线来看，宁德时代的塑料冷板接头组件专利系统申请始于2023年，2024年申请量最为密集。值得注意的是，大量专利从申请到公开仅间隔1-2个月，推测走了专利审查的预审通道，表明宁德时代希望这些专利能够快速授权。这一策略充分说明该技术方向对宁德时代具有重要战略意义，因此进行了重点专利布局。
从专利内容来看，宁德时代的布局覆盖了从单点改进（连接、密封、传感、缓冲）到系统集成（整包分流）的完整技术链条，形成了多层次的知识产权保护网。这种密集而系统的专利布局，不仅保护了自身的技术创新，也提高了竞争对手进入该领域的技术门槛和专利壁垒。
宁德时代作为全球领先的动力电池制造商，在冷板塑料接头组件方面已展开系统性专利布局。从本次分析的专利来看，其技术路线聚焦于以下核心方向：
第一，金属冷板与塑料接头组件的结构融合设计，涵盖密封性能、可靠性和装配效率的全面提升。第二，电池包层面多流道分配的进出口接头设计，实现从零件到系统的完整技术覆盖。
这些专利技术体现了宁德时代在轻量化目标下对散热组件细节的深度打磨。通过将金属冷板与塑料接头的技术难点逐一攻克，宁德时代在降低电池包重量、提升能量密度的同时，确保了系统的可靠性与安全性。
后续值得关注的方向包括：全塑料冷板的可行性探索、更先进的密封材料与工艺、适配更高电压和更高流速的下一代接头设计，以及该领域专利布局对行业竞争格局的深远影响：可能推动接头组件的标准化，进一步提高后来者的进入门槛。我们将持续关注宁德时代在塑料冷板接头组件以及塑料冷板领域的专利公开情况，敬请期待。
