title: SpaceX Plans to Power $16.8B Terafab Without the Grid
content:
SpaceX plans to power its massive
semiconductor and advanced-computing campus in Grimes County, Texas, with onsite generation and battery storage rather than electricity from the grid, according to a fully executed
tax-abatement agreement
with the county.
The agreement states that the facilities, once operational, “are expected to be powered by electricity generated by on-site power plant(s) and are not expected to use electricity from the grid.”
SpaceX and Tesla
announced
an initial $16.8 billion investment in Terafab on Aug. 6. The companies outlined plans for a 100-million-square-foot campus in Grimes County.
Texas incentive filings
describe a four-phase project with a potential investment of up to $119 billion. The county’s June 3 order
designating the site as a reinvestment zone
describes the development as including a semiconductor manufacturing plant, an artificial intelligence facility, and a power plant.
Related:
SpaceX IPO Filing Recasts Company as AI Infrastructure Giant
The county agreement also references “the battery storage project,” making onsite generation and storage part of the contemplated infrastructure. That would put SpaceX in charge of infrastructure typically provided by the electric grid, including generation, reserves, voltage and frequency control, storage, and restoration.
Power Is Part of the Plan
The tax-abatement agreement specifies how SpaceX expects the facilities to operate: onsite power plants will supply electricity, and the facilities are not expected to use grid electricity.
That does not establish that Terafab will have no physical connection to the grid.
Neil Osnato, founder of Persistence Analytics Group, said the distinction is important because a facility can remain grid-connected while relying on onsite generation under normal conditions.
“For industrial facilities to use onsite generation, cogeneration, or dedicated power is not unusual,” Osnato told
Data Center Knowledge
. “For a semiconductor/AI complex of the scale being contemplated here to plan for primary self-supply with essentially no routine grid electricity is much more unusual.”
Meeting annual energy needs isn’t enough for a semiconductor fab. Its manufacturing processes require high power quality, continuity, and protection from voltage, frequency, and other disturbances that can interrupt production.
That makes Terafab’s planned power system more than a conventional backup power installation.
Natural Gas Enters the Picture
Riley Trettel, SpaceX’s lead developer for Terafab, reportedly told Grimes County commissioners Aug. 5 that SpaceX plans to build natural gas-fired power plants and large battery arrays. The tax-abatement agreement itself does not specify the fuel, technology, and capacity for onsite plants.
Related:
Data Centers in Space: Hype, Reality, and the Long Timeline Ahead
Osnato said a facility designed to operate primarily from onsite generation would need to function more like a private utility than a conventional industrial customer.
That could mean multiple generating units, reserve capacity, redundant electrical buses and substations, black start capability, and redundant gas delivery. Battery systems could provide fast response during generator trips, load changes, and other events, while gas generation supplies sustained energy.
“Gas provides energy and sustained capacity; batteries provide speed, stability, and continuity,” Osnato said.
Batteries Add Another Layer
The county agreement’s road-use provisions specifically refer to construction, installation, maintenance, and operation of “the
battery storage
project.”
The agreement does not provide the battery project’s capacity, duration, or technology.
In addition to power, SpaceX plans utility infrastructure for water and wastewater at the campus. The agreement says the company will use commercially reasonable efforts to control water use and promote reuse, and that it intends to construct an onsite wastewater treatment facility. It also indicates SpaceX does not intend to use groundwater for operations, subject to specified exceptions.
Related:
Data Center Space Race: Can Orbital’s Satellites Overcome Doubts?
The combination would give SpaceX control over several infrastructure systems that typically depend on public utilities.
Implications for ERCOT
If Terafab routinely self-supplies, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) would see lower delivered load at the point of interconnection. However, the reliability boundary would shift inside the fence line: instead of relying on ERCOT’s generation, transmission, and distribution, Terafab’s operations would depend on its own gas supply, generators, batteries, and internal electrical network.
“If Terafab is genuinely electrically islanded and never takes ERCOT power, then its operating load would largely sit outside the normal ERCOT load-serving problem,” Osnato said.
A grid connection would change that calculation. Startup power, emergency imports, backup service, or exports would create an ongoing operational relationship with ERCOT even if routine energy comes from onsite assets.
The county agreement says the facilities are “not expected to use electricity from the grid,” rather than saying they will have no grid connection.
That leaves Terafab’s electrical architecture as a potentially important precedent as Texas accommodates increasingly large AI and industrial loads.
A Different Model for Large Loads
Terafab is planned as a vertically integrated semiconductor and advanced-computing campus. SpaceX and Tesla have said the facility will produce chips for Tesla vehicles and Optimus robots as well as SpaceX’s computing systems.
SpaceX has framed the strategy more broadly in its IPO filing, saying the key constraints on AI growth are “physical chip manufacturing, data center infrastructure, and power generation” and that “the future of AI will be determined by the control of the physical stack.”
The companies have set a target to produce enough chips to support 1 terawatt of computing capacity annually. That figure describes the computing capacity of the chips, not Terafab’s electrical load or onsite generating capacity.
The initial phase involves a $16.8 billion investment, while Texas incentive filings describe four phases totaling a potential $119 billion in investment.
The project’s planned power architecture sets it apart from conventional large-load projects. SpaceX is not simply seeking electricity for a massive industrial campus; it is planning to build the generation and storage needed to supply that campus alongside the manufacturing facilities.
For Texas grid planners, that creates a new category of large load: a facility whose gross electricity demand may be enormous while its routine grid demand could be substantially smaller.
Osnato described the broader issue as a shift in the reliability boundary.
“Behind-the-meter generation does not eliminate the reliability problem,” he said. “It relocates the reliability boundary.”

title: Why Data Center Development Is Facing a Legal Reckoning
content:
The rising summer heat has also brought a rise in temperatures from the anti-data center movement. While NIMBYism is not new in American life, the rapid escalation of the anti-data center movement is driving it toward litigation.
Already this summer, just in Texas, we have seen Hill County enter into and then
quickly abandon
a data center moratorium after the filing of a $100 million lawsuit, the scuttling of a proposed data center by Diode Ventures near Cedar Creek Lake after organized community opposition formed, and Governor Greg Abbott putting a
freeze on new data center development
until an audit of the Texas grid is completed.
Nationally, over $64 billion in projects have been blocked or delayed across two dozen states, with over 140 activist groups popping up overnight. For data center developers, litigation may be the only recourse.
Defamation as a Tool to Combat Misinformation
Rhetoric and tactics by data center opponents need to be carefully monitored and logged because when advocacy turns into misinformation, it can lead to litigation.
Related:
Ofgem Fee Aims to Clear Grid Queue – Who Benefits?
Case in point is last year’s jury verdict in
Energy Transfer v. Greenpeace
regarding Greenpeace’s opposition to Energy Transfer’s Dakota Access Pipeline.
Energy Transfer sued Greenpeace for spreading a multi-year misinformation campaign that falsely claimed that the pipeline crossed tribal land, that it destroyed sacred sites, and that its security used violence on protestors.
A North Dakota jury awarded Energy Transfer more than $667 million on its defamation claims, despite the need to prove actual malice by clear and convincing evidence. The lesson from that case is that when protestors or activists cross the line into spreading outright falsities, defamation law can be a powerful check on their tactics.
Critical Factors to Consider
When using defamation as a tool to combat misinformation, there are three key issues to keep in mind.
First, not all statements are actionable under defamation law. Subjective opinions are not actionable (i.e., “I don’t want that data center near my property,” or “data centers destroy the environment,” or “data centers are a scourge on society”). Only misstatements of objectively verifiable facts are actionable (i.e., “data centers do not pay property taxes,” or “data centers emit dangerous radiation”).
Second, the speaker is important. A single local resident making an actionable misrepresentation at a town hall or city council meeting is probably not worth pursuing for multiple reasons. But a well-funded group running advertisements containing a falsehood might be. Especially if – as recent reports have indicated – such a group is funded by foreign money with an ulterior motive (a fact which could be fleshed out in discovery).
Related:
Hinton, Fei-Fei Li, and Andrew Ng Clash Over AI Risks and Regulation at Ai4
Anti-SLAPP as a Sword and Shield
Finally, many states (including Texas) have anti-SLAPP laws that provide a strong shield against speech made in matters of public concern, such as data center development. Anti-SLAPP laws require courts to rigorously scrutinize defamation claims early in the process, often through a motion to dismiss.
While a typical lawsuit can take years to work through the system and slow development, anti-SLAPP motions to dismiss require the plaintiff to provide specific evidence of falsity, fault, damages, and malice.
A party cannot file a lawsuit subject to anti-SLAPP and hope to later develop the facts through discovery. Instead, the filing party must have prima facie proof of each element described in the filing.
The penalty for not doing so is that a court can not only dismiss the case at the pleading stage but also award attorneys’ fees to the defendant for having to fight the lawsuit. Thus, losing an anti-SLAPP motion to dismiss could cost hundreds of thousands of dollars in attorneys’ fees for a losing plaintiff.
Related:
Europe Has Built Sovereign AI Infrastructure. It Didn’t Build the Ability to Govern It.
Likewise, in certain circumstances, a data center developer facing a baseless lawsuit can use anti-SLAPP as a sword against that suit if a protestor interferes with the right to free speech or the right to petition the government.
This would speed up litigation and avoid the trap of a project stalling while litigation takes years to progress.
For example, if a protestor files suit against a developer claiming that the developer is misrepresenting facts to the local government to obtain approval for the development, then the developer can invoke anti-SLAPP to dispose of the claim relatively quickly. But anti-SLAPP would not apply to many other categories of lawsuits (i.e., nuisance claims, zoning cases, cases solely against the government authorities).
Preparing for the Legal Challenges Ahead
No one starts developing a data center expecting litigation to result. But as pushback against data centers becomes more organized and widespread, parties should begin to anticipate the likelihood of litigation.
When parties feel they have no recourse, such as in jurisdictions with limited land-use authority, litigation may be the only tool to block or slow development. Likewise, a developer may need to resort to litigation to clear opposition that has crossed the line.

title: Will Edge AI Make AI Data Centers Less Relevant?
content:
If you made a list of emerging AI trends, edge AI – running AI workloads at or near where data is generated rather than in centralized data centers – would probably make the cut. In a world where businesses worry about sending sensitive data to third parties and the latency of remote services, putting models closer to users promises gains in control and performance.
Those same dynamics raise questions for the data center industry. Much of the
explosive growth
in data center infrastructure in recent years has rested on the assumption that enterprises would host AI models centrally rather than at the edge. If edge AI accelerates, will that make AI-focused data centers less critical?
What Is Edge AI?
Edge AI is the practice of running AI models or applications on edge infrastructure – such as local servers or endpoints – instead of remote hyperscale or
colocation data centers
That’s not how most major AI platforms have been delivered so far. The models behind public services like ChatGPT and Gemini run in hyperscale facilities and are accessed over the internet. Even many privately built or hosted models typically live in data centers rather than on local endpoints or on-premises servers.
Related:
Smartphones as Micro Data Centers: A Creative Edge Solution?
Edge AI offers a different deployment path: keep models and data close to where they’re produced and consumed, often on hardware you control, and access them over local or private networks.
Why Run AI at the Edge: Security and Latency
Edge AI delivers advantages in two core areas: security and performance.
Edge AI can also reduce exposure to network-based attacks. Keeping model endpoints behind internal firewalls – and off the open internet – makes them harder for remote attackers to discover and exploit. Attacks such as
prompt injection
are easier to launch against publicly exposed interfaces than against on-premises services with no direct internet connection.
In terms of performance, edge AI often reduces latency. Rather than sending data from a user device to a distant data center and back – a round trip that can take tenths of a second to several seconds depending on network performance – local networks typically deliver faster, more consistent response times.
Edge AI Today: Local Models, Hardware, and Investment Signals
These benefits help explain why interest in edge AI is rising.
Related:
‘Inference Is Bigger Than Any One Chip’ – d-Matrix CEO on GigaIO Deal
One signal is the growing popularity of local LLMs – models designed to run on end-user devices instead of in the cloud. Once dismissed as impractical due to endpoint hardware limits, local LLMs have gained traction as more efficient architectures and tooling improve on-device performance.
Another is increased investment in edge AI infrastructure and services. IDC’s
Worldwide Edge Spending Guide
(February 2026) predicts a 2024-2029 CAGR of 24.4% for edge AI spending, reflecting strong and accelerating enterprise interest.
A Potential Threat to Data Center Investment
For individuals and businesses, edge AI offers clear advantages. For data center operators, it introduces uncertainty.
The more AI moves to the edge, the less pressure there may be to host models in large centralized facilities. That dynamic could be unwelcome news for companies that have poured capital into
AI-optimized data center buildouts
, many of which are still underway. If a significant share of workloads shifts to the edge, those facilities risk being underutilized.
Why Edge AI Probably Won’t Kill Data Centers
That said, edge AI growth doesn’t have to come at the expense of AI in traditional data centers.
In many scenarios, enterprises are likely to invest in both. They’ll place workloads with especially sensitive data or ultra-low-latency requirements at the edge, while continuing to run other models in centralized environments.
Related:
Edge Data Centers vs. Edge Devices: Which One Fits Your Strategy?
Practical considerations reinforce this hybrid approach. Deploying AI-optimized hardware at scale – GPU-enabled servers, high-bandwidth interconnects, and advanced cooling – is often more feasible and cost-effective in large data centers, where economies of scale improve power, cooling, and operational efficiency.
Physical security matters, too. Edge locations are generally less physically secure than tiered data centers, which can make organizations cautious about placing expensive GPUs and other accelerators in distributed sites.
In short, while edge AI is poised to become an increasingly important way to host AI workloads, it’s unlikely to displace traditional data centers. Some recent AI data center investments may not achieve expected utilization, but if that occurs, edge AI is unlikely to be the primary cause.

title: Cyprus' first utility battery project goes online: Interview - Energy Storage
content: Cyprus has taken its first step into commercial battery energy storage, with a 5 MWh system connected to the island’s electricity grid and entering commercial operation in July. The project, developed by electricity supplier Petrolina Electric, marks the first participation of a utility battery system in Cyprus’s electricity market and could provide a practical blueprint for the wider deployment of storage on the island. Known as the ‘Pavlina Memorial Energy Park’, the hybrid facility combines 1.8 MW of photovoltaic generation with a 5 MWh battery. The battery is installed behind the meter, allowing electricity generated by the solar plant to be stored and subsequently used when it is most valuable. The project has also been developed and is operating without government subsidies. The Pavlina Memorial Energy Park comes at a time when Cyprus is facing a growing mismatch between the rapid expansion of solar power and the ability of the electricity system to absorb it. From January to May this year, Cyprus needed to curtail 162 GWh of renewable energy, equivalent to over 65% of potential solar generation . Dr Andreas Prokopiou, founder of CyprusGrid, a platform specializing in analysis of the Cypriot electricity market, estimates that the battery could return approximately 1.3–1.6 GWh of electricity to the grid each year that would otherwise be curtailed. His estimate assumes one charge-discharge cycle per day and a typical round-trip efficiency of 85 to 90%. With average annual household electricity consumption in Cyprus estimated at approximately 6,000 to 9,000 kWh, Prokopiou says the amount of electricity recovered would be equivalent to the annual consumption of roughly 150 to 270 households. “Those numbers are not large enough to alter Cyprus’s overall energy balance,” Prokopiou told ESS News . “[However], they demonstrate something far more important: that the business and technical model behind the commercial operation of battery storage systems in Cyprus can work.” Cyprus’ energy storage market development has been extremely slow. The government introduced its first-ever energy storage subsidy scheme at the beginning of 2025, offering subsidies for the purchase and installation of energy storage units behind the meter and alongside existing solar PV, wind and biomass power plants. Cyprus introduces energy storage subsidy scheme The scheme had a competitive character and would run until 2027, during which time the government was supposed to publish several open calls for bids. However, the first call for bids in February 2025 was unsuccessful, and to date, the government hasn’t reported whether investors engaged with it or not. Cypriot energy market investors have told ESS News separately that several policy details made Cyprus’ storage subsidy scheme in 2025 unattractive and that the scheme is now considered dead. On the contrary, investors have been applying for licenses allowing them to build and operate unsubsidized battery projects, tied to existing renewable energy storage facilities. Interest in such projects is strong, but the regulatory process is slow, delaying the issuance of grid-connection terms. The Pavlina Memorial Energy Park is, on the other hand, a project that was able to face the regulatory bottleneck and become operational. Investors agreed it can serve as a blueprint for similar projects, allowing all stakeholders taking part in the regulatory process to derive useful lessons.  Furthermore, as reported across countries and agencies during the surge of energy storage installations, meaningful energy storage capacity is critical for the country’s green energy transition and energy market competitiveness. title: Czechia connects 318 MWh of batteries in H1 - Energy Storage
content: Czechia added 318 MWh of new battery capacity during the first half of 2026 (H1), according to figures released by Czech solar association Solární Asociace. The figure represents an 83% increase in added capacity when compared to deployments during the first half of 2025, which reached 174 MWh. There were 12 standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) connected to the Czech grid in H1, with a total capacity of 108 MWh. For comparison, there were zero standalone storage systems commissioned during the first half of 2025. Jan Fousek, Director of Czech storage association AKU-BAT, commented that the Czech market has shown there is huge interest in battery storage since the entry into force of the Lex OZE III amendment, which formally introduced legal frameworks for large-scale energy storage, aggregation and grid flexibility services. He added that further development will logically be limited by the capacity of distribution networks and transmission systems. “The regulatory environment and tariffs will have a significant impact on investor appetite,” Fousek said. “These will decide whether batteries will be used where they bring the highest value – to households, industry and the entire electricity system.” Fousek pointed to a power outage in Czechia on July 4 this year when deployed battery storage and aggregated flexibility proved its value in the market. “Our members from the flexibility aggregators alone provided around 50% of aFRR regulation services, previously secondary regulation, with their batteries at that time, thus proving their irreplaceable role in the security of system operation,” he said. The rollout of standalone storage in Czechia looks set to continue. Projects in the pipeline including two BESS with a combined capacity of 320 MWh , to be delivered by China’s AlphaESS. Last December, the company said its 230 MWh Chvaletice project and 90 MWh Kladno projects will become the country’s largest standalone energy storage installations. Battery storage is also helping to maintain solar deployments in Czechia. Of the 9,346 solar power plants installed in the country during H1, Solární Asociace says 8,079 were equipped with battery storage systems. Earlier this year, the Czech government began to consider proposals that would prevent double taxation on projects installing both storage and solar. While behind-the-meter installations have traditionally made up the majority of Czechia’s battery fleet, analysts are expecting utility-scale storage to lead the development of the Czech market through to the end of the decade, by which point battery storage capacity is expected to reach 6 GWh. title: Standalone BESS to offer up to 12% returns in Greece, Aurora forecasts - Energy Storage
content: A standalone two-hour battery energy storage system (BESS) entering operations in Greece next year could achieve an internal rate of return (IRR) of approximately 11-12%, according to analysis by Aurora Energy Research . The consultancy says this IRR is around two percentage points higher than an equivalent project commissioned in 2030, with current elevated power market volatility causing global gas market uncertainty and creating near-term opportunities for both battery storage and renewables in Greece. Greece remains heavily exposed to developments in global gas markets, with gas-fired generation accounting for up to 45% of electricity supply. Aurora’s latest analysis expects Greek wholesale electricity prices to average around €100 ($115.44)/MWh through to 2029. Beyond the ongoing uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz, Greece’s wholesale prices are expected to be impacted by the European Union’s planned phase-out of Russian LNG imports, with remaining pipeline gas flows expected to cease next year. Aurora says a complete stop of remaining Russian gas supplies could result in a 27% increase in Greek gas prices and a 13% increase in Greek baseload prices by 2028. “These findings suggest that, despite expected capital expenditure reductions and increasing price cannibalization by 2030, near-term market volatility continues to support the economics of both utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects entering the market as early as 2027,” Aurora explains. Sokratis Al Zoampie, Research Analyst at Aurora Energy Research, pointed out that BESS and renewables returns are likely to vary significantly depending on how gas supply disruptions unfold. “However, history suggests that policy interventions often follow periods of market stress and have the potential to correct market disruptions,” Al Zoampie added. “In this respect, the upside for projects may prove temporary rather than structural.” Greece supported the development of its battery storage market with a series of three government-backed auctions, the last of which concluded in March 2025 , before turning its attention to an unsubsidized scheme. A total 900 MW of standalone storage was approved across the three auctions rounds but Greece has struggled to connect such projects, with some insiders citing institutional blocks. In March, ESS News reported that investors have submitted applications for over 12 GW of standalone battery projects in Greece, far exceeding a 4.7 GW target set by the government. title: GM exits $3.5B Indiana battery plant as Samsung SDI takes full control
content:
Samsung SDI
Fred Lambert
| Aug 11 2026 - 6:12 am PT
Samsung SDI is taking full control of its Indiana battery plant. The South Korean cell maker is buying out General Motors’ 49.99% stake in their joint venture, according to a regulatory filing, ending GM’s ownership in the $3.5 billion factory.
That turns the New Carlisle, Indiana plant into Samsung SDI’s first wholly owned battery factory in North America.
A joint venture that lasted about two years
GM and Samsung SDI first announced the partnership in April 2023 and
finalized the $3.5 billion joint venture in 2024
. The plan was a 680-acre site in New Carlisle producing NCA-based, nickel-rich prismatic cells under Samsung’s PRiMX brand, with 27 GWh of annual capacity to start and room to scale to 36 GWh. Mass production was slated for 2027, alongside more than 1,600 jobs.
It was the second Samsung SDI battery plant tied to a US automaker after its
Stellantis joint venture
, and part of a wave of gigafactory announcements that assumed US EV sales would keep climbing through the decade.
They didn’t climb fast enough.
Samsung SDI buys the whole thing
Under the deal, Samsung SDI acquires GM’s 49.99% holding in the venture, filed under the name SDI-GM Synergy Cells Holdings, and converts it into a wholly owned subsidiary. The purchase price wasn’t disclosed.
Samsung SDI tied the move directly to the market. “The ownership change was made in consideration of market changes since the joint venture was announced, including the slower-than-expected growth of EV demand,” the company said.
The two aren’t cutting ties completely. Samsung SDI and GM signed a separate agreement to jointly develop next-generation prismatic batteries for potential future EV use. GM keeps a supply relationship; it just no longer owns the plant.
There’s also a tell in what Samsung SDI plans to do with the factory now that it owns it outright: add an energy storage system (ESS) battery line. That lines up with the company’s
pivot from EV cells toward stationary storage in the US
, which we covered in December, as grid-scale and data-center demand outpaces the US’s abysmal EV take rate compared with the rest of the world.
Investors weren’t thrilled about Samsung SDI absorbing the risk on its own. Shares fell roughly 4.5% on the news.
The tax credit is the backdrop
The timing isn’t a coincidence. US automakers cut EV production after the $7,500 federal tax credit ended on September 30, 2025, and the demand hangover has been rippling through the battery supply chain ever since.
GM has felt it directly. The automaker took a roughly $6 billion charge as it scaled back EV production plans, and its other big battery bet, the Ultium Cells venture with LG Energy Solution, has spent the past year idling and recalling workers as output plans shift. Now GM is handing a battery plant to its partner rather than funding it.
So this is GM stepping back from owning battery manufacturing at the exact moment it’s most exposed to soft demand, and Samsung SDI betting it can repurpose the capacity toward storage.
Electrek’s Take
GM is famously quick to follow political winds in the US rather than staying course firmly toward electrification.
GM committed to a wall of battery capacity when Washington was paying buyers $7,500 to take EVs off lots. Pull the credit, and GM was quick to pump the brakes.
However, it’s not all bad. At least, the factory is still happening. Rather than keep pouring money into a plant it half-owned, GM is offloading the equity to Samsung SDI and keeping only a supply and co-development arrangement. It’s the cheaper, lower-risk position, and it tells you how confident GM is about near-term US EV volume. Not very.
For Samsung SDI, the interesting part is the ESS line. The company all but told us in December that its US future is stationary storage, not just EV cells, and taking full control of New Carlisle gives it a plant it can flex toward whichever demand actually shows up. Grid storage and AI data centers are screaming for cells right now. US EV buyers, post-credit, are not.

title: Oil giant rips out gas pumps for BYD's 1,500 kW EV chargers
content:
Fred Lambert
| Aug 11 2026 - 7:28 am PT
Sinopec, China’s biggest fuel retailer, just gutted one of its Shanghai gas stations and swapped the pumps for BYD’s 1,500 kW flash chargers.
And this wasn’t a case of bolting a couple of chargers onto the edge of the forecourt. Sinopec pulled the underground gasoline tanks out of the ground and turned the whole site into an EV-only charging hub.
An oil retailer tears out its own fuel infrastructure
The station sits at 1209 Huqingping Road in Shanghai, and it’s the first site jointly operated under the BYD-Sinopec partnership. Where the fuel storage tanks used to be, there are now BYD’s second-generation Blade batteries buffering the chargers.
A state oil company dug up its own gasoline tanks to make room for battery packs.
The hub runs six of BYD’s “T”-shaped chargers, each with two cables, for 12 charging spots total. They’re laid out like the pump islands they replaced, which is the point. The muscle memory of pulling in, plugging into an overhead dispenser, and leaving in a few minutes carries straight over.
BYD rates the flash chargers at up to 1,500 kW on a single connector. On a compatible car with a second-gen Blade battery, that’s 10 to 70% in about five minutes, and 10 to 97% in roughly nine. Cold weather stretches it to around 12 minutes at -30°C.
How an old gas station pulls off megawatt charging
A 1,500 kW charger drawing straight from the grid would need a substation-grade connection. No ordinary gas station has that. So BYD doesn’t ask the grid for it. Each charger is backed by four Blade LFP battery packs holding 169-185 kWh, and those buffers deliver the megawatt burst to the car. The site only pulls about 100 kW from the grid to keep the batteries topped up.
So an old fuel station can do megawatt charging without a grid rebuild. The buffers also double as backup power if the grid drops, which keeps the chargers live during a blackout.
It’s the same buffered-battery approach BYD has leaned on since it
committed to deploying 15,000 megawatt chargers across China
, built around the
1,000V Super E-Platform
it confirmed last year. The Sinopec deal is what puts that hardware on real estate that already has cars pulling in and out all day.
The converted station isn’t bare, either. Sinopec kept its 24/7 unmanned “Easy Joy” convenience store and added a rest area with reclining chairs and a health monitoring station while drivers wait out the charge.
Part of a much bigger BYD-Sinopec deal
The two companies signed an industrial and capital cooperation framework on June 3, covering the charging network, integrated services, and supply chain. We covered that agreement when it landed, in
BYD is deploying 2.4x more charging power per month than Tesla
. The Shanghai station is the first physical result of it.
The scale on Sinopec’s side is the whole story. It runs more than 30,000 service stations, over 14,000 charging and battery-swap stations, and serves roughly 20 million customers a day. Every one of those forecourts is a candidate for the same treatment.
BYD, for its part, had built over 6,100 flash charging stations as of late May and is targeting 20,000 in China by the end of 2026. Sinopec’s footprint and its ability to deploy them without a grid upgrade is how it gets there faster.
Sinopec chairman Hou Qijun framed the deal as a push to “jointly promote the green transformation and upgrading of China’s transportation network.” BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu has been pitching a “Flash Charging China” strategy built on the second-gen Blade battery, and BYD executive Li Yunfei has been posting the Shanghai rollout on Weibo. Sinopec says similar conversions are coming to other stations.
Electrek’s Take
This is the image the oil industry has spent billions trying to delay: a state petroleum company digging its own gasoline tanks out of the ground and dropping battery packs in the hole.
Read it as a hedge, not a conversion of faith. Sinopec sells fuel to 20 million people a day, and it can see China’s passenger market going majority-electric. It would rather cannibalize its own forecourts than watch BYD, or anyone else, build a rival network on new land and take the traffic with it. Owning the real estate is the moat, and Sinopec already owns 30,000 of the best-located pieces of it.
To be fair, the deal is not unique. We have seen petroleum companies and gas stations invest in EV charging before, but the scale here is on another level. The scale and the speed of deployment.
The buffered-battery design is the part US and European charging companies should study. The reason megawatt charging feels impossibly expensive here is that everyone assumes you have to rebuild the grid connection to deliver it. BYD’s answer is that you don’t. Put a battery between the grid and the car, pull 100 kW in, push 1,500 kW out. That turns a gas station lot into a megawatt hub without waiting years for a utility upgrade.
The catch is the same one it’s always been: this only hits 1,500 kW on cars engineered for it, and outside China that’s nobody right now. But the infrastructure playbook here, cheap to deploy, grid-friendly, sited where drivers already stop, is one the rest of the world doesn’t have an answer to yet.

title: The 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron delivers more driving range than expected
content:
Audi Q6 e-tron
Peter Johnson
| Aug 11 2026 - 7:10 am PT
Audi’s midsize electric SUV drove further than advertised. The 2027
Q6 e-tron has an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 301 miles, but in the real world, it traveled even further.
2027 Audi Q6 e-tron beats EPA range in the real world
Audi introduced
several big updates
to the Q6 e-tron for the 2027 model year, including a new infotainment system, the return of physical buttons, and improved regenerative braking for better efficiency.
The 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron with standard 20″ tires has an
EPA-estimated driving range
of up to 301 miles, but in everyday driving conditions, it will likely drive even further.
Edmunds’ EV Range Test
, the 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron covered 337 miles on a single charge, beating its EPA-estimated range of 301 miles, or about 12%. The extra 36 miles is enough for at least another day or two of commuting.
Audi’s electric SUV was also more efficient. The 2027 Q6 e-tron achieved an energy consumption of 29.3 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 35 kWh per 100 miles by around 16%.
2027 Audi Q6 e-tron (Source: Audi)
Edmunds EV Range Test
is designed to offer a more accurate estimate of a vehicle’s driving range and efficiency in real-world, everyday driving situations.
It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The team stays within 5 mph of the speed limit, the climate control is on auto at 72 degrees, and the vehicle is in its most efficient drive mode.
2027 Audi Q6 e-tron infotainment system (Source: Audi)
With a real-world driving range of 337 miles, the Audi Q6 e-tron is among the longest-range luxury electric SUVs that
has tested.
The 2026 BMW iX xDrive and Cadillac Optiq still beat it, traveling 338 miles and 339 miles, respectively. However, the Q6 e-tron drove further than the 2025 Porsche Macan 4S and Macan Turbo, which covered 323 miles and 301 miles during the test, respectively.
2027 Audi Q6 e-tron interior (Source: Audi)
Starting at $64,500, the Q6 e-tron is also considerably cheaper than the Porsche Macan 4S ($89,900) and Macan Turbo ($84,600).
Measuring 187.8″ long, 76.2″ wide, and 66.6″ tall, with a wheelbase of 113.7″, the Q6 e-tron is about the same size as the
and Porsche Macan EV.

title: Ukraine debuts mine-resistant all-wheel drive combat electric motorcycle
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Military
Micah Toll
| Aug 11 2026 - 8:29 am PT
Electric motorcycles have already proven themselves in military roles thanks to their quiet operation, but Ukraine has just taken the concept several steps further. The country’s newly approved MUL.E electric motorcycle is more than just another battery-powered dirt bike – it’s an all-wheel-drive machine specifically designed for battlefield logistics, stealth operations, and even traversing certain minefields.
Ukrainian Ministry of Defense
approved the MUL.E for operational use late last month, marking the debut of what is being described as Ukraine’s first all-wheel-drive electric military motorcycle.
So far, there has only been one image provided of the bike, and it clearly appears to be either generated or altered by AI, but it gives us some insight into what the Ministry of Defense intends for the new platform. And considering the number of electric two-wheelers already serving in the defense of Ukraine, it’s not far-fetched to imagine the MUL.E soon entering service alongside them.
At first glance, the MUL.E looks more like an oversized electric fat tire bike than a conventional motorcycle, but that’s part of its anti-mine design. Wide low-pressure tires help spread the vehicle’s weight over a much larger footprint, reportedly allowing it to exert ground pressure similar to that of a soldier on foot. The idea is that this can reduce the likelihood of triggering pressure-activated anti-tank mines, which require far greater force than anti-personnel mines.
It’s worth noting that this certainly doesn’t make the bike “mineproof.” Mixed minefields containing anti-personnel mines remain extremely dangerous, and no vehicle should be viewed as safe for operating in mined areas. But reducing ground pressure is still an interesting engineering solution for military mobility in areas where anti-tank and anti-vehicle mines would deny entry to typical military jeeps, trucks, and tanks.
The bike’s other features read like a wishlist for battlefield transportation. Dual electric motors provide all-wheel drive for improved traction across mud, snow, sand, and marshland, while the nearly silent electric drivetrain makes it much harder to detect than a gasoline-powered motorcycle. That’s a significant advantage for reconnaissance missions or moving personnel and supplies near the front lines, and Ukraine has
famously taken advantage of two-wheeled electric vehicle platforms before
for just such roles.
Range is listed at around 62 miles (100 km), but it can be extended with an onboard gasoline generator. Instead of relying on charging infrastructure, troops can recharge the motorcycle’s batteries wherever fuel is available. The generator also allows the bike to double as a portable power station for field equipment, giving it utility beyond simply transporting riders.
The MUL.E is also designed to tow cargo trailers, helping move supplies through terrain that would bog down larger military vehicles while maintaining a much lower acoustic and thermal signature.
We’ve seen electric motorcycles increasingly adopted by militaries around the world over the last several years, largely because of their stealth advantages. The US military
has evaluated e-bikes and electric dirt bikes
other countries
have explored similar concepts for reconnaissance and special operations.
Ukraine’s MUL.E seems like the next logical evolution of that idea. Rather than simply replacing a gasoline motorcycle with an electric one, the design embraces the unique advantages of electric propulsion while adding features specifically tailored to modern battlefield conditions.

title: 超12.2GWh！宁德时代/东方日升等6企储能订单落地
content:
近期，储能市场订单及项目建设持续推进。宁德时代、东方日升、绿色能源公司接连获得储能订单；同时，由卫蓝新能源、远东电池、星星充电供货的多个构网型储能项目陆续并网投运。
宁德时代获海外3GWh储能订单
近日，全球独立发电商ContourGlobal宣布与宁德时代达成电池供应协议。宁德时代将为其在英国、希腊和智利的储能项目提供储能系统，总规模约3GWh。
英国项目包括500MW/2000MWh的苏格兰Wallace储能项目；
希腊地区，ContourGlobal已布局约500MW/2000MWh储能资产组合；
智利地区，其Victor Jara光储项目配套200MW/1.3GWh储能系统，具备6.5小时长时放电能力。
东方日升获10MWh工商储订单
近日，东方日升与东莞市晟羽能源科技有限公司签署2026年度工商业储能柜10MWh战略合作协议。
本次签约，晟羽能源正式成为东方日升广东区域授权样板合作伙伴，依托原厂产品供给、技术支持、交付保障，为广东工厂、产业园区、商业综合体提供可靠的储能硬件底座。
绿色能源获3.6GWh储能设备订单
近日，绿色能源公司与铁投能源（天津）有限公司签订2027年度储能设备采购框架合作协议，年度合作规模达3.6GWh。
根据协议，绿色能源公司将负责储能核心设备供应、系统集成及技术支撑，铁投能源则负责宁夏、山西、新疆等区域储能项目资源开发、用地、并网及配套保障，双方将推动3.6GWh储能项目分批落地。
星星充电4GWh储能项目并网
近日，内蒙古锡林郭勒盟东苏变电站两个构网型储能电站实现全部并网，星星充电为项目提供全栈自研5MWh储能柜，共配置800套储能设备，项目总规模达4GWh。
该项目总投资约30亿元，占地约420亩，是内蒙古重点建设的新型储能项目之一。项目采用构网型磷酸铁锂技术路线，预计8月底全面投运。
卫蓝新能源供货构网型储能项目
8月8日，卫蓝新能源宣布，山西转型综改示范区华景和顺400MW/800MWh构网型储能项目近日完成系统出货，并实现首台储能设备吊装。
据了解，该项目位于山西转型综改示范区，总投资约11.5亿元，配置卫蓝新能源自主研发的半固态储能电池系统Spower IV，并搭配变流升压一体化PCS舱，实现储能系统集成与运行可靠性的提升。

title: HEROES project targets green hydrogen production efficiency
content:
HEROES – Heat and Energy Recovery of Electrolyzer Systems – aims to demonstrate one of the world’s most energy-efficient hydrogen production systems. The project is part of Danfoss’ Fossil Free Future Veturi program, funded by Business Finland.
The consortium brings together VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, the University of Vaasa, Convion, Hitachi Energy, Elcogen, and other partners. It combines expertise in power electronics, heat recovery, energy systems, and hydrogen technologies to explore approaches that can improve overall system performance.
Green hydrogen is seen as particularly important in sectors such as heavy industry and maritime, where direct electrification is difficult. However, producing hydrogen remains energy intensive, and improving production efficiency is considered one of the sector’s biggest challenges.
Pia Karumaa, lead of Danfoss’ Fossil Free Future program, said: “As countries and industries work to reduce emissions, hydrogen is becoming an increasingly important part of the solution. The challenge is not whether hydrogen will play a role in the energy transition, but how efficiently we can produce it. Through HEROES, we are bringing together expertise from across industry and academia to tackle one of the most critical barriers to large-scale adoption.”

title: LANXESS powers iron oxide pigment dryer with hydrogen
content:
The spray dryer is described as one of the first large-scale industrial plants in Germany to use hydrogen as a fuel in continuous operation. LANXESS installed the hydrogen burner at the end of 2025 and has been gradually bringing it online since then. The system is designed to run entirely on hydrogen.
Technical integration includes a dedicated hydrogen line, an adapted burner, measurement control technology, and additional safety and control systems.
The hydrogen is produced as a byproduct of chlorine electrolysis at the neighboring Covestro plant and transported directly to the LANXESS facility via a pipeline. The two companies operate within the same Verbund site, where short pipeline routes, shared infrastructure, and established safety concepts support the hydrogen supply.
Michael Ertl, Head of the Inorganic Pigments business unit at LANXESS, said: “Switching from a natural gas burner to a hydrogen burner is a significant technological step towards low-greenhouse-gas processes. We are proving that decarbonizing industry works not only in pilot projects, but also in the day-to-day operation of large production facilities.”
Rob Eek, Production Manager at Covestro in Krefeld-Uerdingen, said: “The project shows that industrial partners at a Verbund site can particularly successfully shape the transition to climate-friendly production.”
LANXESS and Covestro have a long-standing production partnership at the site. Covestro supplies nitrobenzene for LANXESS’s iron oxide pigment production, while aniline produced as a byproduct is returned to Covestro as a raw material. The hydrogen application in the spray dryer adds a further climate-relevant element to that established arrangement.
LANXESS operates what it describes as the world’s largest production facility for iron oxide pigments at Krefeld-Uerdingen, where pigments have been manufactured for 100 years.

title: Power to Hydrogen begins installing 0.5 MW AEM system in Belgium
content:
The system is the first commercial deployment of Power to Hydrogen’s M-Class hybrid anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzers and the first project to use 250 kW AEM electrolyzer stacks. Commissioning is planned for September 2026.
The 0.5 MW system is designed to scale to 25 MW for high-demand industrial environments. It features sub-50-millisecond response for renewable load-following and pressurized operation intended to reduce downstream compression requirements. The technology replaces precious metals used in PEM electrolyzers with lower-cost materials including steel and nickel. Power to Hydrogen has said the approach can reduce capital expenditure by up to 65% compared with comparable PEM electrolyzers.
Once commissioned, the project is expected to establish a repeatable configuration and provide third-party validation to support future multi-megawatt deployments. It is designed to serve both mobility and industrial hydrogen demand in the region and is expected to generate commercial revenue from its first year of operation. The key offtaker at launch is Holthausen, a regional supplier of industrial gases and hydrogen-powered trucks.
Rob Smeets, Chief Executive Officer of Port of Antwerp-Bruges, said: “By welcoming Power to Hydrogen’s commercial-scale AEM electrolyzer, we take another concrete step in supporting the demonstration of scalable, flexible technologies in Europe that are needed in Europe’s energy transition.”
Paul Matter, Chief Executive Officer of Power to Hydrogen, said: “Bringing our system to the Port of Antwerp-Bruges is a tangible step toward financeable deployment: it proves we can build and ship industry-ready hardware, integrate into a live site, and commission a megawatt-class AEM platform designed for renewable load-following.”
Daniel Joisten, Head of Technology Scouting and Innovation at E.ON Energy Infrastructure Solutions, said: “This project at the Port of Antwerp-Bruges is an important step in proving flexible, renewable load-following AEM electrolysis at commercial scale and in building confidence that these systems can be deployed broadly.”

title: 台风过境：宁波用 AI“算”出防汛最优解，预报模型 5 秒生成方案
content:
IT之家 8 月 11 日消息，今年第 13 号台风“白海豚”于 8 月 9 日登陆，给地处三江交汇、濒临海湾的浙江宁波带来强降雨。
据央视报道，作为人均水资源占有量远低于全国平均水平的缺水城市，宁波在台风防御中面临水库既要腾库防洪、又要蓄水保供的两难困境。当地依托数字孪生等智慧水利手段，实现了防洪与蓄水的精细化平衡。
水库调度在台风防御中常面临矛盾：水放多了怕台风改道导致后续用水紧张，放少了又怕雨量超预期威胁大坝安全。
宁波市水利水电规划设计研究院防灾减灾部总监江雨田介绍，这一平衡点需要靠调度软件不断滚动分析计算。该调度软件的核心是一套 AI 预报模型。
以甬江流域为例，以往开展一场完整的方案计算需要 5 到 10 分钟，如今 AI 预报模型仅需 5 到 10 秒，预报时效性从分钟级提升至秒级。根据降雨预报和水位变化，该模型每 5 分钟更新一次调度建议，调度员可据此实时调整下泄流量。
在数字孪生调度平台上，皎口水库与其上游的周公宅水库实现了联合调度。IT之家从央视获悉，两座水库构成“梯级水库”，周公宅的泄流量直接影响皎口的水位。
目前，宁波全市 16 座大中型水库已接入统一调度平台，实现市级、县级、水库管理单位三级联动。哪座水库接近汛限、哪座尚有库容，在大屏上一目了然。
此外，皎口水库大坝内安装了上百个传感器和监测点，包括 121 个坝基渗流点、32 个测压管、19 组三向测缝仪，24 小时不间断向后台传输数据。平时无人机用于替代人工巡查，台风天则由人工加密巡查。
宁波市水利部门数据显示，从 8 月 6 日至 11 日 10 时，全市大中型水库共增蓄水量 4.54 亿立方米。在保证水库防洪安全的前提下，居民供水得到充分保障。据央视报道，浙江省水利厅数字孪生平台已覆盖全省 1 万多个水文站，可在 2 分钟内自动生成防御方案。

title: 微软确认上个月导致 XBOX 大规模宕机的问题已解决，本周推送固件更新
content:
IT之家 8 月 11 日消息，据外媒 VGC 今天（11 日）报道，微软 XBOX CTO 斯科特 · 范弗利特称，导致 XBOX 上个月发生大规模服务中断的故障已经修复，具体原因也已查明。
XBOX 于 7 月 27 日早些时候确认，多项服务出现“重大中断”，玩家因此无法登录账号、查看游戏库，也无法启动部分游戏或应用。XBOX 从首次发文承认服务出现问题，到再次发文宣布故障已经解决，前后相隔 13 小时，而且在官方首次确认之前，服务异常已经持续了一段时间。
随后，XBOX CTO 斯科特 · 范弗利特在 X 上发布长文，说明大规模服务中断的原因，并承诺进一步调查，避免同类故障再次发生。
范弗利特今天转发了上述帖子，并补充说，XBOX 已经找到故障根源：XBOX 常用主机共享、Game Pass 已购内容以及部分 PC 使用场景都依赖一项底层服务。该服务发生中断，而一次系统更新又导致部分服务失去响应。
XBOX 客户端软件栈同时存在一个漏洞，进一步放大了故障影响。最初的底层服务中断后，其他许可证验证也因该漏洞而失败。两个问题随后引发级联故障，导致部分玩家无法启动游戏，并使游戏库内容枚举出现连锁异常。
据IT之家了解，目前，XBOX 已经着手处理故障，并将在本周向用户推送固件更新。
我们正把底层许可服务转交 XBOX 团队负责，同时，工程师正在加固服务和基础设施，提高后续系统更新时的稳定性。
客户端漏洞已经在即将发布的新版本中修复，新版本从今天，也就是 8 月 10 日开始推送，并将在 8 月 17 日转为强制更新。
范弗利特透露，XBOX 工程和运营团队接下来将全面审视整个技术栈，提高产品和服务的可靠性，进一步降低以后再次发生服务中断的可能性。

title: 消息称英伟达开发万亿参数开源 AI 模型 Nemotron 4，目标挑战全球顶级
content:
IT之家 8 月 11 日消息，今天（11 日）晚间，The Information 援引项目参与者消息称，芯片巨头英伟达正在研发新一代 AI 模型系列 Nemotron 4，希望借此与全球最先进的开源模型展开竞争。
英伟达是美国少数主动推出开源模型的大型科技企业之一。今年以来，AI 开发和运行成本持续攀升，而价格更低的中国模型在性能上逐步逼近 Anthropic、OpenAI 等美国领先 AI 实验室的顶尖系统，使开源模型获得更多关注。
近期接连披露的多起涉及自主 AI 智能体的黑客攻击事件，也进一步加大了外界对开源模型的关注，尤其是因为开源模型通常不会对网络安全用途施加限制。
英伟达希望通过开放模型生态扩大 AI 应用范围，并进一步推动市场对其 GPU 算力的需求。英伟达生成式 AI 副总裁 Kari Briski 在邮件中透露：“投资 Nemotron，是因为我们相信每家企业、每个国家都需要可及的前沿开源模型。”
多名参与 Nemotron 4 开发的员工透露，其中规模最大的模型预计至少拥有 1 万亿个参数。英伟达目前尚未确定 Nemotron 4 的发布日期，最终训练也尚未完成。不过报道称，员工认为该模型最早可能在今年秋末准备就绪。
据IT之家了解，英伟达上个月还与多家企业成立联盟，共同开发并共享 AI 安全和网络安全工具。此外，英伟达与微软等科技巨头共同签署公开信，支持开放权重模型，以避免创新能力向海外转移。
另外，英伟达还发布了 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 模型，进一步扩充现有模型产品阵容，主要面向代码审查、工具调用、安全警报监控、回答账单问题等任务。
英伟达同时推出开源模型路由库 NeMo Switchyard，可根据不同 AI 任务的需求，自动将任务分配给最合适的模型。

title: 苹果 Apple Arcade 下月新增两款益智游戏，分别为《Cozy Puzzles+》《舒适拼图 +》
content:
IT之家 8 月 11 日消息，苹果公司今天宣布旗下 Apple Arcade 订阅服务将从 9 月 3 日起新增两款益智游戏，分别是《Cozy Puzzles+》和《舒适拼图 +》。
IT之家了解到，《Cozy Puzzles+》是一款类似《俄罗斯方块》的游戏，玩家需要将不同的彩色方块拖入 8*8 网格中，通过填满横向、纵向的整行来获得更高分数，空间耗尽即代表游戏结束，考验玩家的布局策略。
而《舒适拼图 +》（Art of Fauna: Cozy Puzzles+）则是一款氛围轻松的拼图游戏，内含 18 和 19 世纪的复古野生动物插画与科学文献艺术作品，主打轻松、从容的解谜体验，本作曾获得 2025 年 Apple 设计大奖。
按照惯例，这两款 Apple Arcade 平台的新游戏都不会有广告，也不会有内购项目，主打完全沉浸的体验。

title: 苹果 iOS 27 测试版出现 iCloud+ 限制变化，库克此前曾暗示将对高级 AI 功能收费
content:
8 月 11 日消息，苹果今日发布了 iOS 27 第五个开发者测试版。有用户发现，该版本中出现了与 iCloud+ 订阅服务和 HomeKit Secure Video 相关的新提示，可能暗示苹果未来将针对部分高级功能进行收费。
苹果 CEO 蒂姆 · 库克此前曾表示，部分 Apple Intelligence 功能未来可能会产生额外费用。不过，目前苹果尚未公布具体收费方案。
根据苹果现行 iCloud+ 服务规则，50GB 套餐支持 1 个 HomeKit Secure Video 摄像头，200GB 套餐支持最多 5 个摄像头。而 2TB 至 12TB 容量的高阶套餐则不设限制。
在 iOS 27 开发者测试版 Beta5 中，有用户发现 HomeKit Secure Camera 设置页面出现了与现有规则不同的提示。
使用 2TB iCloud+ 套餐时，页面显示该账户仅支持 5 个摄像头。按照当前订阅规则，2TB 套餐应支持无限数量摄像头。
用户 Stephen Robles 分享的另一张截图显示，系统提示“你的 iCloud+ 套餐包含 15 个摄像头的视频摘要功能”。而他订阅的是最高级别的 12TB iCloud+ 套餐，该套餐目前价格为每月 59.99 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 405.3 元人民币）
因此，上述变化可能是 iOS 27 测试版中的程序错误，也可能是苹果正在测试新的 iCloud+ 服务策略。目前尚无法确认苹果是否计划修改 HomeKit Secure Video 权益。
库克称苹果正评估算力成本，iOS 27 的 Siri AI 额度方案尚未敲定
库克暗示苹果将为高频使用 AI 的 iOS 27 用户增加 iCloud+ 订阅层级

title: Potenzial im Herzen Europas
content:
Potenzial im Herzen Europas
TU-Forscher*innen entwickeln Instrumente, um die sächsische Lausitz auf dem Weg vom Braunkohlerevier zur internationalen Logistikdrehscheibe und zum Tourismusmagneten zu begleiten
Jahrhundertelang war die Lausitz in Sachsen eine traditionelle Bergbau- und Industrieregion. Sie zeichnet sich bis heute jedoch auch durch historische Städte wie Dresden, Bautzen oder Görlitz aus und hat mehrere Weltkulturerbe-Schätze vorzuweisen. Mit dem Kohleausstieg Deutschlands, der bis 2038 abgeschlossen werden soll, steht dem Braunkohlerevier ein tiefgreifender Strukturwandel bevor. Wissenschaftler*innen der TU Berlin wollen diesen Wandel begleiten und die Lausitz als internationale Logistikdrehscheibe und als Tourismusmagnet stärken.
Im Oktober 2025 stellte ein Konsortium um Prof. Dr.-Ing. Frank Straube vom TU-Institut für Technologie und Management, Fachgebiet Logistik, „DiSTILL“ vor, ein digitales Simulations-Tool, das auf frei verfügbaren Daten basiert. Es macht nicht nur die Logistikleistung der Region messbar, sondern ermöglicht vor allem die Planung und Kostenabschätzung neuer Großprojekte für Verwaltung und Investoren. Das nun abgeschlossene Projekt wurde mit 2,2 Millionen Euro vom Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr und der Investitionsinitiative mFUND gefördert. „DiSTILL“ steht für „Digitales Simulations-Tool zur Weiterentwicklung des Lausitzer Reviers zur Internationalen Logistikdrehscheibe Lausitz“.
Das Analyse-Tool „DiSTILL“ hilft Unternehmen, Verwaltung und Politik, Investitionen zu planen
„Die Region Lausitz liegt günstig an drei Ländern und an der Schnittstelle mehrerer europäischer Verkehrskorridore“, erklärt Frank Straube. „Bereits erfolgte Industrieansiedlungen haben zu wesentlichen Verkehrsströmen geführt. Und wir haben drei bedeutende Binnenhäfen dort wie Dresden, Riesa und Torgau, die hochtechnisiert für Waren-Umschläge sind und die den modernen Anforderungen der Zeit genügen.“
Ziel des Projekts war es, die aktuellen und zukünftigen logistischen Anforderungen an das Lausitzer Revier zu analysieren sowie eine Datenbank mit aktuellen und geplanten Logistikinfrastrukturprojekten aufzubauen, um Unternehmen, Verwaltungen und politischen Entscheidungsträgern ein Instrument an die Hand zu geben, Verkehrsströme zu analysieren, Emissionen und Logistikkosten zu vergleichen oder potenzielle Gewerbeflächen zu bewerten. „Denn“, so Straube, „die gesamte Logistik muss sich umstellen. Sie muss weg vom Schüttgut kommen, also von der Kohle, hin zu Stückgut, zu Konsumgütern, insbesondere zu nachhaltigen Produkten.“ Das Simulations-Tool „DiSTILL“ helfe, belastbare Wertschöpfungsnetzwerke voranzutreiben und unterstütze bestehende Unternehmen bei der Optimierung ihrer logistischen Prozesse. Es stellt Unternehmensansiedlungen, Straßen- und Schienennetze, Knotenpunkte und verkehrliche Anbindungsmöglichkeiten dar. „Damit ist es ein zentraler Hebel für die nachhaltige Strukturentwicklung, transparent und handhabbar.
Es bietet echte Entscheidungshilfen und macht Investitionen besser planbar“, so Straube. Während der Projektlaufzeit wurden Zwischenergebnisse kontinuierlich durch Vorträge oder Präsentationen einer breiten, auch überregionalen Öffentlichkeit zugänglich gemacht. „In unsere Datenbank, die kostenfrei nutzbare ‚Mobilithek‘, haben wir dafür aufbereitete und qualitätsgesicherte Datensätze eingestellt – eine wichtige Grundlage für weiterführende Analysen und Anwendungen.“ Fachveranstaltungen, Workshops und Netzwerktreffen richteten sich insbesondere an Zielgruppen aus Praxis, Verwaltung, Wissenschaft und Politik.
Denn der Wandel ist längst in vollem Gange. Als „Region mit Potenzial im Herzen Europas“ wirbt die Lausitz bereits mit einem leistungsfähigen Logistik-Verkehrsnetzwerk als Standortvorteil, zum Beispiel durch verkehrsträgerübergreifende Transportmöglichkeiten mit internationaler Anbindung. Das Logistik- und Eisenbahnverkehrsunternehmen BLG Railtec GmbH hat in Falkenberg in ein modernes Waggonservice- und Logistikzentrum investiert. Im Industriepark „Schwarze Pumpe“ sind inzwischen große Logistik-Unternehmen mit eigener Fahrzeugflotte, sogar für Gefahrgüter, ansässig. Auch BASF, bereits seit 100 Jahren am Standort Schwarzheide vertreten, stellt heute dort hunderttausende Kathoden für E-Autos her.
Das Projekt „FlexiDug“ soll die schnelle Umnutzung von Bahnstrecken ermöglichen
Eine rentable Logistik erfordert dabei die Nutzung verschiedener Verkehrsmittel. Für den multimodalen Umschlag, insbesondere zwischen Straße und Schiene, stellen große Unternehmen wie die Deutsche Bahn notwendige Anlagen zur Verfügung. Denn vor allem die Infrastruktur für das nachhaltigste Verkehrsmittel, die Bahn, befindet sich in der Lausitz in einem entscheidenden Wandlungsprozess: Wenn in den kommenden Jahren die Kraftwerke abgeschaltet sind und der Kohleabbau sein endgültiges Ende findet, wird die Bahn für die Braunkohleindustrie nicht mehr gebraucht. Sie transportierte bislang einen Großteil der Kohle zu den Kraftwerken. Mit der Frage, wie die Region die vorhandene Schieneninfrastruktur wirtschaftlich und nachhaltig weiterhin nutzen kann, haben sich Wissenschaftler*innen um Prof. Dr.-Ing. Birgit Milius, Leiterin des Fachgebiets Bahnbetrieb & Infrastruktur der TU Berlin mit weiteren Partnern beschäftigt.
„FlexiDug“ heißt das Infrastrukturprojekt (Flexible, digitale Systeme für den schienengebundenen Verkehr in Wachstumsregionen), das mit 2,5 Millionen Euro vom Bund gefördert wurde und dessen Abschlussbericht nun ebenfalls vorliegt. Es zeigt, wie Digitalisierung helfen kann, eine schnelle Umnutzung von Bahnstrecken zu ermöglichen, zum Beispiel auch für den Personenverkehr. Entwickelt haben die universitären Partner gemeinsam mit den Industriepartnern einen digitalen Zwilling, ein virtuelles Umgebungsmodell, das flexibel erweiterbar ist. Computerbasiert können hier Sensornetzwerke der digitalen Sicherungstechnik verknüpft werden oder in Echtzeit Daten ausgetauscht werden, um bahnbetriebliche Funktionalitäten zu unterstützen. „Wir haben uns unter anderem angeschaut, wo künftige Arbeitsplätze liegen und welche Strecken es gibt, die als Arbeitsweg in Frage kommen“, erläutert Birgit Milius. „Daraus hat sich ein Netz ergeben, das Stadt-, Regional- und Industrieentwicklung integriert und das virtuelle Umgebungsmodell bereichert.“ Das ist auch für den Tourismus wichtig, den die Lausitz mit ihren Naturdenkmälern weiter ausbauen will.
So profitiert die Region verkehrsübergreifend vom Wissenstransfer zwischen Forschung, Industrie und öffentlicher Verwaltung. Gerade zusammen mit der ansässigen Großindustrie können bereits jetzt auch Gefahrengüter international umgeschlagen und sicher transportiert werden, zum Beispiel zu den Häfen in Bremerhaven und Hamburg. In der Nähe von Cottbus entsteht darüber hinaus derzeit der Industrie- und Gewerbepark „Gral“ (Green Areal Lausitz) mit Schienenanschluss. Er soll komplett durch erneuerbare Energie wie Wind, Sonne und Wasserstoff versorgt werden und besonders dem grenzüberschreitenden Verkehr nach Polen zugutekommen. Dieser Knotenpunkt taucht ebenfalls sowohl in den DiSTILL-Daten als auch im Umgebungsmodell „FlexiDug“ auf. Ansiedlungswillige Unternehmen können so mögliche Investitionen verlässlich abschätzen.
Logistische Unterstützung für strukturschwache Regionen auch in Afrika
Und last but not least: Die Erforschung nachhaltiger Logistik für strukturschwache Regionen macht keineswegs an Europas Grenzen halt. Das TU-Fachgebiet Logistik von Professor Straube forscht ebenfalls an Logistiklösungen und nachhaltigen Lieferketten für die faire Industrialisierung von Schwellenländern des globalen Südens, insbesondere die wirtschaftliche Teilhabe von Afrika. Die Forscher*innen arbeiten bereits seit vielen Jahren zusammen mit afrikanischen Partnern. „Wir unterstützen die Zusammenarbeit von Politik, Wirtschaft und Wissenschaft gezielt, um neue Lieferketten, innovative logistische Lösungen und Mobilitätsangebote schneller zu entwickeln“, erklärt Straube den Hintergrund. „Damit können wir die industrielle Wertschöpfung der afrikanischen Hersteller beziehungsweise Zulieferer in der Automobil- und Verkehrstechnik sowie in der Lebensmittel- und Kleidungsindustrie nachhaltig unterstützen. Das ist auch für die Zukunft der europäischen Wirtschaft wichtig.“

title: „Ein Verbot aus dem Affekt trifft die Falschen und bremst Innovation“
content:
„Ein Verbot aus dem Affekt trifft die Falschen und bremst Innovation“
Heimliche Aufnahmen mit Smart Glasses sind ein reales Problem. Ein Verbot der Geräte wäre aus Sicht des Technologieforschers Prof. Dr. Philipp A. Rauschnabel von der Universität der Bundeswehr München dennoch der falsche Weg. Es würde eine Technologie blockieren, die Menschen im Alltag unterstützt, Inklusion fördern kann und sich zu einer neuen Computing-Plattform entwickeln könnte. „Der Nutzen dieser Geräte wird unterschätzt!“
Ein Verbot der Geräte wäre aus Sicht des Technologieforschers Prof. Dr. Philipp A. Rauschnabel von der Universität der Bundeswehr München dennoch der falsche Weg. Es würde eine Technologie blockieren, die Menschen im Alltag unterstützt, Inklusion fördern kann und sich zu einer neuen Computing-Plattform entwickeln könnte. „Der Nutzen dieser Geräte wird unterschätzt!“
Anlass der Debatte sind einige Influencer, die mit Smart Glasses ungefragt Menschen, überwiegend Frauen, gefilmt und die Aufnahmen ins Netz gestellt haben. „Menschen heimlich zu filmen und bloßzustellen, ist nicht akzeptabel, unabhängig davon, ob dafür eine Brille, ein Smartphone oder eine Knopfkamera verwendet wird“, sagt Rauschnabel. „Aber solange solche Videos Nutzerreaktionen erzeugen, belohnen die Plattformalgorithmen genau dieses Verhalten. Das Problem ist nicht die Brille, sondern eine Plattformlogik, die Missbrauch mit Aufmerksamkeit belohnt.“
NICHT DIE BAUFORM IST DAS PROBLEM
Der Hamburgische Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit hat die Debatte zuletzt mit der Frage befeuert, dass bestimmte Smart Glasses unter das Verbot getarnter Aufnahmegeräte nach § 8 TDDDG fallen könnten. Über ein solches Geräteverbot entscheidet allerdings nicht die Datenschutzbehörde, sondern die Bundesnetzagentur. Sie beschäftigt sich seit Jahren mit versteckten Aufnahmegeräten und prüft bei Smart Glasses vor allem, ob eine Aufnahme für Dritte erkennbar ist.
Entscheidend ist daher, ob die sichtbaren LED-Signale heutiger Brillen ausreichen. Rauschnabel verweist auf einen Lernprozess: So wie Menschen gelernt haben, ein hochgehaltenes Smartphone als Hinweis auf eine mögliche Aufnahme zu erkennen, werden sie auch lernen, auf die Signale von Smart Glasses zu achten. Das ersetzt technische Standards nicht, spricht aber für eindeutige, gut sichtbare Signale statt für ein grundsätzliches Verbot. Maßstab sollte dabei nicht der besonders misstrauische oder technisch versierte Beobachter sein, sondern ein durchschnittlich aufmerksamer Mensch.
Das größere Problem sieht Rauschnabel bei Geräten ohne solche Schutzmechanismen. Im internationalen Onlinehandel finden sich günstige Modelle aus Asien ohne sichtbare Aufnahmeindikatoren. Bei ihnen ist zudem unklar, wo und von wem Daten verarbeitet werden. Rauschnabel und sein Team haben solche Modelle untersucht: Datenschutzinformationen seien teils unvollständig oder nur auf Chinesisch verfügbar; zudem fehle ein greifbarer Verantwortlicher in der EU.
Darin sieht er ein regulatorisches Paradox: Große, in Europa erreichbare Hersteller lassen sich leichter kontrollieren als jene Anbieter, bei denen Schutzmechanismen fehlen und Regulierung besonders notwendig wäre. Wie schwierig die Durchsetzung ist, wenn ein Anbieter nicht greifbar ist, zeigt ein Fall aus Hamburg. Der dortigen Datenschutzaufsicht lag seit Juli 2020 eine Beschwerde gegen die biometrische Gesichtssuchmaschine PimEyes vor. Nach mehr als fünf Jahren entschied die Behörde, über ein Informationsschreiben hinaus keine konkreten Maßnahmen gegen das inzwischen in Dubai ansässige Unternehmen zu ergreifen. Die Datenschutzorganisation noyb hat dagegen Klage erhoben.
PHYSISCHE SHUTTER STATT VERBOTE
„Für konkrete Nutzungssituationen braucht es nicht zwingend neue Verbote. Viele Anwendungen sind bereits durch bestehende Regeln erfasst, etwa durch den AI Act oder die DSGVO. In Freibädern gelten längst Fotografierverbote. Es geht also nicht darum, neue Verbote zu schaffen, sondern bestehende Regeln auf ein neues Gerät anzuwenden. Dasselbe gilt für Unternehmen: Dort stellt sich vor allem die Frage, wann, wo und wie Beschäftigte eigene Smart Glasses im Betrieb nutzen dürfen.“
Rauschnabel plädiert deshalb seit mehr als zehn Jahren für physische Shutter: mechanische Abdeckungen, die sich über die Kamera und gegebenenfalls weitere Sensoren schieben lassen. Für Umstehende wäre damit unmittelbar erkennbar, dass eine abgedeckte Kamera nicht aufnehmen kann.
WAS AUF DEM SPIEL STEHT
Eine seit Jahren frei verfügbare Technologie wegen einzelner Missbrauchsfälle grundsätzlich infrage zu stellen, hält Rauschnabel für falsch. Manche Brillenträger nutzen Smart Glasses inzwischen als einzige Korrektionsbrille. Zugleich wächst der Markt für Anwendungen und Dienstleistungen, auch bei Start-ups und Technologieanbietern in Deutschland.
Schon heutige Smart Glasses zeigen, dass Kameras in Brillen weit mehr können als nur aufnehmen: Sie können blinden und sehbehinderten Menschen ihre Umgebung beschreiben oder Beschäftigte in Industrie und Wartung durch Arbeitsschritte führen. Trotzdem hält er heutige Devices für eine „Übergangstechnologie“. Künftige Augmented-Reality-Brillen mit eingebauten Displays bauen auf der heutigen Technologie auf: Sie müssen ihre Umgebung verstehen, um digitale Informationen passend in der realen Welt zu verankern. Damit sind heutige smarte Brillen eine Vorstufe dessen, was zur nächsten Computing-Plattform werden könnte.
„Wir sollten gefährliche Anwendungen begrenzen und sinnvolle ermöglichen. Computer, Internet und Smartphones sind massiv missbraucht worden – für Betrug, Stalking und heimliche Aufnahmen. Trotzdem würde heute wohl niemand behaupten, ein Verbot vor 30 Jahren wäre die richtige Antwort gewesen.“
Prof. Dr. Philipp A. Rauschnabel ist Professor an der Universität der Bundeswehr München und forscht an der Schnittstelle zwischen Behavioral Science, Technology Management und Regulierung. Er forscht seit über zehn Jahren zu Smart Glasses und Augmented Reality und ist von Clarivate als Highly Cited Researcher ausgezeichnet. Er gehört zu den führenden Forschern im Bereich Augmented Reality und Smart Glasses weltweit und hält zu diesen Themen regelmäßig Vorträge.

title: The Download: the next big thing in LLMs and how AI academic research is shifting

The Download: the next big thing in LLMs and how AI academic research is shifting
Plus: Nvidia has secured $500 billion from Wall Street for AI infrastructure.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
These startups are chasing the next big thing in LLMs
Nine years after Google researchers introduced the transformer, this family of neural networks has become the engine inside every major large language model. But transformers are starting to show their age.
As LLMs get bigger and better, transformers have become a bottleneck. Their dense attention mechanism becomes increasingly expensive as the amount of text grows, and they’re not great at keeping track of a lot of information at once.
Here are four new ideas for how to solve the transformer problem—innovations that could change LLMs for good, making them faster, far more efficient, and (maybe) even smarter.
—Will Douglas Heaven
This story is from MIT Technology Review’s What’s Next series, which looks across industries, trends, and technologies to give you a first look at the future. You can read the rest of them here.
AI professors are negotiating the new realities of academic research
—Grace Huckins
Last week, I headed to a hotel in Mountain View, California, to join some of the most accomplished, and some of the most promising, AI researchers in the world. I was hosting roundtable interviews and speaking at a media training for a convening of the Schmidt Sciences AI2050 program, an initiative funded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt that supports academics whose work involves AI.
The fellows list is a who’s who of AI luminaries, and though not all of them made it out to the Bay, every time I turned a corner I saw a scientist whom I’d interviewed previously or whose research I admired. It’s a weird time for university AI researchers, who make up most of the AI2050 group. Read Grace’s story to find out why, and what could be coming next.

One More Thing
The race to make the perfect baby is creating an ethical mess
A new field of science is using genetic sequencing to predict what kind of person an embryo might become. Some parents turn to these tests to avoid devastating genetic disorders, while a much smaller group are willing to pay tens of thousands of dollars to optimize for intelligence, appearance, and personality.
Customers, however, may not be getting what they’re paying for. Genetics experts have highlighted the potential deficiencies of this testing for years, while its underlying assumptions have made these companies a political lightning rod.
As this technology edges toward the mainstream, scientists and ethicists are racing to confront the implications—for our social contract, for future generations, and for our very understanding of what it means to be human. Read the full story.

title: NE时代
content:
首部L3、L4级自动驾驶强制国标发布 拟明年7月正式实施
8月5日消息，近日，工业和信息化部组织制定并归口的《智能网联汽车 自动驾驶系统安全要求》（GB 44721—2026）强制性国家标准由国家市场监督管理总局、国家标准化管理委员会批准发布，拟于2027年7月1日起正式实施。
《智能网联汽车 自动驾驶系统安全要求》适用于搭载L3级、L4级（高度自动驾驶）系统的M类和N类车辆，不适用于自动泊车系统。
据介绍，该标准立足我国产业发展与行业监管实际需求，兼顾技术可行性、产业适配性与落地实操性，构建了维度完整、要求清晰、适配国情的安全要求体系。
一是健全企业全生命周期安全保障机制，筑牢安全根基。标准要求车辆制造商从安全方针、风险管理、安全保证、安全提升四个维度，建立覆盖产品设计开发、生产制造及部署后全过程的保障能力，从源头降低自动驾驶系统潜在的安全风险。同时，明确车辆制造商应在自动驾驶系统研发验证过程中组织开展相应的仿真、场地及道路试验，并确保相关试验资源和条件满足研发验证要求。
二是强化系统动态驾驶任务执行能力，保障使用安全。标准要求自动驾驶系统安全水平应至少达到正在承担动态驾驶任务的合格且专注驾驶人的水平，同时不得对用户及其他道路使用者造成不合理安全风险。在此基础上，明确系统在各类场景下执行动态驾驶任务的安全要求，并明确最小风险策略的触发和执行要求。
三是规范人机交互与用户告知要求，防范误用滥用风险。标准要求自动驾驶系统的激活和退出过程应安全，并明确就绪、激活、退出等状态信息及信号的提示规范。对于L3级自动驾驶系统还应具备驾驶人接管能力监测功能。同时，要求车辆制造商除产品使用说明书外，还可通过官网、车载显示终端等渠道清晰告知用户驾驶自动化等级、能力范围、局限性、控制策略及用户角色转换等关键信息，引导用户正确认知与使用。
四是完善多维度检验检测方法，保障标准可落地实施。标准构建“企业保障能力检验+安全档案检验+确认性试验”多位一体的检验检测体系，对企业安全保障能力和产品安全档案的完整性和鲁棒性等进行检验。在此基础上，由第三方检测机构依据GB/T 41798《智能网联汽车 自动驾驶功能场地试验方法及要求》、GB/T 44719《智能网联汽车 自动驾驶功能道路试验方法及要求》和GB/T 47025《智能网联汽车 自动驾驶功能仿真试验方法及要求》推荐性国家标准，综合采用场地试验、道路试验、仿真试验等方法开展确认性试验，确保对自动驾驶系统实际能力进行全面检验检测。
据了解，我国牵头制定的联合国自动驾驶系统全球技术法规（ADS GTR）于2026年6月正式获批发布。与ADS GTR相比，我国标准对L3级、L4级自动驾驶系统提出更为细化的技术要求，进一步明确不同级别产品的安全边界，完善用户使用告知、操作培训等要求，创新性构建了统一的标准化试验场景体系，在保持核心技术要求与国际法规协调一致的同时，更贴合我国道路交通环境与行业管理实际需要，更具有落地实施的可行性。

【月度分析】2026年7月份全国乘用车市场分析

1.2026年7月全国乘用车市场回顾
零售：2026年7月全国乘用车市场零售146.1万辆，同比下降20.9%，环比下降8.8%；今年以来累计零售1,017.3万辆，同比下降20.3%。2026年7月国内乘用车市场呈现“总量持续承压、环比走弱、结构极致分化”的运行态势，淡季下行特征凸显，行业结构性调整进一步深化。
2026年7月车市走弱，是油价反弹、宏观走弱、季节性淡季、前期需求透支及政策切换等多重因素共振所致。地缘冲突引发霍尔木兹海峡通航扰动，推动国际油价震荡上行，2026年国内汽油价格累计上调1,575元/吨，大幅抬高用车成本，燃油乘用车消费需求剧烈萎缩，但对商用车的影响很小。同时7月CPI、PPI环比回落、PMI景气下行，居民收入与消费预期偏谨慎，大额耐用品消费意愿低迷，住行消费持续走弱，拖累车市终端需求。叠加7月高温淡季压制线下到店客流、6月半年冲量提前透支市场需求，终端订单与客流同步回落。此外，新能源安全新国标正式落地，行业技术门槛抬升，低端车型短期出清扰动市场。而7月政治局会议明确财政加力、加码扩内需促消费政策，为车市提供底部支撑，本轮市场下行属于阶段性结构性波动，并非行业趋势性恶化。
综合来看，2026年7月乘用车市场呈现五大鲜明特征：一、总量持续承压，结构性分化极致放大，“燃油深度降温、新能源强势领跑”成为市场核心主线，油价波动主导了“油电替代”节奏；二、燃油车全线收缩，其中纯燃油车型近乎失速，混动车型相对抗跌，导致燃油车内部结构持续优化；三、新能源渗透率持续突破新高，供给端新国标合规产品集中迭代上市，行业从价格内卷全面转向价值竞争；四、出口持续发挥托底作用，有效稳住车企批发与产能，缓解国内零售疲软压力；五、行业库存持续良性去化，厂商、渠道库存降幅同步扩大，整体库存风险充分释放，行业经营压力稳步缓解、整体韧性有所修复。

2.2026年8月份全国乘用车市场展望
2026年8月乘用车市场整体呈现“总量弱修复、结构强分化”的运行态势，21个产销工作日叠加高温淡季，终端市场回暖节奏平缓，多重宏观与行业因素交织塑造了市场格局。受霍尔木兹海峡通航受阻影响，7月国际油价震荡上行，国内成品油价格两轮累计上调近985元/吨，大幅抬升燃油车用车、养车成本，持续压制用户燃油车购买意愿，传统燃油车需求持续走弱，也成为新能源车逆势走强的核心外部利好，持续拓宽新能源车型的国内和海外市场增长空间。
最新宏观数据显示国内消费与制造业景气偏弱，直接约束车市复苏力度。7月CPI同比上涨0.5%、环比微降0.1%，反映终端内需动力不足；PPI同比上涨3.5%、环比下降0.7%，上游成本边际缓解但传导滞后；PMI回落至49.2%，制造业景气度下行，叠加居民消费信心谨慎，汽车大额消费观望情绪浓厚，导致车市整体增长乏力。政策端形成强力对冲支撑，7月中央政治局会议明确：充分发挥各项存量政策效能，及时谋划出台务实管用的增量政策，加大逆周期调节力度，加力扩大内需、优化供给。随着消费品以旧换新配套政策持续优化加力，汽车消费扶持预期持续升温，将有效推动三季度车市从底部逐步复苏。
供给侧门槛持续提升，新能源车大型化趋势明显。2026年1-7月的新能源车新车中，5米以上新车达到49款，占新能源新车总数量的56%（2024年38%、2025年36%），而4米以下车型仅有1款占比1%，而去年同期5款占比6%。经济型车供给剧烈减少。
整体来看，8月车市处于底部蓄力修复阶段，随着各项稳消费政策逐步落地，叠加基数逐步改善，乘用车市场降幅将稳步收窄，行业正式进入“价值驱动、结构优化”的成熟发展阶段，为传统“金九银十”行情铺路蓄力。
3.2026年1-6月汽车行业利润率3.8%
今年上半年，面对国际环境复杂演变和国内转型压力不减等多重挑战，国民经济仍开局良好、质效提升，装备制造业和高技术制造业利润快速增长，原材料制造业利润两位数增长。近期随着车市生产规模扩大，PPI上行，上游有色和石油等矿业利润暴涨，钛酸锂价格近20万，2026年1-6月锂电池出口每吨单价10.48万元下降12%（2024年下降26%、2025年下降21%），而国内电池价格仍然坚挺，且锂电上市公司应付账期200天而应收账期要求60天。
2026年1-6月汽车生产1,510万辆，同比下降4%。2026年1-6月的汽车行业收入51,893亿元，同比增长1.8%；成本46,100亿元，增长2.8%；利润1,954亿元，同比下降20%。历年6月汽车业一般利润率都是较高的，今年6月达5.2%，已经好于3-4月3.7%的月度表现，但2026年1-6月汽车行业销售利润率仍只有3.8%，相对于上下游工业企业利润率6.5%的平均水平，汽车行业仍属偏低的。
2026年各地大力度推动“两新”政策落地实施，逐步有效释放内需活力。但汽车行业效益的改善明显落后于其它消费品。汽车行业利润受上游挤压，采购成本维持高位，叠加油价暴涨，有色金属、半导体利润暴增，终端用户购车观望心态严重价格内卷，导致车企运行压力持续加大，高质量发展受到来自上下游行业的巨大冲击。
4.2026年6月中国汽车实现出口107万辆，同比增73%
2026年1-6月中国汽车实现出口531万辆，同比增速53%，6月中国汽车实现出口107万辆，同比增长73%，环比增长8%，同比走势总体较强, 环比走势超预期正增长。今年增长的主要动力仍是高油价和中国产品竞争力提升以及全球南方国家市场的持续增长。
2026年6月中国汽车出口总量的前10国家：俄罗斯84,451辆、英国62,487辆、澳大利亚60,510辆、比利时59,606辆、菲律宾462,43辆、墨西哥45,528辆、阿尔及利亚33,358辆、泰国29,923辆、马来西亚26,767辆和巴西25,856辆，其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：俄罗斯58,053辆、澳大利亚41,065辆、比利时35,070辆、英国33,913辆和菲律宾21,358辆。俄罗斯市场中国车企防风险意识提升，2025年出口去库存力度很大。2026年1-6月我们对俄罗斯的出口恢复较大。
2026年1-6月累计整车出口总量的前10国家：俄罗斯448,157辆、巴西410,825辆、英国255,260辆、澳大利亚237,823辆、比利时219,730辆、墨西哥210,155辆、意大利154,870辆、菲律宾148,727辆、阿联酋146,274辆和阿尔及利亚143,012辆，其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：俄罗斯267,411辆、巴西249,571辆、英国118,848辆、阿尔及利亚100,382辆和澳大利亚94,368辆。
2026年6月中国新能源汽车出口46.3万辆，同比增长59%，1-6月累计出口242万辆，增长70%的表现很好，6月新能源车出口环比表现较强。2026年6月中国汽车出口中纯电动占比30%（同比0%），插混占比19%（同比+8%），混动占比7%（同比+1%），纯燃油车占比35%（同比-8%）。
2026年6月中国新能源汽车出口总量的前10国家：比利时57,217辆、英国50,157辆、澳大利亚46,434辆、菲律宾43,466辆、泰国28,978辆、德国17,900辆、西班牙14,974辆、韩国13,764辆、马来西亚12,399辆和巴西11,089辆，其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：澳大利亚34,736辆、比利时33,277辆、英国31,305辆、菲律宾24,927辆和泰国20,980辆。
2026年1-6月中国新能源汽车出口总量的前10国家：巴西299,803辆、比利时209,217辆、英国181,260辆、澳大利亚167,126辆、泰国126,646辆、菲律宾126,062辆、德国84,190辆、意大利79,503辆、韩国75,430辆和西班牙72,723辆，其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：巴西183,399辆、澳大利亚98,744辆、英国89,216辆、泰国66,297辆和比利时63,953辆。
中国新能源车2026年1-6月出口表现好于预期，主要是插混和混动替代纯电动成为出口增长的新增长点，尤其是纯电动货车出口表现较强，成为商用车新能源车出口亮点。运力恢复促进6月出口暴增。中国新能源车出口主要是出口西欧和中南美市场。中东市场受阻。
5.2026年6月中国汽车进口3.8万辆
2026年6月进口车进口3.8万辆，同比下滑11%，但由于2025年6月基数低，虽然美国与伊朗战争导致运输受阻，进口车总体下降较小。2026年1-6月进口汽车20万辆，同比下降11%。2026年1-6月仍是近期少见的较好表现，主要原因是因为2025年的低基数。由于2025年初低基数的促进，今年1-6月进口车零售19万辆，下滑29%的表现不算太差，6月下降到3万辆，下降了39%，下半年压力仍大。
进口车以传统燃油车为主格局。2026年6月进口量最高的前10国家是：日本18,486辆、德国9,272辆、斯洛伐克4,122辆、美国3,359辆、英国1,426辆、墨西哥654辆、奥地利555辆、韩国128辆、南非71辆和波兰70辆。其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：日本5,131辆、德国928辆、奥地利303辆、墨西哥290辆和南非65辆。
2026年1-6月进口量最高的前10国家是：日本103,493辆、德国44,311辆、美国17,732辆、斯洛伐克13,520辆、英国10,855辆、墨西哥2,981辆、奥地利2,521辆、泰国1,733辆、瑞典604辆和韩国486辆。其中本期较同期增量增长的前五是：日本20,095辆、泰国1,515辆、奥地利960辆、墨西哥735辆和南非319辆。
在进口车近几年持续下滑的背景下，今年的豪华市场走势分化，雷克萨斯销量相对较稳，保持进口豪华车的第一位置。部分超豪华品牌波动异常，出现崩盘迹象，行业运行压力较大。
国产与进口豪华车市场的需求总体偏弱，其中上海、北京、苏州、杭州、成都、无锡等地区的豪华车市场压力较大。今年的喀什、伊犁、大庆、阿克苏等中西部地区需求较强。
6.2026年1-6月中国占世界汽车份额31%
根据世界汽车组织统计数据，全球汽车生产不断增长，2025年达到9,638万辆，较2024年的9,272万辆增长4%，中国占世界生产份额36%。根据我们统计2025年全球汽车销量9,689万辆，同比增长6%。2026年6月的世界汽车销量达到860万辆，同比增长6%。2026年1-6月世界汽车销量达到4,786万辆，同比增长3%。
随着美国、中国车市的年初相对负增长，2026年1-6月世界车市销量增长不强。2025年中国达到世界汽车35.4%的份额；2026年初中国份额31.4%，2026年初中国汽车销量下滑较大，由于今年政策补贴促进中国商用车走强落地，6月份额回升到32.2%。年初较低是入门级销量萎缩因素的异常体现，乘用车弱、商用车强，出口暴增。期待能有改善低端收入和减少抑制低端消费的政策出台。随着政策刺激效果逐步恢复显现，预计未来中国车市逐步走强。
2026年1-6月的全球汽车销量增长3%，其中中国汽车销量下降4%，美国销量下降3%，印度汽车市场销量增长19%，泰国汽车市场增长18%，俄罗斯市场销量增长10%，越南增长31%。新兴市场拉动市场表现较好。
东升西降，电动化发展的趋势也导致部分国际车企逐步走弱，除了丰田、现代起亚、铃木和塔塔等，其它国际品牌份额2026年出现较大幅度的下滑。吉利、比亚迪、奇瑞、上汽、长安等自主表现较强，中国自主品牌将全面提升世界份额。
7.2026年1-6月中国占世界新能源车份额62%
2026年1-6月世界新能源乘用车达到1,122万辆，同比增长13%，其中6月新能源车销量238万辆增长25%，增速回到历史正常水平。2026年1-6月的新能源车占世界汽车份额达到25.5%，其中纯电动车的占比达到16.3%，插电混动达到7.1%的汽车比例，混合动力达到8%，表现优秀。
中国之外市场的新能源走势总体增长迥异。由于欧洲新能源走势大幅回暖，因此海外新能源车1-6月销量427万辆、增速达到28%，接近于前两年平均水平。
初步统计欧洲新能源乘用车6月47万辆，同比增长23%，2026年1-6月累计234万辆，同比增长31%。由于高关税和新能源补贴取消的涨价因素的影响，美国新能源车2026年6月销量10.8万辆，同比下降20%，1-6月美国新能源车销量61万，下降27%。
世界新能源车渗透率总体呈现快速提升趋势，2022年已经达到13.1%水平，2023年达到15.9%，2024年达到19.5%，2025年渗透率达到23.6%。2026年累计新能源渗透率23.4%，其中，德国达到32%，挪威达到81%，英国35%，而美国仅有7%，日本仅有3%，因此世界新能源发展的不均衡性极为明显。
2025年中国新能源乘用车世界份额68.3%；2026年1-6月中国新能源乘用车世界份额达到62%的水平。2026年中国在世界纯电动车市场份额58%，2026年中国在世界插电混动份额达到71%的高水平，中国在世界插电混动市场呈现超强的表现。
2025年自主新能源乘用车海外市场销量份额达到15.8%，提升较大。2026年自主新能源乘用车海外市场销量份额大幅提升，6月达到26%，进一步大幅跃升。

TI 推出 MSPM33C321x 微控制器，助力车载智能与硬件安全双重升级
M33C321x 系列微控制器（MCU）结合 Arm® Cortex®-M33 内核，支持 ASIL-B 认证，配备丰富外设，为车身电子、汽车照明、仪表中控、电池管理等提供跨场景解决方案
M33C321x MCU TrustZone® 构建硬件隔离，赋能后量子加密（PQC）升级，为 AI 数据中心和工业支付终端构筑长期安全防线。
MSPM33C321A 是一款主频 160MHz 的微控制器，搭载 Arm® Cortex®-M33 处理器，存储器保护单元（MPU）、数字信号处理扩展指令集（DSP）与浮点运算单元（FPU）。该器件最高配备 1MB 双分区闪存、256KB 静态随机存储器（SRAM），两类存储均支持 ECC 校验，可满足设备现场升级需求，保障长期稳定运行。
M33 内核：车载智能的边缘节点
车身电子 – 针对车门、座椅、车窗上的多电机控制，M33C321x MCU 集成双路 12 位 9.4Msps 高速 ADC，高速比较器，多种定时器，提供丰富的 PWM 资源，驱动多个直流有刷和无刷电机，同时精准采集电流和位置信号，实现高效的闭环控制。双路 CAN-FD 接口高速联动车身域控，实现手指防夹、一键升降、记忆调节多种功能。
汽车照明 – 为了满足前大灯 LED 自适应调光、交互式尾灯、以及车内动态氛围灯，M33C321x MCU 提供多种通信接口，包括双路 CAN-FD，带 1KB 专用 SRAM，确保 CAN 通信稳定不丢帧。多路可配置 LIN/UART/SPI/I2C 资源，在系统层面还开发了对 T1S 以太网、对 OSP 等不同通信接口的桥接方案。
仪表中控 – 对于车机导航和车况数据高速处理，M33C321x MCU 集成 1MB Flash + 256KB SRAM，带 ECC 数据纠错，支持 AB 备份，同时配备 QSPI 接口快速加载小型 UI 图形信息。对于车机屏幕的旋转控制，TI 开发了步进电机闭环 FOC 的控制方案，降低了开环控制下的噪音和抖动问题。此外，在车载无线充电的应用上，TI 与合作伙伴开发了全套系统方案，支持包括 QI2.2 等全面的充电协议，助力快速开发。
MSPM33C321 属于可灵活扩展的 MSP 系列产品矩阵，软硬件均与 MSPM0 共用引脚兼容封装，并共享统一软件开发环境，用户能够最大化复用现有软件研发成果，可在整个 MSP 产品家族内灵活升级、降级，按需调整芯片运算性能与外设集成度。选用 MSPM33C321A 开展设计，工程师获得的不只是一款优质微控制器，更是覆盖众多项目、多达上百款器件的选型方案，能够支撑多样化产品开发。
TrustZone：AI 终端的安全屏障
系统级增强安全能力以 TrustZone® 技术为基础，借助此功能，开发人员能够将外设与存储区域划分为安全域与非安全域，阻止未授权主体访问指定存储分区。MSPM33C321A 还集成全局安全控制器（GSC）。这是德州仪器 MSP 系列微控制器产品独有的外设，在 TrustZone® 架构之上额外构建一层安全防护。GSC 可为外设、闪存以及 SRAM 配置安全属性与访问权限等级。开发人员可依托这一独立 IP，防范非安全域外设非法访问内存安全区域，实现全部核心资源统一防护。
第二层增强安全能力依托内置在 ROM 中的信任根（i-RoT）实现，支持安全启动与密钥配置。i-RoT 提供一套完整可信的设备身份校验机制，从生产阶段开始持续保护应用固件，防止固件遭到恶意篡改。这套硬件实现的 i-RoT 保护，满足物联网平台安全评估标准 SESIP-2 级以及 PSA-2 级安全认证要求。
最后，MSPM33C321A 内置硬件密码加速器，包含 256 位高级加密标准（AES-256）、256 位安全哈希算法（SHA-256）以及公钥加速模块（PKA），可分担椭圆曲线密码（ECC）、RSA 非对称加密等算力密集型公钥运算。上述功能能够应对大量传统安全风险。与此同时，开发人员借助 MSPM33 SDK，可以逐步部署后量子密码（PQC）算法，以应对未来新型安全威胁，使方案符合商用国家安全算法 CNSA 2.0 规范。MSPM33C321A 融合完善的硬件与软件防护方案，为工程师提供全套工具，全方位保护应用系统免受各类安全威胁。
