title: China's Tianneng warns of profit fall as lead battery material costs rise – Batteries International
content: Tianneng Power International has warned of a potential half-year profit fall of up to 66% as high raw material costs hit its mainstay lead acid battery business — but said long-term prospects are strong. The China-based lead battery major, part of the Tianneng Group, issued the profit warning on August 7, saying revenue for the six months ended last June is expected to be down by 5%-8% compared to the year ago period. Upstream raw material prices such as for sulfuric acid, which remain at relatively high levels, are to blame — along with intensified competition in downstream industries, Tianneng said in its Hong Kong stock exchange filing. Another contributory factor was the additional VAT deduction applicable to advanced manufacturing companies in mainland China. However, Tianneng said lead acid battery sales remained generally stable, thanks to the firm’s leading market position and solid customer base. Meanwhile, its Li ion battery business, synergies in battery recycling operations and expansion into overseas markets is proceeding steadily. Interim first-half results are expected to be published toward the end of this month. International expansion In terms of expansion, Tianneng has revealed it commissioned a manufacturing base in Indonesia last June. The company plans to establish a “full-lifecycle lead battery industry chain” in the country and expand into lithium motive power, energy storage systems, start-stop and industrial power batteries. Separately, Tianneng said it had signed a cooperation agreement with US lead and lithium giant Clarios last May, focusing on the raw material supply chain, waste battery recycling, and full lifecycle management. Tianneng said in 2018 was considering setting up a factory in another, unspecified Asian country, to produce 100,000 tonnes of lead batteries a year. Batteries International discussed pressures on the global battery supply chain amid geoopolitical upheaval earlier this year with lead market veteran, Farid Ahmed. title: GM Battery Strategy Shift: Samsung Exit, Ultium Restart
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Battery Manufacturing
The automaker's diverging battery partnerships reflect broader industry restructuring as Ford and Stellantis also recalibrate US battery manufacturing strategies.
August 13, 2026
5 Min Read
General Motors corporate logo shines from the Hudson's Detroit building Friday, October 10, 2025 after being affixed overnight to the company's future global headquarters in downtown Detroit, Michigan.
John F. Martin / General Motors
At a Glance
Samsung SDI acquires GM's stake in Indiana battery JV; facility to focus on energy storage systems instead of EV batteries
GM-LG Energy Solution's Ohio Ultium plant resumes production after 7-month shutdown, bringing back 1,400 workers
Ford and Stellantis also restructuring battery partnerships, reflecting industry-wide recalibration amid softer EV demand
General Motors is reshaping its North American battery manufacturing footprint through a pair of significant moves that signal both retreat and renewal in the automaker's electrification plans. The company has ended one joint venture while reviving another, reflecting broader industry adjustments to slower-than-expected electric vehicle demand and growing opportunities in stationary energy storage.
Samsung SDI takes full control of Indiana facility
On August 11, Samsung SDI announced
it had acquired GM's 49.99% stake in SynergyCells
, their $3.5 billion joint venture battery plant under construction in New Carlisle, IN. The ownership change effectively ends GM's participation in the project, which was originally announced in 2024 with plans to produce 27 gigawatt-hours of EV batteries annually.
"While reflecting recent market changes, this acquisition decision is to continue the strategic partnership with GM," a Samsung SDI official stated in the announcement. "We will continue our commitment to an electrified future with the partner, while utilizing the plant to proactively respond to the fast-growing ESS market in the U.S."
Related:
Ford Unveils Fathom Electric Pickup at $29,945 With Frunk & Bi-Directional Charging Capability
Samsung SDI President & CEO Yoon-ho Choi flanked by GM executives at the JV signing event in 2024. Credit: Samsung SDI
The decision reflects pressure on global automakers and battery makers to scale back or adjust investment plans, particularly following
the Trump administration's elimination of EV incentives
. The loss of the federal $7,500 consumer tax credit in September 2025 has weighed heavily on EV demand across the industry.
Despite the joint venture dissolution, Samsung SDI and GM signed a new agreement to jointly develop next-generation prismatic battery cells featuring high energy density and fast charging capability for potential future EV applications. Samsung SDI plans to initially use the Indiana facility for energy storage system battery production before potentially incorporating the co-developed prismatic cells.
Ohio Ultium Cells plant returns to operation
In contrast to the Indiana development, GM's partnership with LG Energy Solution is experiencing a revival. The Ultium Cells joint venture plant in Warren, OH
resumed battery cell production on August 18
after a seven-month shutdown, according to The Korea Herald.
The restart brings approximately 1,400 workers back to the facility, including most of the roughly 850 employees who were temporarily laid off when production halted in January 2026. The Ohio plant, Ultium Cells' first manufacturing facility, has an annual production capacity of approximately 35 gigawatt-hours and produces battery cells for GM electric vehicles.
Related:
Hyundai Ioniq 9 AWD Performance Calligraphy Delivers Strong Range & Fast Charging Capability
Tom Gallagher, Ultium Cells' vice president of operations,
confirmed the restart
to Reuters, as reported by CBT News. The resumption is expected to lift LG Energy Solution's overall plant utilization rate from 52.8% in the first half of 2026 to above 60% in the second half, according to The Korea Herald.
Tennessee facility pivots toward energy storage
While Ohio returns to EV battery production, GM and LG Energy Solution's second Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee is undergoing a strategic transformation. According to Electrive, the partners are investing $70 million to retrofit production lines at the Tennessee facility to manufacture
lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for stationary energy storage systems
The Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, TN. Credit: GM
However, Ultium Cells characterizes this as a diversification rather than a complete pivot, with plans to produce cells for both stationary storage systems and electric vehicles at the site. This dual-purpose approach reflects LG Energy Solution's broader strategy to offset weaker EV demand by expanding its energy storage business. The company aims to increase its global production capacity for energy storage systems to over 60 gigawatt-hours by 2026, with more than 80% of this capacity located in North America.
Related:
Electric Aviation Progress with Hybrid and Fully Electric Systems
Broader industry restructuring of battery partnerships
GM's battery partnership recalibration reflects a wider pattern of restructuring across the US automotive industry. Ford Motor Company
dissolved its BlueOval SK battery joint venture with SK On
in December 2025, with the split completed in early 2026.. Ford took full ownership of two battery plants in Kentucky through a wholly owned subsidiary, while SK On assumed full control of the Tennessee plant at BlueOval City. The Kentucky plant
workforce faced layoffs beginning in February 2026
, with plans to rehire 2,100 employees in 2027 after retooling for energy storage system production, The Detroit News reported.
BlueOval SK battery plant in Kentucky. Credit: BlueOval SK
The dissolution was driven by diverging chemistry strategies
and Ford's pivot toward energy storage
). Ford is separately building a $3 billion wholly-owned LFP battery plant in Michigan using CATL technology through a licensing arrangement rather than a joint venture. The facility
began pilot production in mid-2026
, CBT News reported, and expects to produce launch-ready battery cells before the end of 2026, with an annual capacity of 35 gigawatt-hours—enough for 400,000 vehicles. This makes Ford the first automaker to produce LFP batteries in the US for mainstream EVs.
Stellantis has also been reconsidering its battery manufacturing strategy. Electrive reported in February 2026 that the company was exploring options
to exit its StarPlus Energy joint venture with Samsung SDI
, which is building two battery plants in Kokomo, IN. The first plant, with 33 gigawatt-hours of capacity, was expected to launch in the first quarter of 2025, while the second plant with 34 gigawatt-hours of capacity was
targeted to start production in 2027
, according to Samsung SDI.
Industry implications
The restructuring of battery joint ventures across GM, Ford, and Stellantis illustrates the complex calculus facing automakers and battery manufacturers in the current market environment. These partnerships, conceived during the EV boom of the early 2020s, are being reconfigured to accommodate market realities including reduced consumer demand and shifting chemistry preferences.
The pivot toward energy storage systems by Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution reflects the rapid growth of the stationary storage market in the United States, driven by grid modernization needs and renewable energy integration. This diversification strategy allows battery manufacturers to leverage their North American production capacity across multiple applications rather than relying solely on automotive demand.
For the battery industry, these moves underscore the importance of manufacturing flexibility and the value of facilities capable of producing cells for multiple end markets and chemistries. As automakers continue to adjust their electrification timelines and production volumes, battery manufacturers are positioning themselves to serve both transportation and stationary storage applications from their US manufacturing bases, while also adapting to the industry's growing interest in LFP chemistry for cost-sensitive applications.

Mike is also a member of

title: Data Centers Face Critical Mineral Supply Chain Strain
content:
Critical minerals such as copper, lithium, cobalt, and rare earth elements form the literal wiring of the AI age, used in everything from energy storage to cooling systems and power supply. Yet the surging demand for the materials is pushing up against a supply chain gap that some warn could be difficult to bridge.
Declining ore grades, geopolitical tensions, and limited refining capacity are heightening uncertainty around critical mineral supplies, even as AI infrastructure investment accelerates worldwide.
Copper is particularly at risk, facing a
projected shortfall
of 10 million metric tons by 2040 if “meaningful expansion” of the sector is not seen.
Brendan Smith, co-founder and CEO of SiTration, an MIT spinout that recovers copper from mining waste, told
Data Center Knowledge
that data centers have become one of the more "visible sources” of rising copper demand.
“It takes about 50,000 tons of copper to build a new hyperscale data center, and we’re talking about installing many of these in the coming years,” he said.
Related:
Beyond Lithium: How Organic Flow Batteries Could Transform Data Center Energy Storage
While data centers still account for a relatively modest share of global copper consumption, Shashank Sriram, Senior Research Analyst at Wood Mackenzie, said their buying power is reshaping the market.
“Unlike traditional utilities, automotive OEMs, or construction firms operating on thin margins, hyperscalers generate revenues that allow them to absorb virtually any metal price spike,” he said. “AI isn’t creating the physical deficit on its own, but its bottomless willingness to pay is pricing everyone else out of a structurally disrupted market.”
Copper, the backbone of data center infrastructure, faces growing supply challenges as demand for this essential conductor skyrockets in the tech industry. (Getty Images)
Critical Minerals Powering Data Centers
Data centers rely on several critical minerals to operate efficiently. Copper is used for power distribution, playing a key role in busbars and switchgear that deliver electricity to every rack.
underpins battery storage, while cobalt and rare earth elements show up in specialized electronics, magnets, and precision components.
Of these four distinct categories, copper is the one under the
greatest near-term supply strain
, as its demand extends far beyond the data center industry and is essential for grid infrastructure, electrification, defense, and batteries.
Lithium, Brendan notes, faces its own supply-demand gap, albeit for different reasons.
“While also growing rapidly, the value of the global lithium market today is about 10 times smaller than copper,” he said. “With lithium, we have a lot of reserves globally that are known and accessible. Copper’s problem is more structural. We’re seeing a rapid decline in supply due to a fundamental reduction in copper ore grade, which you can’t really overcome. There’s no way to magically reverse that.”
Related:
The Carolinas May Hold a Critical Resource for AI Data Centers
For an industry planning hundreds of new AI facilities over the coming decade, those pressures are beginning to shift attention from simply buying materials to securing long-term access to them.
A Supply Chain Under Threat
According to Brendan, building a new greenfield copper mine in the US takes an average of 23 years from discovery to production, with permitting alone consuming roughly half that timeline. Refining capacity also remains heavily concentrated overseas, leaving manufacturers exposed to geopolitical tensions and shifting trade policies.
“Only about 3% of copper that’s consumed globally is fully refined in the US today,” Brendan said. “We’re exporting a lot of raw copper ore concentrate to other countries to be refined and produced there.”
Recently proposed copper tariffs have added another layer of volatility. In June, the White House
adjusted its tariff regime
to include a 15% transitional rate for metal-intensive industrial equipment and electrical grid equipment. While refined copper was temporarily exempted, tariffs are scheduled to be phased in starting in 2027.
Related:
Could Algae Be the Key to Data Center Sustainability?
Sriram said businesses trying to get ahead of the tariffs coming into effect have “sucked vast tonnages of copper into US warehouses,” trapping nearly 2% of total global copper demand.
“A massive amount of physical inventory has effectively been locked out of the global market,” he said. “Simultaneously, regulatory crackdowns on scrap trading mechanics (such as stricter enforcement on reverse invoicing) have choked off secondary feeds, forcing fabricators onto the spot market for refined cathode.”
In this climate, Greg Smith, CEO of copper manufacturer Pantheon Electric, said supply chain resilience has become just as important as manufacturing capability.
“More than 50% of the US’ copper needs come from imports,” he told
Data Center Knowledge
. “From our perspective, the supplier with the best, most resilient and reliable supply chain wins.”
Copper as a Case Study
Pantheon announced in July that it had unified 21 plants across North America and Europe into a single platform, becoming, by its own account, the largest independent US maker of copper conductors and busbars. The group processes over a million pounds of copper a day for customers, including Schneider Electric, Eaton, and Prysmian Group.
While copper is only one component of a modern data center, it is among the hardest to replace. Busbars, conductors, and electrical distribution equipment form the backbone of every facility, meaning supply disruptions can delay entire construction projects.
“It’s a national security issue that must be dealt with, whether it’s friendshoring or other ways to get access to these critical minerals,” Greg said. “Even a relatively small component like a busbar can hold up delivery of a multi-million-dollar system.”
For the group, arming itself against geopolitical volatility has meant building local relationships with suppliers, recyclers, and traders in both the US and Europe.
Innovation is also creating opportunities to expand supply.
Rather than competing for newly mined ore, SiTration is recovering copper directly from mining wastewater using an electro-extraction process that produces commercial-grade copper cathode without conventional smelting or refining.
“The approach is about creating new supply outright, rather than competing for existing supply,” Brendan said.
He estimates that roughly $3.5 trillion in critical minerals remains stranded in mining waste streams worldwide, including around $500 billion in copper.
In June, the company
completed a trial with BHP
to recover both copper and gold from waste streams in South Australia, and has also worked with Rio Tinto in the US, with further deployments in Chile in the pipeline.
Both companies point to the same underlying strategy, even if their approaches differ: diversifying supply chains to protect future copper supply.
Neither company frames this as a permanent fix to the underlying scarcity, but together they illustrate how the industry is starting to respond to the potential fallout from a supply shortage.
Future-Proofing Data Center Buildout
According to Sriram, the immediate priority for data center developers and manufacturers is securing reliable access to materials already in circulation.
“Large buyers are increasingly signing long-term offtake agreements, pre-purchasing material, and locking in supply with fabricators and refiners several years ahead of need,” he said. “This doesn't create new supply, but it does reduce exposure to shortages and price spikes.”
Over the medium term, he said
recycling
is expected to play a growing role. Recycling copper and other critical minerals from waste streams or retired equipment could boost domestic supply faster than developing new mines, although scaling high-purity recycled material will require continued investment in processing infrastructure.
Diversifying supply chains is another priority, with countries such as Canada, Australia, and Chile highlighted as potentially important partners.
“In terms of what moves the needle today: long-term supply agreements, inventory strategies and selective substitution,” Sriram said. “Recycling and friendshoring can improve resilience over the medium term. Domestic refining is the most durable solution, but it remains a longer-term strategic bet.”
As hyperscalers invest billions in the next generation of AI campuses, critical minerals are becoming another pillar of data center strategy, joining power availability, cooling capacity, and network connectivity as essential considerations for future growth.

title: Zayo, Nvidia Target Fiber Capacity as AI Infrastructure Spreads
content:
Zayo is building more than 8,000 miles of long-haul fiber across emerging AI corridors with anchor customer Nvidia as demand for dedicated connectivity grows.
The Denver-based digital infrastructure provider says it will build six new long-haul routes and expand capacity across 10 high-demand markets. The broader program now spans more than 15,000 route miles across North America, according to Zayo.
The buildout adds networking to the
infrastructure required
to support AI, alongside power, data center capacity and computing hardware.
Analysts differ on how quickly network constraints are developing.
Jimmy Yu, vice president at Dell’Oro Group, said he has not heard of wide-area network bottlenecks caused by AI traffic. The industry remains in the early stages of the AI infrastructure cycle, he said.
Ron Westfall, vice president and practice lead for networking and infrastructure at HyperFrame Research, said existing routes are already running into capacity limits as AI factories move into new markets to access available power.
Related:
Why IPv6 Is the Non-Negotiable Foundation for AI-Agentic Systems
Existing fiber routes were designed around legacy data center topologies, Westfall said. As AI factories spread geographically,
wide-area optical capacity
is becoming a rate-limiting dependency for distributed computing clusters.
The longer-term requirement is massive data center interconnect capacity between AI facilities.
Yu said purpose-built routes with low latency and thousands of fiber pairs could become critical to connecting AI data centers, other facilities and exchange points.
“Providers are building ahead of anticipated demand,” Yu said.
Network Becomes Part of AI Infrastructure
Zayo said its new routes will connect emerging AI corridors where existing long-haul capacity is limited or does not yet exist. It also plans to expand capacity on existing routes where it expects demand to increase.
“AI is fundamentally reshaping where and how network infrastructure needs to be built across the U.S.,” Zayo CEO Steve Smith said in a statement.
The company said it has spent the past 18 months expanding its AI-focused network footprint, with construction and overbuild projects now spanning more than 15,000 route miles.
Nvidia will have significant access to capacity on new routes, while Zayo will build, own and operate the network and make remaining capacity available to other customers.
That gives Zayo an anchor customer while opening the infrastructure to AI developers, cloud providers, neoclouds and enterprises.
AI training can span multiple facilities, while inference places computing capacity closer to users and enterprise applications. For large AI systems, this creates a data center interconnect requirement beyond individual campuses.
Related:
Arm Chips May Get Their Own Virtual RAN Boost
Yu said large AI factories could require dedicated, low-latency routes and thousands of fiber pairs to connect facilities and exchange points.
Westfall said the biggest gaps are emerging along secondary corridors where high-capacity long-haul fiber does not exist.
At the wide-area level, distributed AI clusters require high-capacity connections to move data between facilities. At the metro level, regional data centers may lack the dense fiber and low-latency optical connections needed to connect AI infrastructure to corporate networks and edge environments, Westfall said.
A new AI campus can bring hundreds of megawatts or more of computing capacity to a market that lacks the network infrastructure to connect it to other facilities.
Fiber operators have an incentive to identify AI corridors and build before demand arrives.
Optics Face Near-Term Constraint
Optical equipment is putting pressure on existing routes.
Yu said pump lasers used in amplifiers and coherent transponders are constrained in the near term. Ciena and Nokia have product lead times extending beyond 12 months, with growing backlogs, he said.
Related:
A Guide to Network Redundancy in Data Centers
Existing fiber routes can carry more traffic when operators add optical equipment. Equipment availability can limit how quickly that capacity becomes available.
New AI campuses create a separate requirement for physical routes that equipment upgrades cannot address.
“I think both are constrained,” Yu said of fiber and optical equipment. “It’s just a question of near term and long term.”
Westfall said AI workloads also produce traffic patterns that differ from traditional cloud networks.
Distributed GPU clusters can require significant bandwidth to coordinate workloads across regions, he said. Training runs can generate bursts of traffic as systems synchronize data between geographically separated clusters.
Those requirements can make dedicated, high-capacity routes important as developers distribute AI computing across multiple locations.
Building new routes takes time.
Yu said new fiber routes can take more than a year to build and approach two years – roughly the same order of magnitude as new data center construction.
That creates a potential timing problem for AI developers.
A data center can be complete, powered and equipped with GPUs while lacking the connectivity needed to operate as part of a larger distributed AI system.
“Providers need to begin building these new fiber plants now otherwise data centers will sit idle,” Yu said.
Zayo Builds Ahead of Demand
Zayo’s strategy is to build ahead of projected demand.
Smith said the company has modeled where AI-driven demand will emerge and is expanding infrastructure ahead of that demand.
For fiber providers, a new route can serve multiple customers and an entire emerging market.
Zayo’s expansion follows its acquisition of Crown Castle’s Fiber Solutions business, which added 90,000 metro route miles and 40,000 on-net enterprise locations, according to the company. Zayo has said the additional metro density will support AI inference workloads.
The company has also introduced an AI Infrastructure Blueprint focused on connecting training, inference and interconnection environments.
Zayo said the expanded network is intended to serve more than hyperscalers, including neocloud providers, frontier model developers and enterprises across health care, finance, manufacturing and other industries.
GPU clouds, model developers and enterprises are deploying computing capacity across a growing number of locations, including markets selected for access to power.
That geography creates a network planning requirement alongside the AI buildout.
For now, AI traffic has not overwhelmed wide-area networks, according to Yu. Optical equipment is putting pressure on efforts to add capacity to existing routes, while new AI facilities are creating demand for physical fiber in markets that lack it.

title: Australian BESS moves: BW ESS buys 1 GWh project, Edify reaches financial close on hybrid projects - Energy Storage
content: BW ESS has acquired the ready-to-build 250 MW / 1,000 MWh Yanco battery energy storage system (BESS) in the Riverina region of New South Wales from ACEnergy, with plans to have the facility operational by 2028. Construction will begin in late 2026 on the Yanco BESS facility, following its acquisition from Melbourne-headquartered clean energy developer ACEnergy by Swiss energy storage owner-operator BW ESS. Located in the Riverina, New South Wales (NSW) region, approximately southwest of Sydney by around 560 kilometers, the Yanco BESS also sits adjacent to the EnergyCo South West Renewable Energy Zone (REZ), tied via a connection to regional transmission network manager and operator Transgrid’s 132 kV Yanco substation. BW ESS Executive Director Andy Hadland said as a long-term owner and operator of energy-storage assets, the company’s priority is to progress the project responsibly. “Australia’s investment in a more flexible and reliable power system creates a compelling role for battery storage, and we are delighted to support that transition through Yanco BESS,” Hadland said. ACEnergy developed Yanco BESS from origination through to ready-to-build status, securing land, planning approval, grid connection and all key project rights and contracts. It appointed China-headquartered energy storage technology company CATL as system integrator for the project and Australian engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) company ACLE Services as Balance of Plant (BoP) contractor. ACEnergy Managing Director Raymond Wang said financial close on Yanco BESS is a significant milestone for ACEnergy and a strong endorsement of its platform. “We have taken the project from origination through to ready-to-build, working closely with the local community and stakeholders along the way,” Wang said. The addition of Yanco BESS adds to BW ESS’s Australian wholly or jointly-owned project portfolio totaling 1.3 GWh in the commissioning phase, 1 GWh entering construction, and a greenfield pipeline totaling around 2 GW across the NEM. Edify reaches financial close on hybrid projects in Queensland Meanwhile, Edify Energy has reached financial close on its integrated hybrid Ganymirra and Majors Creek solar and storage projects co-located in north Queensland, which in aggregate will supply 360 MWp of solar together with 1,200 MWh of lithium-ion BESS. Located near Townsville in the far north of the country, 14 domestic and international lenders have committed AUD$3.2 billion (USD 2.25 billion)  towards the projects that also include the 720 MWp / 2,400 MWh Smoky Creek and Guthrie’s Gap projects, which reached financial close in May 2026. Both projects are backed by Australia’s Capacity Investment Scheme (CIS) and will be operational in 2028. The projects are supported by DT Infrastructure as engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor, China-headquartered energy storage manufacturer CATL as battery supplier and state-owned transmission developer Powerlink Queensland as network and connection works head contractor. Edify Energy Chief Executive Officer Ben Warne said the Smoky Creek, Guthrie’s Gap, Ganymirra and Majors Creek project milestones represent the company’s consistent ability to deliver projects. “It demonstrates the strength of our business, our people and our ability to consistently progress projects from concept to construction and play our part in accelerating the energy transition and ensuring low cost and reliable energy security,” Warne said. “Projects succeed when communities share in the prosperity. Ganymirra and Majors Creek are backed by commitments to local procurement, employment, training and long-term community and First Nations funding, creating a legacy that will extend throughout the projects’ operating life and beyond.” With pv magazine Australia . title: Italian developer secures ready-to-build status for 1 GWh standalone BESS in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Limes Renewable Energy has achieved Ready-to-Build (RTB) status for its 200 MW / 1,000 MWh BESS Huañil project in the Coquimbo region of Chile. The milestone marks the Italian developer’s first RTB project in the country and its first outside of Italy, supporting its broader international expansion strategy. Located in the municipality of Salamanca, the Huañil Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) will store electricity from Chile’s National Electric System (SEN) and provide up to 1,000 MWh of storage capacity. The lithium-ion project is designed to deliver 200 MW of continuous power for up to five hours and represents an estimated investment of approximately $188 million. Since November 2025, Limes has secured environmental approvals for three projects in Chile: the 200 MW BESS Huañil, the Pradera Larga hybrid project (84 MWp solar PV and 90 MW BESS), and the 150 MW BESS Ganso. While BESS Huañil is the first to reach RTB status, the other two projects are actively progressing toward the same milestone. In total, Limes’ maturing Chilean pipeline currently includes approximately 180 MWp of solar PV and 620 MW of BESS capacity. Following the RTB milestone, Limes will focus on revenue structuring aligned with project finance requirements, while concurrently advancing strategic partnerships and power purchase agreement (PPA) negotiations. The company stated that the pipeline in Chile will support its plans to increase installed capacity and strengthen its position as a hybrid Independent Power Producer (IPP). Martin Libra, Head of LATAM at Limes, noted that the RTB milestone reflects the company’s focus on developing “high-quality, bankable, grid-ready projects” and positions it to advance strategic partnerships in Chile. Cristiano Spillati, Managing Director of Limes, stated that the achievement reinforces the company’s long-term commitment to Chile and its local-international development model. Across Chile and Italy, Limes’ fully authorized and RTB pipeline now exceeds 600 MW. In its home market of Italy, the company has more than 400 MWp across 25 projects, with an additional 120 MW across six solar projects progressing toward authorization before the end of the year. title: Italy's 2028 Capacity Market auction: Northern zones rewarded in shift for developers, notes Aurora - Energy Storage
content: Italy’s upcoming 2028 Capacity Market auction is set to introduce structural shifts that will impact energy storage deployment, according to recent analysis by Aurora Energy Research. The primary adjustment involves a new geographic focus designed to steer energy storage capacity to areas where the grid requires the most support, notably rewarding projects in Italy’s northern zones. Historically, capacity market mechanisms have often treated different regions with a broad brush. However, the 2028 framework will adjust the capacity rating coefficients for battery storage based directly on their specific location, marking a major departure from previous iterations and a deliberate step toward geographical optimization. This localized approach, decided on August 6th in a decree by the Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security (MASE), means developers must now re-evaluate project pipelines and expected returns across the country. “The most relevant change introduced by the Capacity Market 2028 is the geographic differentiation, for the first time, of battery rating coefficients, with the aim of providing more locational development signals,” said Maddalena Cerreto of Aurora Energy Research. Within the analysis, Aurora provides an example of a dramatic drop in remuneration in certain locations, while also showing that northern areas seem to be rewarded. “For a 4-hour battery in Sicily and Sardinia, the coefficient has gone from 67% in the previous auction to 31%. This latter value is also much lower than the 51% proposed in the consultation phase. Consequently, the final values ​​imply a battery remuneration 50% lower than in the previous auction for a 4-hour battery in Sicily and Sardinia, two of the regions most affected by renewable overgeneration in Italy and where BESS development is needed.” According to Aurora, from the regulator’s perspective, this choice is consistent with the fact that southern regions and Sicily and Sardinia already have a dedicated instrument for storage development via MACSE , while the Capacity Market focuses on system adequacy in areas where the risk of shortages is greatest and where there are fewer alternatives for remunerating new technologies, such as in Northern Italy. According to the consulting and intelligence firm, the picture is now more complex for developers. “For BESS plants located in the South and the Islands, opportunities outside of the MACSE currently appear more limited. Not only are the new rating coefficients significantly lower than those of previous auctions, but with the newly published data, it seems more likely that the 2028 auction will be the first to experience a true market split between geographic areas. Regions like Sicily could indeed post significantly lower prices than the North. The next auction will therefore represent a particularly important test to understand how the market will interpret the new balance between the Capacity Market and the MACSE and what the future geography of battery investments in Italy will be,” concluded Cerreto. title: Scatec completes 'Africa's largest' solar-plus-storage Obelisk project, adding 200 MWh of BESS - Energy Storage
content: Norway-based renewable energy developer Scatec has completed Africa’s largest solar-plus-storage project, according to the company, bringing the final 564 MW phase of its Obelisk development online near Nagaa Hammadi, Upper Egypt. The Obelisk project is a hybrid facility, combining 1.1 GW of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity, alongside a 100 MW / 200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). Scatec had not responded to a question on the system integrator for the BESS aspect of the project by the time of writing, and typically does not name its partners. BYD Energy said it was Scatec’s partner at its major Kenhardt project in South Africa, Scatec’s largest BESS at 225 MW / 1,140 MWh. The two‑phase build began with a power purchase agreement (PPA) signed in November 2024, with full commercial operations achieved less than two years later. Scatec said the Obelisk project will deliver over 3,000 GWh of clean electricity annually and will cut emissions by more than 1.2 million tonnes per year, with power generation being supplied to the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) under a 25-year PPA. “Reaching full commercial operations at Obelisk marks a defining milestone for Scatec. Completing Africa’s largest hybrid solar and battery installation demonstrates our ability to develop, finance, and deliver large-scale renewable energy projects in emerging markets. Obelisk will supply clean, reliable power to Egypt for 25 years and is a tangible contribution to the country’s energy security and transition,” Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog said. The project was financed by a consortium of development finance institutions , including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), African Development Bank (AfDB), British International Investment (BII) and European Investment Bank (EIB), which together provided $479 million in senior debt. In total, the Obelisk project costs around $590 million, meaning more than 80% is classified as non-recourse debt. With Obelisk now online, Scatec has approximately 1.5 GW of solar capacity operational in Egypt, as the new project joins its existing 380 MW BenBan solar plant portfolio. The company is also advancing a pipeline of more than 4.3 GW of renewable energy capacity, as well as 4.1 GWh of BESS in Egypt. Obelisk contributes to Egypt’s national target of sourcing 42% of its electricity from renewables by 2030, and 60% by 2040. title: Ford's EV pickup is almost here, promising much more than an affordable price tag
content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 13 2026 - 6:00 am PT
The Ford Fathom will go on sale in early 2027, starting at $28,350.
said the electric pickup is on track to go into production at its Louisville Assembly plant in Q1 2027.
Ford Fathom EV pickup enters production in Q1 2027
revealed the name and starting price
of the upcoming midsize electric pickup last week, the first vehicle based on its Universal EV (UEV) platform.
The first prototypes will roll off the assembly lines at Ford’s 3-million-square-foot Louisville Assembly Plant (LAP) in the first quarter of 2027.
announced plans
a year ago to transform it from a gas-powered vehicle plant into a facility for building fully electric vehicles, starting with the Fathom.
The $5 billion investment will create 4,000 new jobs at both the Louisville Assembly Plant and BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, and it will help fund the new equipment needed for the UEV platform. That’s where things get interesting.
The assembly process is a step change from Ford’s and most traditional automakers’ current manufacturing methods. Instead of a fully assembled vehicle rolling down the line, the UEV Production System breaks the vehicle into three sections: the front clip, rear clip, and battery deck.
Covered Ford Fathom UEV Production System at the Louisville Assembly Plant (Source: Ford)
Ford will use large unicastings to build the front and rear body sections. The single large aluminum casting piece replaces dozens of stamped and other welded components it currently uses.
The method cuts the number of parts from 146 to build the current Maverick to just two for the Fathom.
In the third line, the interior components (seats, consoles, and carpeting) are installed on top of the battery housing, which serves as the vehicle’s floor. The battery itself is then attached from the bottom.
Ford Fathom prototype (Source: Screenshot/ Ford)
Ford said the UEV Production System will enable it to assemble the Fathom 40% faster than current vehicles at the plant.
It’s also more ergonomic, Bryce Currie, Ford’s chief manufacturing officer, said, which will “require less twisting, turning, and bending.”
“We’ve engineered an 84% reduction in reaching over the fender,” Currie explained, adding, “The wiring harness is also more than 4,000 feet shorter and 22 pounds lighter than in our first-gen
electric SUV, making it much easier to install.”
(Source: Ford)
Ford is reinvesting some of the time it saves during assembly into insourcing and automation to improve quality and cost. LAP will have the highest level of automation in final assembly across all Ford plants globally.
For example, Ford installed a software module flash station, a first at one of its assembly plants, to ensure the vehicle has the latest software before the vehicle is fully built.
Before, if an issue were detected, updates would take about 10 minutes per vehicle. Now, it can be done as the vehicle rolls down the assembly line. With 5G in the facility, operators can diagnose and perform quality checks instantly.
Ford Universal EV Production System (Source: Ford)
With fewer parts and steps in the process, there’s less opportunity for issues to arise, Ford said, which will help improve quality.
The new UEV Production System and assembly tree will go online in the first quarter of 2027, starting with the Ford Fathom.
Ford said the Fathom will have more interior passenger space than a Toyota RAV4. It will also be equipped with a large, high-resolution touchscreen, bidirectional charging enabling vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, a digital key, and Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard.
The Ford Fathom will also be the first vehicle to have
Apple Maps integrated
directly into the navigation system, with turn-by-turn directions, EV routing, and more.

title: Rivian's 2027 R1S adds captain's chairs, its most-requested feature
content:
Rivian R1T
Rivian R1S
Fred Lambert
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:00 am PT
The 2027 Rivian R1S's new second-row captain's chairs.
Rivian is rolling out its 2027 model year R1S and R1T, and the headline change is one owners have been asking for since day one: second-row captain’s chairs on the R1S.
The automaker calls it the single most-requested feature since the R1S launched. It arrives alongside a simplified trim structure, a new standard wheel for the R1T, a new paint color, and higher starting prices across the board.
Captain’s chairs finally come to the R1S
Until now, the R1S only came with a second-row bench. For MY2027, Rivian is adding a six-seat layout built around a center pass-through, so passengers can walk back to the third row without folding a seat or disturbing a child seat mounted in the second row.
The new six-seat configuration is built around a center pass-through.
Each captain’s chair gets an individual armrest that stows flush into the seat and a push-to-release cup holder that folds down from the inside edge. Both seats are heated, fold flat, and keep the full car-seat tie-downs from the bench setup. Skis and other long gear can slide down the middle while all six seats stay occupied.
If you’d rather keep three seats in the middle, the seven-seat bench sticks around. It’s standard on R1S Premium and on the Black Mountain Signature interior for Performance and Quad.
The catch is the price. On Premium trim, the captain’s chairs require the Sound + Vision package, so the option runs $4,000 with the Black Mountain interior and $6,000 with Ocean Coast. On Performance and Quad, the chairs start at $1,500 with Black Mountain Signature, and two interiors, Ocean Coast Signature and Slate Sky Signature, are only available if you check the captain’s chairs box, at $4,000 and $4,500 respectively.

The Dual/Tri/Quad names are gone
Rivian is also killing the motor-count naming that defined the R1 lineup. Out go Dual, Tri, and Quad as battery-and-motor combos; in come three trim tiers: Premium, Performance, and Quad. It mirrors the structure Rivian
rolled out on the R2
, so the two families now read the same way.
Premium is the dual-motor tier, with 533 horsepower and 610 lb-ft of torque, and a 0-60 mph time of 4.5 seconds. An optional power upgrade pushes it to 665 hp and a 3.4-second sprint, and a Long Range pack is rated at up to 410 miles on the R1S and 420 miles on the R1T.
Performance is the tri-motor tier at 850 hp and 1,103 lb-ft, good for 2.9 seconds to 60 and up to 371 miles of range. Quad stays the
halo of the lineup
with 1,025 hp, 1,198 lb-ft, a 2.5-second 0-60 on the R1T, and up to 374 miles.
Interior names change too. Performance and Quad get three Signature interiors: Slate Sky Signature, Black Mountain Signature, and Ocean Coast Signature. Premium offers Black Mountain and Ocean Coast.
A new trail wheel and a new color
The R1T picks up a new standard 20-inch Adventure All-Season wheel and Goodyear tire, meant to add off-road traction without the usual range hit from a more aggressive tire. It’s standard on R1T Premium and a no-cost option on R1T Performance, and Rivian rates it at 300 miles on Premium, 380 miles on Premium Long Range, and 348 miles on Performance.
Both trucks also get Esker Silver, the liquid-metal finish Rivian first showed on the R2. It replaces LA Silver as the included paint on the R1S and R1T.
The new Esker Silver finish on the 2027 Rivian R1T.
Esker Silver replaces LA Silver as the included R1 paint.
Esker Silver first appeared on the Rivian R2.
The 2027 Rivian R1S in Esker Silver.

Prices are up
The MY2027 R1S now starts at $83,990 and the R1T at $79,990. That’s a jump from the
2026 model year
, where the R1S opened at $76,990 and the R1T at $70,990. The cheapest way into an R1 went up $7,000 on the SUV and $9,000 on the truck.
Electrek’s Take
The captain’s chairs are significant, and overdue, add-on that might bring some demand back to the R1S amid a focus on R2. A three-row family SUV without a walk-through middle row was always an odd gap in the R1S, especially at $80,000-plus, and Rivian is right to call it the most-requested feature. Building it around a center pass-through that doesn’t force you to disturb a car seat is exactly the kind of detail Rivian tends to get right.
The trim simplification is smart too. “How many motors do you want?” was never a great way to sell a car to a normal buyer, and lining the R1 up with the R2 gives the whole brand one language. I like it.
But the price is the part buyers will actually feel. A $7,000-to-$9,000 bump on the entry point, plus captain’s chairs that can cost $4,500 once you’re forced into the Sound + Vision package on Premium, adds up fast. Rivian is leaning harder into premium positioning right as the
more affordable R2
gets close to launch. That’s probably the plan: push R1 up-market and let R2 catch the volume. The question is how many R1S shoppers were waiting on captain’s chairs at the old price, not this one.

title: Rivian's long-delayed ALSO e-bike is only delayed a little bit longer
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 13 2026 - 4:28 am PT
The wait for Rivian’s first electric bike just got a little bit shorter. After months of delays, ALSO has informed reservation holders that they’ll finally be able to place pre-orders for the company’s highly anticipated TM-B electric bike starting August 18.
It’s welcome news for the unknown number of people who put down reservations, though it’s hard to ignore just how far the timeline has slipped.
When ALSO first unveiled the TM-B
last year
, the company targeted Spring 2026 deliveries. Spring has now come and gone, and with Summer well upon us now, reservation holders are only now getting the opportunity to actually order their bikes – or at least they’re being told that such an opportunity will be coming very soon.
No customer TM-B bikes have been reported as delivered yet, meaning the first shipments are still ahead of us.
The latest email from ALSO explains that the company’s Gear Shop pre-order opening was itself pushed back by another week, from August 11 to August 18, so the company could align Gear Shop purchases with bike ordering for “the best and most seamless experience.”
One point of frustration that’s been bubbling up in the reservation community is ALSO’s decision to open ordering for all reservation holders at once.
Rather than giving earlier reservation holders priority based on when they put down their deposits, everyone appears to be entering the ordering process simultaneously.
For customers who reserved last year, that’s understandably rubbed some people the wrong way, especially since ALSO’s reservation page still includes language indicating that reservation order impacts fulfillment, stating that “The sooner you reserve, the sooner you ride” and “Reservations will be fulfilled on a first-come basis.”
The TM-B itself remains one of the more technically ambitious e-bikes we’ve seen in years. The lightweight urban bike features Rivian-inspired industrial design, a carbon belt drive, integrated lighting, a removable battery, connected features, GPS tracking, automatic electronic shifting, pedal-by-wire, and a suite of sensors intended to improve security and the riding experience. It was designed to be more of a premium mobility platform than just another commuter e-bike.
The catch, of course, is
the price
. The bike is priced at US $4,500 for the Performance version or $3,500 for the lower-range version with a smaller battery.
The TM-B enters an increasingly competitive market
at a time when many buyers are gravitating toward value-oriented e-bikes that deliver much but not all of the performance of a TMB, yet for a fraction of the cost. That’s a difficult backdrop for any premium newcomer.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve said it before, and I still think it’s true: the TM-B is undeniably cool. Sure, the design is divisive in the classic love-it-or-hate-it way, but the engineer in me nerds out on how cool the technology and design turned out to be. Rivian’s innovative DNA is all over it, and there are some genuinely clever features here.
But I also wonder whether the company has misread where today’s e-bike market is. The industry is still recovering from a painful downturn, consumers have become far more price-conscious, and ALSO has clearly invested heavily in branding, social media marketing, and building out what appears to be a sizable, highly talented workforce that has to be weighing heavily on the company’s burn rate. That’s an expensive way to launch into a market that increasingly rewards value over novelty.
If the riding experience is as polished as ALSO promises, maybe the bike will justify its premium positioning. But after months of delays, the company now has even more to prove. And that has to start with delivering bikes.

title: Tesla defeats Sweden's IF Metall union after 1,021-day strike
content:
Fred Lambert
| Aug 13 2026 - 8:08 am PT
Sweden’s largest industrial union, IF Metall, is calling off its strike against Tesla after 1,021 days, the longest labor conflict in modern Swedish history. The union says it’s stopping because Tesla bought out every one of its striking members, leaving the walkout with nothing left to withhold.
The dispute started in October 2023 over a single demand: that Tesla sign a Swedish collective bargaining agreement for its mechanics. Nearly three years later, Tesla still hasn’t signed one. And now the union is standing down.
IF Metall announced today that it’s ending all conflict measures against Tesla effective 00:01 on August 19. In its statement, the union was blunt about why. Tesla “bought out” its members at the company, so the strike “no longer has any effect.”
The longest strike in modern Swedish history
The fight began on October 27, 2023, when Tesla’s roughly 120 mechanics across seven Swedish workshops walked off the job after Tesla refused to sign a kollektivavtal, the collective agreement that covers the vast majority of Swedish workplaces.
It snowballed fast as other unions started supporting Tesla workers. Dockworkers refused to unload Teslas at Swedish ports. Denmark, Norway, and Finland joined the port blockade. PostNord stopped delivering Tesla’s license plates. Electricians wouldn’t service Tesla’s chargers, and cleaners stopped cleaning its showrooms. We covered each escalation as it happened, from the
ports closing
to the fight reaching the Superchargers.
Tesla routed around all of it. It imported cars through Germany and trucked them up to Trelleborg, and it went to court to get plates directly rather than through the post. Elon Musk called the Swedish model “insane.” The company never budged.
How Tesla actually won
The union didn’t lose a vote or run out of money. Tesla simply paid its way out.
According to IF Metall, Tesla bought out all of its remaining striking members, one by one, until there was no one left on the picket line to represent. “Tesla has gigantic economic resources and has used them, among other things, to buy out the strikers. That is unique,” LO agreement secretary Veli-Pekka Säikkälä told Swedish outlet Ny Teknik.
IF Metall’s leadership framed it as a moral stand that ran into a wall of cash. “Our members at Tesla are union heroes who have fought for collective agreements against an employer with such a strong anti-union stance,” chair Marie Nilsson said, adding that three years of striking meant “enormous personal sacrifice.”
Contract secretary Simon Petersson went further, saying Tesla “is so opposed to collective agreements that they would rather buy out union members than offer secure conditions.” The union called it strikebreaking of a kind Sweden hasn’t seen in decades.
The sales never cracked — until Musk did
Here’s the part the union’s opponents will point to: the strike never actually hurt Tesla’s business in Sweden.
The Model Y was Sweden’s single best-selling car, of any kind, in both 2023 and 2024, straight through the blockade. Tesla registered 21,894 vehicles in Sweden in 2024, its best year in the country, with the strike in full swing. As
we reported in October 2024
, Tesla stayed dominant while the union fight dragged on with no visible effect on demand.
What finally broke Tesla’s Swedish sales wasn’t the union. It was Musk.
Registrations collapsed to 7,252 in 2025, down roughly 67% from 2024, as
Tesla’s sales cratered across Sweden
and the rest of Europe. That drop tracked the political backlash to Musk’s activities, not the labor dispute, which by then was old news. Sweden’s own registration data shows Tesla down 63% year-over-year through the first seven months of 2025.
2026 has been a partial recovery off that low base: 512 registrations in January, 553 in February, a 1,784-unit surge in March, then 429 in April and 858 in May. Better than 2025, still well below the pre-Musk-backlash peak.
So the union’s leverage argument was always shaky. It couldn’t dent Tesla’s sales at their height, and by the time sales did fall, a bigger force was doing the work.
Electrek’s Take
This is a clean loss for IF Metall.
The union picked a fight on principle, that Tesla should follow the Swedish model like everyone else, and Tesla answered with a checkbook. Buying out strikers one at a time until the bargaining unit is empty is ruthless, and it’s exactly the kind of thing the collective agreement system exists to prevent. If it holds up, it’s a template every foreign employer in Sweden just watched work.
But the sales data undercuts the union’s whole theory of the case. The strike was supposed to make Tesla feel enough pain to sign. It never did. The Model Y was Sweden’s top seller during the worst of the blockade, and the eventual collapse in 2025 came from Musk’s politics, not from dockworkers refusing to unload cars. Tesla proved a determined company can wait out even the most coordinated labor action in a country built around labor, as long as it’s willing to spend and absorb the bad press.
The bigger question now is whether this emboldens Tesla to take the same posture in Germany, where IG Metall has been circling Grünheide for years.

title: Urban Arrow enters the longtail cargo e-bike market in US with its new Breeze
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:02 am PT
Urban Arrow has spent the last 14 years building a reputation around front-loading cargo bikes, becoming one of the biggest names in the family cargo bike world. Now the Dutch company is branching out into an entirely new category with the launch of the Urban Arrow Breeze, bringing its first-ever longtail electric cargo bike to the North American market.
While Urban Arrow’s signature
front box bikes
have long been popular with parents hauling kids and groceries, longtail cargo bikes have become an increasingly important part of the North American market. They offer much of the utility of a cargo bike while riding and feeling more like a conventional bicycle, making them an easier transition for riders who may be intimidated by larger front-loaders.
That’s exactly the audience Urban Arrow is targeting with the Breeze.
According to Urban Arrow North America General Manager Mark Danhof, longtail cargo bikes now make up the majority of the North American cargo bike segment, making this a natural expansion for the company.
The Breeze is built around 24-inch wheels instead of the more common 20-inch rear wheel seen on many longtails. Urban Arrow says the larger wheels create handling that feels closer to a standard bicycle while also improving stability at higher speeds and when carrying passengers.
Power comes from Bosch’s Cargo Line motor, paired with an Enviolo continuously variable hub transmission and Gates carbon belt drive. That’s a premium drivetrain combination that should appeal to riders looking for low maintenance and smooth operation.
Despite its relatively compact appearance, the Breeze is designed to haul some serious weight. The rear rack is rated to carry up to 176 lb (80 kg), enough for two children or a combination of passengers and cargo, while total payload capacity reaches 440 lb (200 kg). A very low step-through frame should also make mounting and dismounting easier, particularly when the bike is fully loaded.
Urban Arrow has also added several family-focused touches, including spoke and belt guards, a sturdy dual-leg kickstand for easier loading, Bosch’s Purion 200 display, integrated security features, and the MIK HD accessory mounting system on both the front and rear racks for quickly swapping between passenger and cargo setups.
The company is sweetening the launch with more than $700 worth of included accessories, including a passenger protection bar, footrests, seat cushions, and a front rack.
The Urban Arrow Breeze is available now through select dealers in the US and Canada in a single green colorway.
Pricing starts at $6,999
, putting it squarely in the premium cargo bike category, though the included accessories help soften the blow compared to many competitors that charge extra for those essentials.
Electrek’s Take
Urban Arrow already knows how to build excellent family cargo bikes, so it isn’t surprising to see the company bringing that expertise into the longtail segment. If anything, it’s surprising it took this long.
The longtail cargo bike design also makes a lot of sense for North America, as this style has become the default recommendation for many families looking to replace car trips because they offer a gentler learning curve than front-loaders while still carrying one or two kids with ease.
We shouldn’t really be surprised at the price, since Urban Arrow has long been a premium brand, so you’re going to have to pay to play when it comes to a Dutch cargo e-bike brand. At nearly $7,000 it certainly isn’t inexpensive, but neither is the rest of the premium cargo bike market. For families planning to rack up thousands of miles replacing school drop-offs and grocery runs, that investment may be easier to justify than it first appears.
I’m a bit surprised they only brought one colorway to the US, and not the darker option that debuted
when they launched this model in their home market of Europe last year
, but I guess they have their reasons.

title: Volkswagen's new electric camper van turns the ID. Buzz into a home on wheels
content:
Volkswagen
VW ID BUZZ
ID. Buzz
Peter Johnson
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:33 am PT
Volkswagen
is giving people what they want — an all-electric, fully fledged camper van that can be assembled in minutes. The ID. California Cruise is coming as the first all-electric California camper.
Volkswagen reveals first electric California camper van
Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Stuff Bubble, which developed the world’s first inflatable camping kitchen, have teamed up to develop a new family of electric camper vans.
“This partnership gives us the opportunity to rethink the campervan,” Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles CEO, Stefan Mecha, said.
At Caravan Salon 2026 later this month, Volkswagen will unveil two new camper van concepts: the ID. California Cruise, the first fully electric member of the California family, and the California Beach, which the company says will unlock “maximum freedom.”
Volkswagen and Stuff Bubble are developing new inflatable camping equipment, or modules, that are lighter and easier to install.
According to VW, the special parts turn an everyday van into a “fully-fledged camper in just a few minutes,” without adding unnecessary weight or permanent fixtures.
The solution is perfect for those who “still want to enjoy the comforts of camping on spontaneous getaways, festival weekends, or outdoor adventures,” the company said. Unlike traditional camper van conversions, the parts can be installed by one person and removed just as quickly.
The inflatable kitchen was specifically designed to fit in the luggage shelf of the California Beach, with “full kitchen functionality,” despite weighing less than 23 lbs (10 kg). It even includes a closed water system.
The new inflatable bed is just as flexible, weighing just 12 lbs (6 kg) as a single or 26 lbs (12 kg) as a double.
Even with the bed installed, there’s plenty of room in the camper to cook, move around, or store things. The concept shown has enough room for four people to sleep.
At Caravan Salon, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles will reveal the ID. California Cruise for the first time. While the company didn’t share any other details, it did say the electric camper van will be based on the ID. Buzz.
Like the ID. Buzz, the ID. California Cruise will likely be available with 79- or 86-kWh battery pack options, which provide WLTP ranges of around 250-300 miles, depending on the trim.
The ID. California Cruise “marks an important milestone towards an entirely new generation of all-electric campervans,” Volkswagen said, set to arrive through 2028.
Volkswagen will reveal full details during Caravan Salon, which runs from August 28 to September 6. Check back for more.
Will Volkswagen bring the electric van to the US? It has yet to be confirmed, but Volkswagen doesn’t sell the current
California camper van
in the US.
The ID. Buzz is back on sale. After a brief hiatus, Volkswagen launched
the 2027 ID. Buzz
with a new Tourer model (pictured above) that essentially turns it into a camper van with a fold-out mattress and Overnight Mode. So, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the ID. California Cruise go on sale in some form in the US as well.

Canadian natural hydrogen exploration firm Primary Hydrogen plans to start drilling at a prospect well in British Columbia later this year.
Pending geochemistry and radiometric tests at its Wicheeda North project, the firm aims to complete 1,500 metres of drilling across 70 permitted sites over the next five years.
Primary claims the 2,138-hectare Wicheeda North rare earth element project contains nine minerals and holds significant potential for natural hydrogen. It acquired its 75% stake
in the project
The company’s 2026 plans will progressively refine drill targets ahead of the maiden drill. Soil sampling will build on data gathered in 2025 fieldwork and an airborne radiometric survey will narrow areas prospective for rare earth mineralisation.
Results will then be combined with existing geological and geophysical data to select final drilling targets.
The move comes as natural hydrogen gains traction with firms seeking and identifying prospect resources worldwide.
While the potential route to low-carbon hydrogen is experiencing a boom in attention and investment, it remains early-stage, with few real-world extractions having been undertaken.
Worldwide, there are estimated to be over 40 companies exploring for natural hydrogen reserves. However, alongside its nascency,
experts suggest
that more research is required for its safe and successful extraction.

title: VLC 播放 MP3 卡顿 33 秒？微软 Microsoft Defender 背锅
content:
IT之家 8 月 13 日消息，游戏《时空幻境》（Braid）与《见证者》（The Witness）的开发者乔纳森 · 布洛（Jonathan Blow）昨日在 X 上发文称，他已放弃使用 VLC 播放器，因为该软件在 Win11 上打开一个简单的 MP3 文件需要约 33 秒，并评论称“很大一部分开源软件如今已处于令人尴尬的境地”。
这一吐槽迅速引发了广泛讨论。VLC 播放器官方账号今日回应澄清，表示该延迟并非 VLC 本身的问题，而是 Windows 11 的一次更新导致 Microsoft Defender 错误地将 VLC 的插件缓存隔离所致。
VLC 依赖该缓存来存储已安装模块和插件的信息，以避免每次启动时都重新枚举，一旦缓存丢失或无法使用，播放器在启动时就需要花费大量时间重新扫描，从而导致严重的启动延迟。
VideoLAN 团队建议用户通过重新安装 VLC 或重新生成插件缓存来解决此问题。具体操作方法包括：在命令行中执行 vlc --reset-plugins-cache，或使用 Windows 开始菜单“VideoLAN”文件夹中的“VLC media player - reset preferences and cache files”快捷方式。
IT之家注：后者在重置插件缓存的同时也会清除用户的个性化设置（如自定义快捷键、字幕偏好等），若仅需修复缓存问题，建议优先使用命令行方式。另有用户指出，在 Microsoft Defender 中将 vlc.exe 添加至排除列表可从根本上避免缓存再次被隔离。

title: 全球最大电池纯电动飞机 Heart Aerospace X1 完成首飞：超 1 兆瓦功率输出 + 超 11 吨起飞重量
content:
8 月 13 日消息，当地时间 8 月 12 日，瑞典航空航天公司 Heart Aerospace 宣布其 X1 演示机在美国纽约州普拉茨堡国际机场完成首次载人飞行。
这架飞机翼展达 106 英尺
（IT之家注：约 3,231 厘米）
，机长 76 英尺
（约 2,316 厘米）
，起飞重量超过 25,000 磅
（约 11,340 千克）
，这也是迄今为止完成飞行的最大电池的电动飞机。
此次试飞在美国联邦航空管理局颁发的实验类特殊适航证书（SAC-EC）框架下进行。飞行持续约 27 分钟，最高爬升至离地高度 1,100 英尺
（约 335.3 米）
测试内容涵盖滑行、起飞、爬升、机动以及着陆等科目。飞行过程中，飞机全电池电力推进系统输出功率超过 1 兆瓦。据公司披露，整次任务消耗的电费约为 5 美元
（现汇率约合 33.8 元人民币）
Heart Aerospace 创始人兼首席执行官 Anders Forslund 表示，X1 的首次飞行展示了在商业客机规模上的电动飞行能力。X1 是该公司为后续 30 座混合动力区域客机 ES-30 项目开发的全尺寸验证平台，主要用于验证飞行特性、关键技术及获取相关运行数据。

title: 小米汽车：小米龙甲电池最大特点在于远超国标的安全标准
content:
感谢IT之家网友
Autumn_Dream
8 月 13 日消息，小米汽车官方今日发布答网友问（第 276 集），针对小米龙甲电池是什么、电池包涉水能行吗等问题进行了集中解答。
IT之家附小米本集答网友问重点内容如下：
小米龙甲电池是什么？有什么特点？
「小米龙甲电池」是小米汽车主导的动力电池系统化解决方案
。小米负责产品定义，小米主导电池包的设计开发，小米参与电芯的设计开发，小米负责全流程质量管控。
在于远超国标的安全标准
结构安全标准远超国标：以底部撞击场景为例，
「小米龙甲电池」要求电池底部可以耐受直径为 25mm 的撞击头以 500J 能量进行撞击
，冲击头直径更小、压强更大、能量等级更高，远超新国标的 30mm 撞击头和 150J 的能量标准，且在底部撞击后，「小米龙甲电池」不仅要求不泄漏、不起火、不爆炸，相比国标还额外要求电池功能不失效，严苛程度远超国标。
热安全标准远超国标：
「小米龙甲电池」要求在 55℃ 高温、满电的极端条件下，触发单电芯热失控后电池包依然无热蔓延、不起火、不爆炸
，严苛程度远超国标的 22±5℃ 常温以及电量≥95% 要求。
电气安全标准远超国标：「小米龙甲电池」在设计开发标准上，电气安全距离冗余远超国标，而且还配有「毫秒级机械闸刀」在电池短路、车辆碰撞等紧急情况下，可以在数毫秒内完成物理层面的高压切断，守护电池安全。
大数据安全标准远超国标：
「小米龙甲电池」支持 24 小时车云协同安全预警以及全天候云端 AI 主动巡检
，其信息采集频率达到国标 10 倍，数据量达到国标 3 倍，可以实现 7×24 小时的全天候安全守护能力。
电芯循环寿命远超国标：「小米龙甲电池」对电芯的循环寿命也提出了更高的标准。通过严选正负极、电解液、隔膜，并优化电芯核心设计及工艺，
「小米龙甲电池」的电芯循环寿命远超国标的 1000 次循环后容量保持率≥80% 要求
另外，「小米龙甲电池」也有着严苛的质量管控标准：
穿透式管理体系：“影子工厂”的穿透式管理体系，每个模块均有小米质量专家深度管控。
先进的质检技术：从原料到电池包，全流程穿透式质检每个生产流程都有先进的质检技术。
质检数据可追溯：制程数据全量存档 15 年，每颗电芯的质检数据均可追溯。
电池包涉水能行吗？暴雨天开会不会有风险？
小米澎程全系均配备应急涉水模式，具备一定的应急涉水能力。其中，N90 Max 的最高涉水深度为 750mm，N70 Max 最高涉水深度为 650mm，可以有效应对越来越多的城市内涝场景，给到用户更自在、更安全的用车体验。
针对应急涉水工况，小米澎程的动力电池满足 IPX8 及 IPX9K 防水标准，可以满足 1 米水深 24 小时浸泡的静态防水需求以及 80±5℃ 高温高压水流冲洗的动态防水需求，
可以为浅层积水行驶、高速涉水行驶、高压水枪清洗等常规涉水场景提供可靠防护
，您无需担心动力电池在常规涉水情况下的安全性能。
应急涉水过程中，车辆应低速缓慢行驶，并严格控制涉水时间与距离，切勿长时间、长距离涉水
。应急涉水行驶后，应立即联系小米汽车服务中心进行全面检查或维修，否则可能造成车辆损坏及安全风险。

title: 微软整合个人、企业版两套 Copilot AI 助手，为“超级应用”铺路
content:
IT之家 8 月 13 日消息，据外媒 The Verge 今天（13 日）晚间报道，微软终于开始整合面向个人和企业用户的两套 Copilot AI 助手，目标是打造一个统一的“超级应用”。
为超级应用“铺路”的第一步，就是从 Copilot 和 Microsoft 365 Copilot 两款应用开始，个人账户和工作账户都会迁移到新版统一应用。
新应用继续沿用“Microsoft Copilot”名称，并启用新的图标。完成整合后，系统托盘或任务栏里也不会再同时出现两个 Copilot 图标。
微软通过更新公告宣布，新版应用首先带来焕新的界面，将 Copilot 聊天和图像生成功能与 Microsoft 365 的办公能力结合起来。
此次更新主要是为微软计划在今年晚些时候推出的“超级应用”打下技术基础，也预示着 Copilot 产品接下来的调整方向。
微软称，移动端和网页版将在 8 月中旬开始面向全球推送，Windows 和 Mac 版本则从 9 月中旬开始更新。移动端用户会收到下载新版 Copilot 应用的提示，本周起部分 Windows 预览体验成员也会率先收到更新。
据IT之家了解，现有 Microsoft Copilot 用户会直接迁移到新版，聊天记录和内容也会得到保留。已在同时使用两款应用的用户，聊天记录和内容会整合到新版 Copilot 应用中。
微软强调，应用内部的个人账户与工作或学校账户仍然彼此独立，双方的聊天记录、内容和数据不会混在一起。
企业安全、合规和政府管控功能保持不变。用户仍然可以在个人 Microsoft 账户与工作或学校使用的 Microsoft Entra ID 账户之间切换，两类账户依旧完全分开。Copilot 的核心功能继续免费提供，部分用户在新版应用中可能会遇到不同的免费使用额度。
也有一些功能不会进入统一版的 Copilot。播客和深度研究功能将在 8 月 18 日之后停止提供，群聊中的会话、消息和内容也不会迁移到新版应用。
微软目前只列出了上述受影响的服务，并称购物、Copilot Health 等其他功能在新版 Copilot 推送期间则可能暂时无法使用。

title: 我国核电总装机规模居世界第一，在运和核准在建总装机达 1.35 亿千瓦
content:
IT之家 8 月 13 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，今年，我国加大核电项目建设力度，57 台机组核准在建，在运和核准在建总装机达 1.35 亿千瓦，核电工程建设规模稳居世界第一。
报道提到，我国核电以在全国电力装机中不到 2% 的占比，贡献了近 5% 的发电量。广东、福建、辽宁、海南等 4 个省份的核电发电量占比均超过 15%。核电已成为东部沿海地区重要的清洁能源供给来源。7 月底，我国又新核准 8 台核电机组，这也是“十五五”时期首批核准的核电项目。
据IT之家此前报道，国家能源局在 8 月 6 日发布《中国核电发展报告（2026）》。截至 2025 年底，我国在运和核准在建核电机组共 112 台，装机规模 1.25 亿千瓦，总规模居世界首位，在建规模持续保持全球第一，是 2012 年的 2.6 倍。
值得一提的是，我国核电安全运行业绩稳居世界前列。所有核电机组保持良好安全纪录，未发生国际核与辐射事件分级 2 级及以上运行事件 / 事故，未对公众和环境造成任何不良影响。世界核电运营者协会 (WANO) 核电机组运行综合指数连续 10 年保持全球第一，满分比例和综合指数平均值位居世界前列。

title: 澳大利亚青少年社媒禁令上路半年间，Meta 清理 75.6 万个疑似未成年账户
content:
8 月 13 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 13 日（今天）Meta 披露，自澳大利亚实施全球首个 16 岁以下青少年社交媒体账户禁令以来，公司已经清理
超过 75 万个
疑似属于 16 岁以下澳大利亚用户的账户。面对监管机构可能采取进一步措施，Meta 还承诺继续加强执法。
Meta 称，从禁令去年 12 月正式生效前夕到今年 6 月，公司累计停用
46.2 万个疑似未成年人的 Instagram 账户和 29.4 万个 Facebook 账户
，总数为 75.6 万个。
澳大利亚政府担忧社交媒体对儿童和低龄青少年身心健康造成影响，因此推动制定了这项具有里程碑意义的法律。据IT之家了解，禁令于 2025 年 12 月 10 日正式生效。
其他平台尚未公布覆盖相同时间范围的合规数据。澳大利亚政府数据和多项独立研究显示，禁令实施后的前三个月，仍有
超八成 16 岁以下青少年
继续使用社交媒体。
随后，澳大利亚政府指责社交媒体平台

title: 神秘生图模型“mona-lisa-1”曝光：含 OpenAI 来源信号，GPT-Image-2 发布三个月仍稳坐第一
content:
感谢IT之家网友
汪汪的主人是喵喵
8 月 13 日消息，8 月 9 日有一款代号为“mona-lisa-1”的图像生成模型出现在 AI 竞技场的盲测列表中。
爆料者 AiBattle 称，他将该模型生成的图片提交至 OpenAI 官方内容验证工具后，检测到了与 OpenAI 相关的来源信号。因此，这款“mona-lisa-1”被认定为新一代的 GPT-Image 模型。
OpenAI 方面截至目前尚未就该模型发布任何正式公告、产品文档或公开说明，也未确认其与现有产品的具体关系。
@TimJayas 使用相同提示词，将这款神秘模型其与 GPT-Image 2 进行了对比。测试结果显示，“mona-lisa-1”在部分细节表现上更为丰富。
据多位测试者反馈，该模型目前仅出现在 LM Arena 的盲测环节，尚未接入 ChatGPT、OpenAI API 或 Codex 等正式产品通道。部分对比测试显示，“mona-lisa-1”在真实感、细节层次以及减少传统 AI 生成图像常见的人工质感方面有一定表现差异，但也有测试指出部分生成结果仍存在噪声或伪影现象。
IT之家注意到，GPT-Image 2 正式发布前也曾以匿名代号形式出现在 Arena 平台进行盲测。目前“mona-lisa-1”的具体技术架构、训练完成时间及后续正式发布计划，均有待 OpenAI 进一步公开。
OpenAI 官方 Verify 页面明确说明，该工具可检查图片或音频文件中是否存在与 OpenAI 工具相关的内容来源信号，包括 C2PA 元数据以及 SynthID 水印，主要面向由 ChatGPT、OpenAI API 或 Codex 生成的内容。
OpenAI 同时指出，若检测到受支持的来源信号，可表明相关内容由 OpenAI 工具生成或导出，但验证结果本身并不能用于确认具体使用了哪一款模型。因此，目前尚不能仅凭 SynthID 等来源信号确认“mona-lisa-1”即为 GPT-Image 2 的直接继任型号。

title: 维珍银河新一代 Delta 级飞船首飞推迟至 2027 年，75 万美元太空票获超额认购
content:
8 月 13 日消息，维珍银河（Virgin Galactic）在 8 月 12 日举行的 2026 年第二季度财报电话会议上宣布，其新一代“Delta 级”亚轨道太空飞机的首次商业飞行将推迟至 2027 年 2 月。此前的计划是在 2026 年第四季度开始商业运营。
维珍银河 CEO 迈克尔 · 科尔格拉齐尔（Michael Colglazier）表示，此次推迟并非由单一重大问题导致，而是在新飞船的组装过程中遇到了“数百个相对较小但重要的安装任务”的工期延长。
他举例称，许多组件的尺寸存在“千分之几英寸”的偏差。科尔格拉齐尔指出，这类“未预期到的安装不匹配”数量超出了预留的缓冲时间，尤其是在 7 月底之后此类问题开始加速累积。他强调，团队需要更多时间来以正确的方式完成工作。
根据调整后的计划，维珍银河预计将于本月晚些时候开始集成飞行器地面测试，并于 10 月将该飞行器运至美国新墨西哥州的美国太空港（Spaceport America）开始一系列飞行测试。公司已增派人员以加快组装进度，实行两班倒、每周工作七天的工作制。
尽管首飞推迟，维珍银河首席财务官道格 · 阿伦斯（Doug Ahrens）表示，公司财务状况稳健，预计不会因此出现重大变化。截至第二季度末，公司持有现金及等价物 2.86 亿美元。
维珍银河第二季度通过按市价增发股票筹集了 1.34 亿美元，并偿还了 9300 万美元的债务。阿伦斯表示，目前资金足以支撑公司进入商业服务阶段。
维珍银河还宣布，已完成今年 3 月启动的以每张 75 万美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 506.8 万元人民币）
价格销售的一批太空旅行机票。原计划销售 50 张，因需求旺盛超额认购，总预订金额超过 5,000 万美元
（现汇率约合 3.38 亿元人民币）
科尔格拉齐尔表示，新一批客户包括多代际探险、研究任务、企业包机和非营利机构预订等更多团体客户。公司计划在今年晚些时候以更高的价格开启新一轮售票。
其第二艘飞船已投入生产，预计于 2027 年 3 月加入机队。维珍银河预计，到 2027 年第二季度末可实现每月至少 10 次飞行的频率，并在该季度实现季度现金流转正。

title: 英伟达 GeForce NOW 原生 Linux 应用发布：结束 Beta 测试，支持 Ubuntu 24.04 及 Flatpak 安装
content:
IT之家 8 月 13 日消息，英伟达于当地时间 8 月 13 日宣布，其云游戏服务 GeForce NOW 的原生 Linux 应用已正式结束测试阶段，面向所有用户发布。
该应用于 2026 年 1 月以 Beta 版形式首次登陆 Linux 平台，经过数月的社区反馈与优化，现已推出正式版本。
Linux 版 GeForce NOW 客户端将继续支持 Ubuntu 24.04 及更新版本。英伟达同时新增了官方 Flatpak 软件仓库，以简化安装和后续更新流程。用户可通过英伟达的.bin 安装程序或添加 Flatpak 仓库直接安装 com.nvidia.geforcenow 包。
性能方面，英伟达对云端 DLSS 帧生成技术进行了优化，以降低延迟，使游戏操作反馈更加灵敏。这一改进在 1440p 和 4K 分辨率下以 60 或 120 FPS 进行串流时效果尤为明显。
针对 GeForce NOW Performance 会员，英伟达还部署了额外的服务器端软件优化，旨在提升部分对 CPU 性能要求较高的游戏的帧率。这些云端升级均为自动生效，用户无需进行任何安装或配置操作，且不产生额外费用。
此外，本周的“GFN Thursday”为游戏库新增了九款作品，包括《Car Wash Simulator》、《Pax Autocratica》、《Clawed》、《Hell Let Loose: Vietnam》、《Sandustry》、《Cat Mail Co.》、《Misery》、《Monster Hunter Wilds Prologue Demo》和《Pratfall》。IT之家注：GeForce NOW 目前支持超过 2000 款 PC 游戏，用户可串流来自 Steam、Epic Games、Xbox、Ubisoft 等平台的已购游戏。

title: 英特尔锐炫 A 系列 Linux 显卡驱动获 Vulkan Video AV1 编码支持，补齐硬件编码短板
content:
感谢IT之家网友
8 月 13 日消息，开源咨询公司 Igalia 的工程师 Hyun-jun Ko 昨日在 Mesa 26.3 开发版中合并了一项重要更新，正式为英特尔锐炫 A 系列 DG2/Alchemist 显卡启用了 Vulkan Video AV1 视频编码功能。
这意味着锐炫 A 系列显卡在 Linux 平台 Vulkan 生态中的编解码能力终于形成了完整闭环，此前长期缺失的 AV1 硬件编码短板已被补齐。
IT之家注：AV1 是由 AOM（开放媒体联盟）开发的开源视频编码格式，在同等画质下比 H.264 节省约 30% 的带宽，已被 Netflix、YouTube 等主流平台广泛采用。
英特尔 DG2 显卡此前虽已通过 VA-API 支持 AV1 硬件编码，但 VA-API 主要面向 Linux 传统视频加速场景，与 FFmpeg、GStreamer 等主流多媒体框架的集成程度有限。而在 Vulkan Video 这一跨平台 API 上，AV1 编码功能长期缺失。
今年年初，因测试不足，英特尔一度在 ANV 开源驱动中禁用了新款硬件的 Vulkan Video 编码功能。Mesa 26.2 已于 7 月重新启用了 H.264 与 H.265 的 Vulkan Video 编码支持。此次 AV1 编码的落地是此前工作的延续，该功能在英特尔 Gen125 硬件上通过 KHR_video_encode_av1 扩展得以暴露，Hyun-jun Ko 在 DG2 Arc A 系列显卡上完成了测试。
此次更新后，FFmpeg、HandBrake 等主流视频工具可直接调用 Vulkan Video API 进行硬件加速的 AV1 编码，大幅提升视频转码效率。
该功能目前已合并至 Mesa 26.3 开发版，预计将在 Mesa 26.3 正式版发布后向所有用户推送。根据合并请求中的说明，10-bit 编码、多 tiling 支持以及环路滤波器 / 恢复滤波器和 CDEF（约束方向增强滤波）支持仍待后续完成。

title: 超薄机身的代价：iFixit 为三星 Galaxy Z Fold8 可维修性打出 4/10 分
content:
IT之家 8 月 13 日消息，iFixit 今天（13 日）晚间公布了三星 Galaxy Z Fold8 的可维修性评测报告，结果显示，超薄机身依然是以牺牲可维修性为代价实现的。
iFixit 给 Galaxy Z Fold8 打出了 4/10 的可维修性评分。过于脆弱的内屏、复杂的铰链结构，以及实际防护能力有限的防尘等级，都是主要扣分项。
Galaxy Z Fold8 也有一些便于维修的设计。iFixit 指出，手机采用标准十字 / JIS 螺丝，USB-C 接口为独立模块，没有直接焊接在主板上。三星还为 Galaxy Z Fold8 换用新的硅碳电池，与 Fold7 相比容量增加 8.8%，电池本身也采用方便拆卸的拉片设计。
然而，机身内部共有两块电池，其中一块必须先拆下脆弱的外屏才能取出。为了更换本就属于耗材的电池，维修人员需要先让昂贵的外屏承担损坏风险。
内屏和铰链的维修难度更高。iFixit 拆解时，内屏周围的塑料边框出现崩裂并逐渐碎开，最终连带损坏了脆弱的折叠 OLED 屏幕。
Galaxy Z Fold8 的 IP4X 防尘等级也挡不住口袋绒毛和细小碎屑。iFixit 在显微镜下用灰尘和沙粒进行测试后，铰链很快发出像是在嚼碎石的声音。
三星通常会把内屏和铰链组合成一整套更换组件，因此无论维修哪一部分，都很可能需要把整部手机几乎完全拆空，普通用户自行维修基本没有可行性。
IT之家获悉，iFixit 还指出，去年 Fold7 的官方替换零部件至今仍不好买，Fold8 的零部件供应情况也难言乐观。如果准备把 Galaxy Z Fold8 用上好几年，对后续维修便利性最好不要抱太高期待。

Nachhaltig, barrierefrei, innovativ: Das Haus für Innovation und Transfer erhält das Prädikat „KlimaKulturKompetenz“. Für die Beteiligten ist das mehr als nur eine Plakette an der Fassade.
„KlimaKulturKompetenz“: So heißt das Qualitätssiegel, mit dem die Bayerische Architektenkammer herausragende Bauprojekte würdigt. Nun gehört auch das Haus für Innovation und Transfer (HIT) der OTH Regensburg dazu. Hochschulpräsident Prof. Dr. Ralph Schneider nahm die Plakette stellvertretend für alle Beteiligten entgegen. Vor allem mit seiner hohen Energieeffizienz und der konsequent umgesetzten Barrierefreiheit überzeugte das HIT.
„Das HIT steht beispielhaft für das, was wir als Hochschule erreichen wollen: Innovation ermöglichen, Menschen zusammenbringen und dabei Verantwortung für Umwelt und Gesellschaft übernehmen. Diese Ehrung und mein herzlicher Dank gilt allen, die das Projekt geplant, begleitet und umgesetzt haben“, sagte Prof. Dr. Ralph Schneider.
Modulare Bauweise und architektonische Qualität ergänzen sich hervorragend
Das Gebäude wurde vom Büro meuer – planen beraten Architekten GmbH geplant. Für Architekt David M. Meuer ist das HIT ein Projekt mit Signalwirkung: „Mit diesem Gebäude konnten wir zeigen, was möglich ist. Die gewählte Bau- und Konstruktionsart, ein sogenannter Modulbau, ist in Architekturkreisen durchaus umstritten. Das HIT beweist heute, dass sich modulare Bauweise und architektonische Qualität nicht ausschließen, sondern hervorragend ergänzen. Solche Projekte gelingen jedoch nur mit Bauherren, die bereit sind, neue Wege mitzugehen.“
Maßgeblich an der Umsetzung beteiligt war das Staatliche Bauamt Regensburg. Gerhard Haslbeck, Bereichsleiter Hochschulbau, betonte den Modellcharakter des Gebäudes: „Die besondere Herausforderung bestand darin, in kurzer Zeit ein qualitativ hochwertiges, wirtschaftliches und nachhaltiges Gebäude zu realisieren. Dass dies gelungen ist, verdanken wir dem engagierten Zusammenspiel aller Beteiligten. Mein ausdrücklicher Dank gilt unseren Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeitern sowie allen Projektpartnerinnen und Projektpartnern.“
Neue Akzente auf dem Campus gesetzt
Die Qualitäten des Gebäudes zeigen sich nicht nur in technischen Kennzahlen. Die konsequente Barrierefreiheit erleichtert Studierenden, Beschäftigten und Gästen die Nutzung im Alltag und stärkt das Ziel einer inklusiven Hochschule. Gleichzeitig setzt das HIT beim klimaschonenden Bauen neue Akzente auf dem Campus. Das betonten bei der Preisverleihung auch Kanzler Utto Spielbauer und Prof. Dr. Christoph Skornia, Vizepräsident für Nachhaltigkeit und Digitalisierung.
Seine Vorbildfunktion konnte das Gebäude bereits unter Beweis stellen: Im Rahmen der Architektouren öffnete das HIT seine Türen für die breite Öffentlichkeit und bot Einblicke in zeitgemäße Hochschularchitektur.
Direkt neben dem HIT entsteht derzeit mit dem Johannes Kepler Building of International Services bereits das nächste markante Gebäude auf dem Campus. Obwohl beide Bauten unterschiedlichen Konzepten folgen, wirken sie gestalterisch nach außen wie eine Einheit und prägen gemeinsam das neue Gesicht dieses Campusbereichs.
Das Prädikat „KlimaKulturKompetenz“
Mit dem Prädikat „KlimaKulturKompetenz" zeichnet die Bayerische Architektenkammer Projekte aus, die beim nachhaltigen Planen und Bauen besondere Maßstäbe setzen. Bewertet werden unter anderem Energieeffizienz, Klimaanpassung, Flächensparen, Barrierefreiheit sowie weitere Aspekte der Nachhaltigkeit. Das HIT überzeugte insbesondere in den Kategorien Energieeffizienz und Barrierefreiheit.
